problem.passage:
For eleven years, Kipchoge and Juma had worked rival matatus on the Ngong Road route, each conductor quietly trying to outdo the other in courtesy, in the crisp folding of change, in remembering regular passengers' names. When an elderly passenger slumped against the window of Kipchoge's crowded vehicle one humid afternoon, Kipchoge glanced toward Juma, who had just boarded at the stage, and braced himself for a smirk at his rival's misfortune. ______ Juma pushed through the aisle without a word, loosened the old man's collar, and called out calmly for someone to pass him a bottle of water.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: For eleven years, Kipchoge and Juma had worked rival matatus on the Ngong Road route, each conductor quietly trying to outdo the other in courtesy, in the crisp folding of change, in remembering regular passengers' names. When an elderly passenger slumped against the window of Kipchoge's crowded vehicle one humid afternoon, Kipchoge glanced toward Juma, who had just boarded at the stage, and braced himself for a smirk at his rival's misfortune. ______ Juma pushed through the aisle without a word, loosened the old man's collar, and called out calmly for someone to pass him a bottle of water.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Instead,
Specifically,
As a result,
Nevertheless,
problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 키프초게가 주마의 비웃음을 예상했다는 내용이고, 뒤 문장은 주마가 오히려 조용히 노인을 도왔다는 내용이다. 따라서 예상된 행동 대신 다른 행동이 일어났음을 나타내는 A가 정답이다. B는 앞의 내용을 구체화하는 연결어인데, 노인을 돕는 행동은 비웃음의 구체적 예가 아니다. C는 인과를 나타내지만, 키프초게가 마음의 준비를 했다고 해서 주마가 도운 것은 아니다. D는 양보 뒤의 반전을 나타내지만, 앞 문장은 인정된 사실이 아니라 빗나간 예상이므로 대체를 뜻하는 A가 더 정확하다.
problem.explanationEn: The previous sentence tells you that Kipchoge expected Juma to smirk. The next sentence shows Juma quietly helping the old man. So Juma did something in place of what Kipchoge expected, and A expresses exactly that. B would introduce a specific detail of what came before, but helping the man isn't an example of smirking. C signals cause and effect, yet Kipchoge bracing himself didn't cause Juma to help. D signals a contrast that comes after a concession, but the first sentence is an expectation that turns out wrong, not a fact being conceded, so A's sense of replacement fits better.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On a crowded Nairobi matatu, aging rival conductors Kipchoge and Juma silently compete for passengers' respect until a medical crisis forces them to recognize each other's quiet dignity.

hardJudge.note: 앞 문장(비웃음 예상) 뒤에 예상과 다른 실제 행동이 오므로 '대체'를 뜻하는 Instead가 가장 정확함. D(Nevertheless)는 대조 기능이 있어 강한 오답이지만, 키프초게의 예상이 주마의 행동을 가로막는 요소가 아니므로 '그럼에도'의 양보 의미는 부정확함. B·C는 각각 구체화·인과로 논리상 배제됨. 한국어·영어 해설 결론 및 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 자연스러움. 케냐 마타투·Ngong Road·stage 등 배경 사실 문제 없음. 오독 시 D를 고르기 쉬운 설계로 medium 적합.

advisory.note: Instead가 '예상된 비웃음 대신 실제로 한 행동'을 정확히 나타낸다. 매력적인 오답은 D(Nevertheless)로, 역접이라는 점에서 일부 맞아 보여 비교가 필요하다. 오답 C(As a result)도 그럴듯하다. 중간 난이도에 맞다.

problem.passage:
Every November, Rodrigo and Estéban met at the shearing shed between their two ranches to see who could clip more ewes before sundown. For years the contest had been fierce: each man counted fleeces under his breath and glanced at the other's pile between animals. This year, Rodrigo pulled ahead early and seemed certain to win. ______ he found himself slowing down to watch Estéban turn a struggling ewe with one easy twist of his wrist, a move Rodrigo had never managed in forty seasons, and he forgot to keep counting.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: Every November, Rodrigo and Estéban met at the shearing shed between their two ranches to see who could clip more ewes before sundown. For years the contest had been fierce: each man counted fleeces under his breath and glanced at the other's pile between animals. This year, Rodrigo pulled ahead early and seemed certain to win. ______ he found himself slowing down to watch Estéban turn a struggling ewe with one easy twist of his wrist, a move Rodrigo had never managed in forty seasons, and he forgot to keep counting.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Consequently,
For example,
Yet
Similarly,
problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 Rodrigo가 앞서 나가 승리가 확실해 보였다는 내용이고, 뒤 문장은 그가 오히려 속도를 늦추고 Estéban의 기술을 지켜보며 세는 것도 잊었다는 예상 밖의 전개이므로 대조를 나타내는 C가 정답이다. A는 앞서 나간 것이 속도를 늦춘 원인인 것처럼 만드는데, 지문에서 그가 늦춘 이유는 Estéban의 솜씨이지 자신의 우위가 아니다. B는 뒤 문장을 앞서 나간 상황의 사례로 만들지만, 속도를 늦추는 것은 앞서 나가는 것의 예가 아니다. D는 두 문장이 비슷한 내용이라고 연결하지만, 둘은 서로 반대 방향이다.
problem.explanationEn: The previous sentence says Rodrigo pulled ahead and seemed certain to win. The next sentence turns against that expectation: he slows down to admire Estéban's skill and stops counting. That is a contrast, so C is correct. A treats his lead as the cause of his slowing down, but the text says he slows down because of Estéban's skill, not because he is ahead. B presents slowing down as an example of pulling ahead, which doesn't make sense. D signals that the two ideas are alike, but they actually point in opposite directions.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Neighbors Rodrigo and Estéban on a Patagonian sheep ranch engage in an annual shearing contest where competition yields to appreciation of each other's weathered skill.

hardJudge.note: 앞 문장(앞서 나가 승리 확실) ↔ 뒤 문장(속도를 늦추고 세는 것을 잊음)은 명확한 대조이므로 C 'Yet'이 정답. 해설(한·영)은 정답과 선택지 글자 참조가 일치하고 결론이 동일하며 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 'Yet' 뒤에 쉼표가 없는 점은 표준 용법상 허용되나 다른 선택지와 표기 형식이 약간 다름(감점 사유는 아님). 난이도: A(Consequently)는 '앞서서 방심→느려짐'으로 오독 가능한 부분적 매력 오답이지만, B·D는 매력도가 낮아 medium 하한에 가까움.

advisory.note: '승리 확실'에서 '속도를 늦추고 세기를 잊음'으로 넘어가는 대조가 분명하므로 Yet이 정답이다. 오답 A(Consequently)는 앞서 나가서 방심해 늦췄다고 읽히면 그럴듯해 보이는 함정이지만, 실제로 늦춘 이유는 Estéban의 기술이므로 문맥을 확인해야 배제된다. B와 D는 비교적 쉽게 배제된다. 중간 난이도의 하단에 해당하지만 적합하다.

problem.passage:
For eleven years, Adeyemi and Olusegun had kept their cloth stalls at opposite ends of the Ebute Metta market, each undercutting the other's prices and whispering to customers that the rival's indigo faded after one wash. When word spread in 1924 that a British trading firm would soon flood the town with cheap machine-printed fabric, Adeyemi expected Olusegun to slash his prices yet again, hoping to outlast them both. ______ Olusegun appeared at Adeyemi's stall one evening with a kola nut and a proposal: they would buy dye together, split the cost, and sell their hand-dyed cloth at a single shared price.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: For eleven years, Adeyemi and Olusegun had kept their cloth stalls at opposite ends of the Ebute Metta market, each undercutting the other's prices and whispering to customers that the rival's indigo faded after one wash. When word spread in 1924 that a British trading firm would soon flood the town with cheap machine-printed fabric, Adeyemi expected Olusegun to slash his prices yet again, hoping to outlast them both. ______ Olusegun appeared at Adeyemi's stall one evening with a kola nut and a proposal: they would buy dye together, split the cost, and sell their hand-dyed cloth at a single shared price.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Instead,
As a result,
Similarly,
For example,
problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 Adeyemi가 Olusegun이 또 가격을 내릴 것이라 예상했다는 내용이고, 뒤 문장은 Olusegun이 오히려 협력을 제안했다는 내용이므로, 예상과 다른 행동을 제시하는 A가 정답이다. B는 외국 회사의 위협이 협력의 원인처럼 보여 그럴듯하지만, 바로 앞 문장의 내용은 '가격 인하 예상'이므로 그 결과로 협력 제안이 나온다는 연결은 논리에 맞지 않는다. C는 두 행동이 비슷하다는 뜻인데, 가격 경쟁과 협력은 서로 반대되는 행동이다. D는 뒤 문장이 앞 문장의 예시여야 하지만, 협력 제안은 가격 인하 예상의 사례가 아니다.
problem.explanationEn: The previous sentence tells you what Adeyemi expected: that Olusegun would cut his prices again. The next sentence shows Olusegun doing the opposite by proposing a partnership, so A, which introduces an alternative to what was expected, is correct. B is tempting because the British firm's threat really does cause the alliance, but the sentence right before the blank is about Adeyemi's expectation of more price-cutting, and a cooperative proposal does not follow as a result of that. C signals similarity, but price-cutting and cooperation are opposite actions. D would make the proposal an example of the expected price war, and it isn't one.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In 1920s Lagos market town, traders Adeyemi and Olusegun transform their cutthroat rivalry into cautious alliance when facing an external economic threat together.

hardJudge.note: 정답 A 검산 완료: 앞 문장은 '가격 인하 예상', 뒤 문장은 '협력 제안'으로 예상과 반대되는 행동이므로 'Instead'가 유일하게 논리적. B는 외국 회사 위협→협력이라는 큰 맥락의 인과 때문에 부분적 매력이 있어 비교가 필요하나, C·D는 비교적 쉽게 배제됨(오답 중 부분적 근거를 가진 것이 사실상 1개). 다만 '예상 vs 실제'라는 두 단계 판단이 요구되어 medium 범위에는 들어감. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답과 일치하며 글자 참조 정확, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 지문은 창작으로 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 A(Instead)가 예상(가격 인하)과 실제 행동(협력 제안)의 대비를 정확히 나타낸다. B는 외국 회사의 위협이 협력의 원인이라는 점에서 그럴듯한 오답이다. C·D는 쉽게 배제되지만 문장으로서 어색하지 않다. 서술형 문맥에서 예상과 실제를 대비하는 판단이 필요해 medium 난이도에 적합하다. 1924년 영국 무역회사가 들어왔다는 설정은 허구 서사로 볼 수 있어 사실 오류로 보지 않는다.

problem.passage:
For thirty-one years, Station Master Crawford had refused to make any decision at the Wheatland grain elevator until he had copied the barometer reading into his ledger in neat, slanted figures. So when the sky to the west turned the color of bruised plums and his young replacement, Lise Moreau, called out that hail would reach the bins within minutes, his hand drifted toward the ledger as it always had. ______ he set the pencil down, looked once at her, and told her to seal the doors.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: For thirty-one years, Station Master Crawford had refused to make any decision at the Wheatland grain elevator until he had copied the barometer reading into his ledger in neat, slanted figures. So when the sky to the west turned the color of bruised plums and his young replacement, Lise Moreau, called out that hail would reach the bins within minutes, his hand drifted toward the ledger as it always had. ______ he set the pencil down, looked once at her, and told her to seal the doors.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: As a result,
Similarly,
For instance,
Even so,
problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 크로퍼드가 평소 습관대로 장부에 손을 뻗었다고 말하고, 뒷문장은 그가 연필을 내려놓고 후임자의 판단을 따랐다고 말하므로 습관과 반대되는 행동이 이어진다. 따라서 앞 내용을 인정한 뒤 반전시키는 D가 정답이다. A는 리즈의 경고를 원인으로 보면 그럴듯하지만, 바로 앞 내용은 습관적으로 장부에 손을 뻗은 행동이고 이것이 연필을 내려놓는 결과를 낳지는 않는다. B는 습관을 따르는 비슷한 행동이 이어질 때만 맞는데, 뒷문장은 습관을 깨는 행동이다. C는 뒷문장이 앞의 일반적 진술에 대한 사례가 아니므로 맞지 않다.
problem.explanationEn: The previous sentence says Crawford's hand moved toward the ledger out of habit, and the next sentence shows him putting the pencil down and following Lise's call, which goes against that habit. So you need a transition that admits the first point and then reverses it, and that is D. A might look right if you treat Lise's warning as the cause, but the sentence right before the blank describes his habitual reach for the ledger, and that reach does not lead to him dropping the pencil. B would fit only if he did something similar that kept his routine, but he breaks it instead. C doesn't work because the final sentence is not an example of a general claim made earlier.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — At a prairie Canadian grain elevator, Station Master Crawford's meticulous routine shatters when a sudden prairie storm forces him to trust his younger replacement's instincts.

hardJudge.note: 앞 문장(습관대로 장부로 손이 감) ↔ 뒷문장(연필을 내려놓고 지시) 사이의 반전이 명확하여 D(Even so)가 정답. A는 리즈의 경고를 원인으로 보면 훑어 읽을 때 그럴듯한 매력적 오답, B·C는 논리적으로 배제 가능. 해설 한·영 일치, 글자 참조 정확, 한글 혼입 없음. 창작 서사 지문으로 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 습관적으로 장부에 손을 뻗은 행동과 연필을 내려놓는 행동이 대조되므로 'Even so'가 정답이다. A는 리즈의 경고를 원인으로 읽으면 그럴듯해서 오답 유인 역할을 한다. B와 C는 비교적 쉽게 배제된다. 곡물 엘리베이터에 'Station Master'라는 직함을 붙인 점은 조금 어색하지만 문항 판단에는 영향이 없다.

problem.passage:
In the cold winter of 1947, Frau Weber spread the parts of her tenant's broken music box across the kitchen table of her Vienna boarding house. She told herself the work was purely practical: the young violinist upstairs was behind on his rent, and a small favor might keep him from leaving before spring. ______ when she finally fit the bent comb back into place and the cylinder began to turn, she found that she had set down her tweezers and was quietly humming along, recalling the lullaby her sister had sung to their children before the war took them all.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: In the cold winter of 1947, Frau Weber spread the parts of her tenant's broken music box across the kitchen table of her Vienna boarding house. She told herself the work was purely practical: the young violinist upstairs was behind on his rent, and a small favor might keep him from leaving before spring. ______ when she finally fit the bent comb back into place and the cylinder began to turn, she found that she had set down her tweezers and was quietly humming along, recalling the lullaby her sister had sung to their children before the war took them all.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Consequently,
Indeed,
Similarly,
Even so,
problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 Frau Weber가 수리를 순전히 실용적인 일(집세 문제)로 여겼다고 말하고, 뒷 문장은 멜로디가 그녀의 개인적 상실의 기억을 일깨워 실용적 태도와 어긋나는 반응을 보였다고 말하므로 대조를 나타내는 D가 정답이다. A는 실용적 동기가 감정적 반응을 일으켰다는 인과 관계를 만들지만, 집세 계산이 허밍과 회상의 원인이 될 수는 없다. B는 앞 내용을 강조하거나 확증하는 말인데, 뒷 문장은 '순전히 실용적'이라는 생각을 뒷받침하지 않고 오히려 뒤집는다. C는 두 문장이 비슷한 내용을 담고 있음을 뜻하지만, 실용적 동기와 감정적 회상은 서로 비슷하지 않고 대립한다.
problem.explanationEn: The first sentence says Frau Weber saw the repair as purely practical, a way to keep a tenant who owed rent. The next sentence shows the melody pulling her into private grief, which goes against that practical view, so you need a contrast: choice D. Choice A sets up cause and effect, but her concern about rent can't explain why she ended up humming and remembering her sister. Choice B would confirm or stress the first sentence, yet the second sentence undercuts the idea that the work was "purely practical." Choice C suggests the two sentences say similar things, but practical motives and emotional memory pull in opposite directions here.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In postwar Vienna, Frau Weber repairs a broken music box belonging to her boarding house tenant, its melody unlocking her own suppressed memories of lost loved ones.

hardJudge.note: 앞 문장 'told herself ... purely practical'과 뒷 문장의 감정적 반응(허밍·회상) 사이의 대조가 명확하여 'Even so,'가 유일한 정답. 'Even so, when she finally...' 구문도 문법적으로 자연스러움. A(Consequently)는 수리 행위→완성이라는 표면적 인과로 훑어 읽으면 끌릴 수 있고, B(Indeed)는 앞 문장 강조로 부분 근거가 있어 비교 필요; C도 문맥상 말은 됨. 'told herself'라는 단서를 포착해 대조를 판단해야 하므로 medium 적합. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 D를 일관되게 뒷받침하며 오답 배제 근거 정확. 창작 서사로 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: "told herself"라는 단서와 실제 감정 반응이 대조를 이뤄 Even so가 명확하다. 하지만 지문을 훑어 읽으면 Indeed나 Consequently를 고를 여지가 있어 medium 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 선생님이 자신의 은퇴를 한 번도 언급하지 않았다고 말하고, 뒷문장은 그럼에도 학생들이 모든 예시에서 이별의 의미를 알아챘다고 말한다. 언급하지 않았는데도 알아챘다는 양보 후 반전 관계이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 뒷문장에 예시가 나열되어 그럴듯하지만, 그 예시들은 앞 문장에서 말한 '은퇴를 언급하지 않음'의 사례가 아니다. B는 언급하지 않은 것이 학생들이 알아챈 원인이 되는 것이 아니므로 인과가 맞지 않는다. D는 두 문장이 같은 종류의 내용이 아니라 서로 대조되므로 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The first sentence tells you Mr. Jayasinghe never mentioned that he was being replaced, and the next says the students still noticed that his examples were all about parting. They picked up on the farewell even though he never said it, so the sentences show a concession followed by a reversal, and C is correct. A is tempting because the second sentence lists examples, but those examples don't illustrate his silence about retiring. B is wrong because his silence isn't what caused the students to notice. D doesn't work because the two sentences contrast with each other instead of making similar points.

hardJudge.note: 앞 문장(교체 사실을 한 번도 언급하지 않음)과 뒷문장(그래도 학생들이 알아챔)은 양보-반전 관계이므로 C가 유일하게 성립. A는 뒷문장에 예시 나열이 있어 훑어 읽으면 끌리는 강한 오답, B는 서사 흐름상 그럴듯해 보이는 인과 오답, D도 '두 반쪽' 반복 이미지 때문에 표면적으로 말이 됨. 두 단계 판단(앞 문장의 '언급 안 함' 파악 + 뒷문장의 '그럼에도 알아챔' 연결) 요구로 medium 적합. 원창작 지문으로 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 'Even so'(언급하지 않았지만 그럼에도 학생들이 알아챘다)는 명확하다. 뒤에 예시 목록이 이어져 A가 매력적인 오답 역할을 하고, B와 D도 그럴듯하다. 중간 난이도에 적합하다.

For years, Otto had kept the small brass key from his mother's estate in a saucer on the windowsill of his room at the Vienna boarding house, never guessing what it might open. When it finally turned the lock of the dented trunk in the attic, he expected to find letters confirming what his parents had always told him: that the family had lived quietly in Linz throughout the war. ______ the papers inside were passports and baptismal certificates showing his parents' faces above names he had never heard, each official stamp ever so slightly crooked.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Consequently,
Likewise,
Nevertheless,
Instead,
problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 Otto가 부모의 말을 확인해 줄 편지를 기대했다는 내용이고, 뒷 문장은 실제로 위조 서류가 나왔다는 내용이므로 기대가 다른 것으로 대체되었음을 나타내는 D가 정답이다. A는 기대가 위조 서류의 원인이라는 뜻이 되어 인과 관계가 성립하지 않는다. B는 두 문장이 비슷한 내용이라는 뜻이지만 실제로는 정반대다. C는 대조를 담고 있어 그럴듯하지만, 앞 내용에도 '불구하고' 무언가가 계속된다는 양보를 나타낼 뿐이어서 기대가 다른 결과로 바뀌었다는 관계를 표현하지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: The first sentence tells you what Otto expected to find: letters confirming his parents' story. The next sentence tells you what he actually found: forged documents with other names. Because the real contents take the place of what he expected, choice D is correct. Choice A is wrong because his expectation didn't cause the forgeries to be there. Choice B is wrong because it signals similarity, but the two sentences contradict each other. Choice C may look right because it signals contrast, but it means "despite this," which describes something holding true in spite of a point, not a discovery that overturns an expectation.

hardJudge.note: 앞 문장 '기대(편지)' vs 뒷 문장 '실제(위조 여권·세례증명서)'의 대체 관계이므로 'Instead'가 가장 정확함. 'Nevertheless'는 대조라는 점에서 그럴듯한 강력한 오답으로 기능하며, 'Consequently'(인과 없음)·'Likewise'(유사성 없음)는 명확히 배제됨. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 D를 일관되게 지지하고 선택지 참조 일치, 한글 혼입 없음. 지문은 창작 서사로 저작권 문제 없음. 기대·실제 파악 + instead/nevertheless 구분의 두 단계 판단이 필요해 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: '기대와 실제가 대체되는 관계'를 짚어 Instead와 Nevertheless를 구분해야 하므로 medium에 맞다. 다만 A와 B는 비교적 쉽게 배제된다.

Now the handwritten list of reasons she should stay, along with two jars of pecan pralines he had bartered from a deckhand, ______ waiting on her bunk when she returned to her cabin.

problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: were
was
is
having been
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'list'이고, 'along with two jars...'는 삽입구라서 주어를 복수로 만들지 않는다. 또 'when she returned'와 지문 전체가 과거 시제이므로 단수 과거형 동사가 필요하다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 과거 시제는 맞지만, 삽입구 속 복수 명사 'jars'에 맞춘 복수형이라 틀리다. C는 단수형이지만 현재 시제라 과거 문맥과 어긋나고, D는 분사라서 문장에 정동사가 없게 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "list." The phrase "along with two jars..." is an interrupting phrase, so it doesn't make the subject plural. The clause "when she returned" and the rest of the passage are also in the past tense, so the sentence needs a singular past-tense verb. That makes B the correct answer. A is in the right tense, but it's plural because it agrees with "jars," the plural noun inside the interrupting phrase. C is singular but in the present tense, which clashes with the past-tense context, and D is a participle, so it leaves the sentence without a main verb.

advisory.note: 주어 list(단수)와 동사 사이에 삽입구 along with ... jars ... from a deckhand가 끼어 있어 수일치를 정확히 따져야 하고, 시제도 확인해야 하므로 판단 단계가 둘이다. A는 근접한 복수 명사에 끌리기 쉬운 강한 오답이고, C는 수는 맞지만 시제가 틀린 부분 정답형 오답이며, D도 그럴듯한 오답이다. 목표 난이도 medium에 적합하다.

have rested
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "Its envelope"이며, "together with ... inside"는 주어 수에 영향을 주지 않는 삽입구이다. 따라서 단수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 필요하며, 이야기 시제가 과거이므로 C "rested"가 맞다. A "were resting"은 삽입구 속 복수 명사 photographs에 끌린 복수 동사여서 틀린다. B "resting"은 분사여서 문장에 정동사가 없게 된다. D "have rested"는 복수형인 데다 과거 서술 흐름과 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "Its envelope." The phrase "together with ... inside" is an interrupting phrase and does not change the subject's number. So you need a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject, and since the story is told in the past tense, C, "rested," is correct. A, "were resting," is plural because it gets pulled toward the plural noun "photographs" inside the interrupting phrase. B, "resting," is a participle, which would leave the sentence without a main verb. D, "have rested," is plural, and it also doesn't fit the past-tense narration.

hardJudge.note: 주어 "Its envelope"(단수) + "together with ..." 삽입구 → 단수 과거 정동사 "rested"가 유일하게 적합. A는 삽입구의 복수 명사에 끌린 근접 오류, D는 수·시제 모두 불일치, B는 정동사 부재로 각각 배제됨. 해설(한·영) 모두 정답과 선택지 글자 참조가 일치하고 논리적 모순 없음. 삽입구 무시 + 시제 확인의 두 단계 판단이 요구되어 medium에 적합. 다만 문장 말미 "unable to open it and unable to look away"가 형식상 Chioma에 걸리는지 다소 느슨하나(원래 서술 의도상 Chioma), 평가 대상 밑줄과 무관하여 정답 판정에 영향 없음.

advisory.note: 'together with' 삽입구를 넘어 단수 주어와 수를 맞춘 뒤 시제까지 확인해야 하므로 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. A는 attraction을 노린 그럴듯한 오답이다. 'rested'는 과거 서술 흐름과도 맞는다.

options: were set down
being set down
having been set down
was set down
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "The sum"이고, "like the thousands of others ... windowpanes"는 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어든 수식어구이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 단수 정동사가 필요하므로 D "was set down"이 정답이다. A는 정동사이긴 하지만 수식어구 속 복수 명사(thousands, winters, windowpanes)에 수를 맞춘 복수형이라 틀렸다. B와 C는 분사 형태라서 주어 "The sum"에 정동사를 제공하지 못하므로 "and" 앞의 절이 불완전해진다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this clause is the singular noun "The sum." The phrase "like the thousands of others ... windowpanes" just comes between the subject and its verb. So the blank needs a singular finite verb, which makes D, "was set down," correct. A is a finite verb, but it's plural because it agrees with the plural nouns inside the interrupting phrase (thousands, winters, windowpanes). B and C are participles, so they don't give "The sum" a main verb, and that leaves the clause before "and" incomplete.

Choice B (the participle "having learned") and Choice C (the relative clause "who had learned") are both just modifiers, so they would leave the sentence with no main verb. Choice D uses "have," which is plural and so doesn't agree with "calf," and its present perfect tense also clashes with the past-tense narration.

advisory.note: 주어와 동사 사이에 긴 동격어구와 독립분사구가 끼어 있어서 본동사가 필요하다는 점을 놓치기 쉽다. B와 C는 훑어 읽으면 그럴듯해 보이고, D는 수 일치에서 걸러진다. 중간 난이도로 적절하다.

problem.explanation: 이 절의 주어는 단수 명사 "patter"이고, "of numbers"와 관계절 "that he had always used...hesitations"는 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 단수 정동사가 필요하며, 뒤의 "hung"과 병렬을 이루는 과거 시제여야 하므로 D "caught"가 정답이다. A는 정동사이긴 하지만 복수형이라 가까이 있는 "hesitations"나 "numbers"에 잘못 일치시킨 것이다. B 역시 복수형이고 현재완료라서 과거 시제의 서술 흐름과 맞지 않는다. C는 분사라서 절에 정동사가 없게 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this clause is the singular noun "patter." The phrase "of numbers" and the relative clause "that he had always used...hesitations" only modify it. So you need a singular main verb in the past tense, matching "hung" in the parallel clause, which makes D, "caught," correct. A is a main verb, but it's plural, so it wrongly agrees with the nearby "numbers" or "hesitations." B is also plural, and its present perfect tense doesn't fit the past-tense narration. C is a participle, which would leave the clause without a main verb.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — At a Montana ranch auction, weathered auctioneer Dalton pauses mid-bid when a mysterious woman appears at the lunch table, her presence unsettling the familiar rhythms of inherited land and loss.

hardJudge.note: 주어 "patter"(단수)와 동사 사이에 "of numbers"와 긴 관계절("that he had always used to carry bidders past their hesitations")이 끼어 있어 근접 명사 "hesitations/numbers"에 잘못 일치시키기 쉬운 전형적 medium 구조. 과거 시제 서술("sat down", "hung")과의 일치까지 두 단계 판단 필요. A는 정동사이나 복수, B는 복수+현재완료, C는 비정동사로 절에 본동사가 없음. D "caught"만 단수·과거로 적합. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답과 선택지 참조가 일치하며 오류 없음. 지문은 독창적 서사로 저작권 우려 없음.

advisory.note: 주어 patter와 동사 사이가 길게 떨어져 있고(관계절 끝 hesitations가 복수), 시제는 hung과 병렬을 이루므로 두 단계 판단이 필요해 medium에 맞다. C(분사)는 비교적 쉽게 배제된다.

problem.passage:
Every morning Giorgi still unlocked the schoolhouse at the edge of the village, a squat stone building whose stove no one had lit since the last family left for Tbilisi. On the final day of the term, he wrote a proof on the board for desks that held only dust______ line of chalk, slanted carefully the way he had taught a generation of children to slant theirs, seemed to him less an equation than a name.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Every morning Giorgi still unlocked the schoolhouse at the edge of the village, a squat stone building whose stove no one had lit since the last family left for Tbilisi. On the final day of the term, he wrote a proof on the board for desks that held only dust______ line of chalk, slanted carefully the way he had taught a generation of children to slant theirs, seemed to him less an equation than a name.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , each
; each
each
and, each
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'he wrote ... only dust'는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 'each line of chalk ... seemed to him ...'도 삽입구를 사이에 둔 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 이을 수 있으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 되는데, 삽입구 때문에 뒤쪽을 수식어로 잘못 읽으면 맞아 보인다. C는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문이다. D는 등위접속사 and를 쓰긴 했지만 쉼표가 and 앞이 아니라 뒤에 와서 잘못 배치되었다.
problem.explanationEn: The text before the blank ("he wrote ... only dust") is an independent clause. The text after it ("each line of chalk ... seemed to him ...") is also an independent clause: its subject and verb are just separated by a long interrupting phrase. You can join two independent clauses with a semicolon, so B is correct. A joins them with only a comma, which creates a comma splice; it can look right if the interrupting phrase makes you misread the second part as a modifier. C fuses the two clauses with no punctuation, which makes it a run-on. D uses the conjunction "and," but the comma comes after "and" instead of before it, so it's misplaced.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In a Soviet-era Georgian mountain village, retired teacher Giorgi delivers his final lesson on mathematics to empty desks, his chalk marks becoming elegies for students scattered across distant cities.

hardJudge.note: 검산: 빈칸 앞 "he wrote a proof ... only dust"는 독립절, 빈칸 뒤 "each line of chalk, [분사구 삽입], seemed to him less an equation than a name"도 주어(each line)+동사(seemed)를 갖춘 독립절. 세미콜론(B)만 적법. A는 콤마 스플라이스, C는 무종지문, D는 "dust and, each line..."으로 and 뒤 쉼표가 잘못 배치됨. 한·영 해설 모두 B를 정확히 뒷받침하고 글자 참조 일치, 한글 혼입 없음. 긴 삽입구 때문에 뒤쪽 절의 독립성을 확인해야 하는 두 단계 판단이 필요해 medium에 적합. 오답 A·D는 부분적 근거가 있고 C도 말이 됨. 지문은 창작 서사로 저작권 의심 없음. 선택지 C·D 앞 이중 공백은 공백 포함 선택지 표기로 보여 형식상 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 'each line ... seemed'가 독립절이라 세미콜론(B)만 맞음. 긴 삽입구 때문에 A가 그럴듯해 보여 중간 난이도에 맞음. D는 배제가 쉬운 편이지만 허용 범위.

problem.passage:
When Madame Rousseau pried loose the cracked hinge of the jewelry box, a walnut case the pawnbroker had wrapped carelessly in yesterday's newspaper, she found what the damage had long kept hidden______ someone had etched a column of tiny dates, each one falling within the years of the Occupation, beside a pair of initials that were not her late husband's.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: When Madame Rousseau pried loose the cracked hinge of the jewelry box, a walnut case the pawnbroker had wrapped carelessly in yesterday's newspaper, she found what the damage had long kept hidden______ someone had etched a column of tiny dates, each one falling within the years of the Occupation, beside a pair of initials that were not her late husband's.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , beneath the lining,
beneath the lining,
; and beneath the lining,
: beneath the lining,
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "she found what the damage had long kept hidden"은 완전한 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "someone had etched..."도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 콜론은 앞 절이 예고한 '숨겨진 것'의 정체를 뒤 절이 밝혀 주므로 D가 정답이다. A는 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B는 "beneath the lining"이 앞 절의 hidden에 붙는 수식어처럼 읽혀 그럴듯하지만, 결국 쉼표 하나로 두 독립절을 연결하므로 역시 쉼표 오용이다. C는 세미콜론 뒤에 등위접속사 and를 불필요하게 덧붙여 어법에 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The part before the blank, "she found what the damage had long kept hidden," is a complete independent clause, and "someone had etched..." after the blank is also an independent clause with its own subject and verb. A colon works here because the second clause reveals what the first clause promises (the thing that was hidden), so D is correct. A joins the two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B is tempting because "beneath the lining" seems to describe where something was hidden, but the clauses are still joined by a single comma, so it is also a comma splice. C adds the coordinating conjunction "and" after a semicolon, which is unnecessary and nonstandard.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In a 1950s Parisian bookshop, Madame Rousseau's antique jewelry box arrives broken from a pawnbroker, and its repair reveals hand-etched dates marking a forbidden wartime romance.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞("she found what the damage had long kept hidden")과 뒤("someone had etched...")가 모두 독립절이며, 뒤 절이 앞 절의 '숨겨진 것'을 구체화하므로 콜론(D)이 정답임을 검산으로 확인. A·B는 쉼표 오용, C는 세미콜론+and 조합으로 SAT 기준상 오답. 다만 C의 "; and"는 일부 스타일 가이드(절 내부에 쉼표가 많은 경우)에서 허용되는 형태라 엄밀히는 가장 약한 오답이지만, SAT 관행상 오답 처리로 무리 없음. 선택지 B 앞 공백이 이중으로 들어간 사소한 표기 흔적 외 형식 문제 없음. 해설(한·영) 결론·글자 참조 일치, 난이도는 두 독립절 판별 + 콜론 기능 확인의 2단계 판단으로 medium 적합.

advisory.note: D의 콜론 뒤에 독립절이 오고, 그 절이 앞에서 예고한 '숨겨진 것'이 무엇인지 밝혀 주므로 문법적으로 옳다. A와 B는 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이다. B에서는 'hidden beneath the lining'이 이어져 읽히는 함정이 있다. C처럼 세미콜론 뒤에 and를 붙이는 것은 SAT 기준상 비표준이다. 앞의 수식 삽입구가 길어서 앞 절이 어디서 끝나는지 따로 확인해야 하므로 medium 난이도에 맞다. B 선택지 앞의 공백이 두 칸인 것은 사소한 형식 문제다.

problem.passage:
The inn at Kanaura smelled of brine and charcoal. Across the low table, Hirokichi kept turning his cup, a chipped celadon piece the innkeeper had set before him without apology ______ did not seem to notice that Tomoe had stopped pouring the moment he spoke the name Oyuki.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: The inn at Kanaura smelled of brine and charcoal. Across the low table, Hirokichi kept turning his cup, a chipped celadon piece the innkeeper had set before him without apology ______ did not seem to notice that Tomoe had stopped pouring the moment he spoke the name Oyuki.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , he
; he
he
, and while he
problem.explanation: "Hirokichi kept turning his cup"는 완전한 독립절이고, 그 뒤의 "a chipped celadon piece ... without apology"는 cup을 설명하는 동격구일 뿐입니다. 빈칸 뒤 "he did not seem to notice..."도 또 하나의 독립절이므로, 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결해야 하고 정답은 B입니다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 됩니다. C는 아무 부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 run-on 문장이 됩니다. D는 and 뒤에 while이 붙어 두 번째 절이 종속절이 되는데, 이 종속절이 기댈 주절이 없어 불완전한 문장이 됩니다.
problem.explanationEn: "Hirokichi kept turning his cup" is a complete independent clause. The phrase "a chipped celadon piece ... without apology" is just an appositive that describes the cup. After the blank, "he did not seem to notice..." is another independent clause, so you need a semicolon to join the two clauses, which makes B correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, so it's a comma splice. C uses no punctuation at all, so it's a run-on sentence. D adds "while" after "and," which turns the second clause into a dependent clause, and that clause has no main clause to attach to, so the sentence ends up incomplete.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In an Edo-period fishing village, merchant Hirokichi and wandering sake brewer Tomoe meet at an inn and discover through accidental conversation that they once loved the same person decades ago.

hardJudge.note: 검산: "Hirokichi kept turning his cup"(독립절) + 동격구 "a chipped celadon piece ... without apology" 뒤에 "he did not seem to notice..."(독립절)가 이어지므로 세미콜론(B)이 유일한 정답. A는 comma splice, C는 fused sentence, D는 "and while"로 종속절화되어 주절 없는 fragment. 긴 동격구가 첫 절의 경계를 흐려 정독이 필요하며, A·D가 그럴듯한 오답으로 기능하므로 medium 적합. 해설 한·영 모두 정확하고 일치.

advisory.note: 긴 동격구가 첫 독립절의 끝을 가려서, 문장을 정독해야 절 경계를 찾을 수 있음. D는 주절이 없는 종속절로 끝나므로 오답이 맞음. A·C도 그럴듯한 오답임.

problem.passage:
From his seat beside the tram window, Senhor Oliveira had watched the Saints' procession wind down Rua da Graça for fifty-one Junes. This year, a spark from a paper lantern caught the hem of a small boy's Saint Anthony costume, and the crowd, a tangle of grandmothers, fishmongers, and brass-band players who had been singing together only moments earlier, ______ neighbors shoved past neighbors, and no one seemed certain whose child the boy was.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: From his seat beside the tram window, Senhor Oliveira had watched the Saints' procession wind down Rua da Graça for fifty-one Junes. This year, a spark from a paper lantern caught the hem of a small boy's Saint Anthony costume, and the crowd, a tangle of grandmothers, fishmongers, and brass-band players who had been singing together only moments earlier, ______ neighbors shoved past neighbors, and no one seemed certain whose child the boy was.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: broke apart neighbors
broke apart, neighbors
broke apart: neighbors
broke apart; and neighbors
problem.explanation: 긴 동격어구를 건너뛰면 주어 "the crowd"와 동사 "broke apart"로 이루어진 독립절이 보인다. 그 뒤의 "neighbors shoved past neighbors..."도 독립절이며, 군중이 흩어진 모습을 구체적으로 설명한다. 따라서 앞 절을 부연하는 독립절을 이어 주는 콜론을 쓴 C가 정답이다. A는 두 독립절을 문장부호 없이 붙인 융합문이고, B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이은 콤마 스플라이스이다. D는 세미콜론과 등위접속사 "and"를 함께 써서 표준 영어 규칙에 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: If you skip the long appositive, you can see an independent clause made of the subject "the crowd" and the verb "broke apart." The words that follow, "neighbors shoved past neighbors...," form another independent clause that shows exactly how the crowd broke apart. A colon correctly introduces an independent clause that explains the one before it, so C is correct. A fuses the two independent clauses with no punctuation at all, and B joins them with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. D uses a semicolon together with the coordinating conjunction "and," which is not standard.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Aboard a Lisbon tram line, elderly passenger Senhor Oliveira watches the annual Saints' festival procession derail into chaos when a child's costume catches fire, exposing fragile community bonds.

hardJudge.note: 주어 "the crowd"와 동사 "broke apart" 사이에 긴 동격어구가 삽입되어 있어 독립절 구조를 파악하는 단계와, 이어지는 "neighbors shoved past neighbors, and no one seemed certain…"이 독립절임을 확인하는 단계가 필요하다. C(콜론)는 앞 절을 부연하는 독립절을 올바르게 연결한다. A는 융합문, B는 콤마 스플라이스, D는 세미콜론+등위접속사로 SAT 기준 비표준이다. D가 그럴듯한 오답으로 기능하고 A·B도 구조 파악 없이는 혼동될 수 있어 medium에 적합하다. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답과 선택지 참조가 일치하며 오류 없음.

advisory.note: 긴 동격어구와 관계절이 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있어 두 단계 판단이 필요하므로 medium 수준에 맞다. 정답 C(콜론 뒤에 설명하는 독립절이 옴)는 옳다. D의 '; and'는 실제 문체에서 가끔 허용되지만, SAT 관례상 오답으로 보는 것이 일반적이다. 다만 A와 B는 같은 오류 계열(융합문, 콤마 스플라이스)이라 오답을 고르는 판단 근거가 다소 단순하다.

problem.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Freight handler Mackenzie has found an undelivered envelope in the office of a prairie grain elevator.

The elevator at Dunmore—its red paint flaking into the ditch, its town name stenciled in letters taller than ______ had stood empty of grain for three years when she finally agreed to drive the forgotten letter six hours west, past a dozen towns that, like Dunmore, were quietly closing.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Freight handler Mackenzie has found an undelivered envelope in the office of a prairie grain elevator.

The elevator at Dunmore—its red paint flaking into the ditch, its town name stenciled in letters taller than ______ had stood empty of grain for three years when she finally agreed to drive the forgotten letter six hours west, past a dozen towns that, like Dunmore, were quietly closing.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: Mackenzie—
Mackenzie,
Mackenzie;
Mackenzie—it
problem.explanation: "its red paint ... taller than Mackenzie"는 대시로 시작된 비필수 삽입구이므로 같은 대시로 닫아야 주어 "The elevator at Dunmore"와 동사 "had stood"가 연결된다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표로 닫아 앞의 대시와 짝이 맞지 않는다. C는 세미콜론으로 주어와 동사를 갈라 앞부분이 완전한 절이 되지 못한다. D는 대시로 제대로 닫지만 주어 "it"이 더해져 "The elevator at Dunmore"가 동사 없이 남게 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The phrase "its red paint ... taller than Mackenzie" is a nonessential interruption that opens with a dash, so it has to close with a dash too. Then the subject "The elevator at Dunmore" connects to its verb "had stood," which makes A correct. B closes the interruption with a comma, so it doesn't match the opening dash. C puts a semicolon between the subject and the verb, which leaves the first part without a complete clause. D closes with a dash correctly, but the extra subject "it" leaves "The elevator at Dunmore" without a verb.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On a prairie Canadian grain elevator, freight handler Mackenzie drives six hours to deliver a single forgotten letter, the absurdity of her journey mirroring the town's slow disappearance.

hardJudge.note: 대시로 시작한 삽입구("its red paint ... taller than Mackenzie")를 대시로 닫아 주어 "The elevator at Dunmore"와 동사 "had stood"를 연결하는 A가 유일하게 옳음. B는 구두점 짝 불일치, C는 주어-동사 분리, D는 "it"으로 주어 중복(앞부분이 동사 없는 조각). 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답과 선택지 참조가 일치하며 모순 없음. 대시 짝 인식 + D의 추가 주어 판별이라는 두 단계 판단이 필요해 medium 적합. B·D는 부분적 근거가 있는 오답, C도 말이 됨.

advisory.note: 정답은 A가 맞다. 대시 짝 맞추기를 묻는 문항이며, 중간에 끼어든 삽입구가 길어서 대시가 열린 것을 놓치기 쉽다. 이 때문에 B(쉼표)가 그럴듯한 오답이 되고, D는 대시 짝은 맞기 때문에 문장 구조까지 따져야 배제된다. 따라서 medium 난이도에 맞다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- "The Brass of Oberwald" is a short story by the fictional author Liesl Brandauer.
- It follows Ernst and Klaus, rival trumpet players in a Bavarian village brass band.

The student wants to show how Helmut's emotional response develops from the beginning to the end of the scene. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

- At the start of the scene, Helmut remembers the years when the first chair was his and feels a quiet ache.

problem.question: The student wants to show how Helmut's emotional response develops from the beginning to the end of the scene. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In Hartmann's novel, Helmut, who has conducted a Bavarian brass band for four decades, feels a quiet ache when his former student Kathi wins the first-chair audition.
In Hartmann's novel, 24-year-old Kathi Vogl wins the first-chair trumpet audition in a Bavarian village band and performs a solo better than her teacher ever did.
In Hartmann's novel, Helmut at first aches as he recalls once holding the first chair, but after hearing Kathi's solo, he judges that she has surpassed him.
In Hartmann's novel, Helmut once played first trumpet in the band himself, and after Kathi's solo, he decides that she plays the passage better than he ever did.
problem.explanation: 목표는 장면의 처음부터 끝까지 Helmut의 감정이 어떻게 변하는지 보여 주는 것이므로, 처음의 아쉬움과 마지막의 인정을 둘 다 담아야 한다. C는 첫 의자를 차지했던 시절을 떠올리며 느끼는 아픔(처음)과 Kathi의 솔로를 듣고 그녀가 자신을 넘어섰다고 판단하는 것(끝)을 'at first … but after'로 연결하므로 목표를 이룬다. A는 처음의 아픔만 제시해 이후의 변화가 빠져 있다. B는 Kathi와 그녀의 실력에 초점을 맞출 뿐 Helmut의 감정은 드러내지 않는다. D는 마지막의 인정만 담고 처음의 아픔이 없어서 감정의 전개를 보여 주지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to show how Helmut's feelings develop over the scene, so the sentence needs both his early wistfulness and his final admiration. C links his ache at remembering his own years in the first chair (the beginning) to his judgment that Kathi has surpassed him (the end), joining them with "at first … but after," so it meets the goal. A gives only the initial ache and leaves out any change that follows. B focuses on Kathi and how well she plays and never tells you how Helmut feels. D includes only his final admiration and leaves out the earlier ache, so it doesn't show how his feelings develop.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In a Bavarian brass band, aging conductor Helmut watches his protégé rival claim the first-chair position, his wistfulness for lost primacy gradually surrendering to genuine admiration.

hardJudge.note: 정답 C 검산 일치: 장면 처음(첫 의자 시절 회상·아픔)과 끝(Kathi가 자신을 넘어섰다는 판단)을 'at first … but after'로 연결해 감정 전개를 보여 줌. A는 처음만, D는 끝만(배경 정보 추가), B는 Kathi 중심으로 Helmut 감정 부재. A·D가 부분적 근거를 가져 비교 필요, B도 말이 됨 → medium 적합. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 선택지 참조와 결론이 일치하고 영어 자연스러움. 가상의 소설·작가로 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: C만 처음(아픔)과 끝(인정)을 모두 담는다. A와 D는 각각 한쪽만 담고 있어 부분적으로 맞는 매력적 오답이며, B는 초점이 Kathi에게 있다. 영어 해설의 'admiration'은 노트의 '더 잘 연주한다고 판단'을 다소 해석한 표현이지만 허용 범위다.

problem.passage:
In the short story "Elevator Siding," Pavel Hrynchuk, a retired stationmaster, still lives beside the grain elevator in the Saskatchewan town where he worked for forty-one years. One autumn morning a letter arrives from England containing a faded photograph: a dozen children with name tags pinned to their coats, standing on Pavel's platform in 1940. They were evacuees sent overseas during the war, and Pavel, then a young clerk, had promised one of them, a girl named Margaret, that he would be at the station when her mother came to take her home. The mother never came that winter, and Margaret was eventually placed with a farm family farther west. Some readers see Pavel's decades in the town as simple contentment with prairie life. One critic, however, argues that Pavel never left because he continued to regard himself as bound by his words to Margaret, long after anyone could have held him to them.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's interpretation?
problem.stimulus: In the short story "Elevator Siding," Pavel Hrynchuk, a retired stationmaster, still lives beside the grain elevator in the Saskatchewan town where he worked for forty-one years. One autumn morning a letter arrives from England containing a faded photograph: a dozen children with name tags pinned to their coats, standing on Pavel's platform in 1940. They were evacuees sent overseas during the war, and Pavel, then a young clerk, had promised one of them, a girl named Margaret, that he would be at the station when her mother came to take her home. The mother never came that winter, and Margaret was eventually placed with a farm family farther west. Some readers see Pavel's decades in the town as simple contentment with prairie life. One critic, however, argues that Pavel never left because he continued to regard himself as bound by his words to Margaret, long after anyone could have held him to them.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's interpretation?
options: Later in the story, Pavel takes the photograph out of its envelope each evening and recalls with evident fondness the way Margaret laughed at the noise of the grain trucks.
Later in the story, Pavel tells his grandchildren about the evacuation train in vivid detail, describing the smell of coal smoke and the rows of small suitcases on the platform.
Later in the story, Pavel admits to the letter's sender that he never found out whether Margaret's mother had survived the war or tried to reach Canada.
Later in the story, Pavel recalls turning down a promotion to a Winnipeg office, explaining to his wife that someone had to stay on the platform in case a parent ever arrived for one of the children.
problem.explanation: 비평가의 주장은 두 부분으로 이루어져 있다. Pavel이 마을에 남은 것이 만족감 때문이 아니라는 점, 그리고 Margaret에게 한 약속에 여전히 묶여 있다고 느꼈다는 점이다. D는 Pavel이 승진을 거절하고 떠나지 않은 행동을 아이들의 부모가 올 경우를 대비해 플랫폼을 지켜야 한다는 이유와 직접 연결하므로 두 부분을 모두 뒷받침한다. A와 B는 Margaret과 피난에 대한 강한 기억과 애정을 보여 주지만, 이는 단순한 향수일 수도 있고 그가 마을에 남은 이유를 설명하지 못한다. C는 약속과 관련된 미해결 상태를 보여 주지만, 그 사실이 Pavel이 마을에 머문 것과 어떤 관계인지는 드러나지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The critic's claim has two parts: Pavel did not stay in the town out of contentment, and he still felt bound by his promise to Margaret. Choice D links a concrete decision to stay, turning down a promotion, to the reason that someone had to keep watch on the platform for a returning parent, so it supports both parts. Choices A and B show strong memories and affection for Margaret and the evacuation, but those could just be nostalgia, and neither explains why Pavel stayed. Choice C shows that the matter of the promise was never resolved, but it doesn't connect that fact to Pavel's decision to remain in the town.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On a prairie Canadian grain elevator, retired stationmaster Pavel receives an old photograph from a former passenger, igniting memories of a promise made during a wartime evacuation.

hardJudge.note: 정답 D는 '떠나지 않은 결정(승진 거절)'과 '약속에 묶인 이유(부모가 올 경우 대비)'를 직접 연결해 비평가 주장의 두 요소를 모두 충족한다. A·B는 Margaret/피난에 대한 강한 기억·애정이라는 부분적 근거가 있고, C는 약속의 미해결 상태라는 근거가 있으나 모두 '마을에 남은 이유'와 연결되지 않아 비교를 통해서만 배제된다. 두 단계 판단(주장 분해 + 선택지 대조)이 필요하므로 medium에 적합. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 글자 참조와 결론이 일치하고 영어가 자연스러우며 한글 혼입 없음. 지문은 가상의 단편으로 저작권 문제 없음. 1940년 영국 아동 캐나다 피난(CORB) 배경은 역사적으로 타당.

advisory.note: D만이 '떠나지 않음'(승진 거절)과 약속에 대한 의무감을 함께 연결한다. D가 '아이들 중 누구든'으로 범위를 넓혔지만 Margaret과의 약속이라는 핵심과는 여전히 맞는다. A·B는 정서적 애착을 보여 주고 C는 해결되지 않은 상태를 보여 줘서 부분적인 근거를 가진 오답으로 잘 작동한다. 중간 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
The following text is adapted from a 2019 novel. Set in a West Virginia coal town in 1974, it follows nine-year-old Tammy Kincaid.

Every evening the men came up the hill from the Number Four tipple walking stiff-legged, their jacket pockets sagging like overfilled feed sacks. Tammy watched from the porch steps as Mr. Ferrell, who sang bass in church, tried to wave hello without letting a lump of coal tumble out of his sleeve. Her daddy came last. He didn't look at her. He set his lunch pail down very gently, as if it might go off.

A literary critic argues that the novel does not let Tammy's reactions to the men's secret coal-taking settle into either amusement or sorrow alone; instead, the critic claims, the novel presents both feelings as arising for Tammy at the very same moment, each sharpening the other.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's claim?

Tammy watched from the porch steps as Mr. Ferrell, who sang bass in church, tried to wave hello without letting a lump of coal tumble out of his sleeve. Her daddy came last. He didn't look at her. He set his lunch pail down very gently, as if it might go off.

A literary critic argues that the novel does not let Tammy's reactions to the men's secret coal-taking settle into either amusement or sorrow alone; instead, the critic claims, the novel presents both feelings as arising for Tammy at the very same moment, each sharpening the other.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's claim?
options: Later in the same scene, Tammy has to bite her cheek to keep from laughing at the men's lopsided walk, and in that same instant she realizes her throat has gone tight watching her daddy lower his pail.
Later in the same scene, Tammy laughs so hard at Mr. Ferrell's falling coal that her mother scolds her, and she goes to bed still giggling about how silly the grown men looked.
In a chapter set years later, Tammy, now an adult, weeps when she remembers the scene, although as a child she had only found the men's stiff walk comical.
Later in the same scene, Tammy's mother both laughs and cries while telling a neighbor about the men's pockets, though Tammy herself simply watches without understanding.
problem.explanation: 비평가는 Tammy가 재미와 슬픔을 '동시에' 느끼며 두 감정이 서로를 날카롭게 만든다고 주장한다. A는 웃음을 참는 바로 그 순간 아버지를 보며 목이 메는 장면으로, 두 감정과 동시성을 모두 보여 주므로 주장을 가장 직접 뒷받침한다. B는 재미만 있어 오히려 한 감정으로 정착한다는 반례에 가깝다. C는 두 감정이 나타나지만 어린 시절과 성인기로 시간상 분리되어 '같은 순간'이라는 조건을 어긴다. D는 두 감정이 동시에 나타나지만 Tammy가 아닌 어머니의 반응이므로 주장과 무관하다.
problem.explanationEn: The critic claims that Tammy feels amusement and sorrow at the same moment, with each feeling sharpening the other. Choice A shows Tammy holding back a laugh at the very instant her throat tightens as she watches her father, so it covers both feelings and the fact that they happen together. That makes A the most direct support. Choice B includes only amusement, so it actually suggests her reaction settles into one feeling. Choice C includes both feelings, but they are separated by years, which breaks the "same moment" condition. Choice D shows both feelings at once, but in Tammy's mother, not in Tammy.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In a 1970s Appalachian mining town, nine-year-old Tammy notices miners stuffing pockets with coal to sell illegally, the adults' hushed desperation striking her as both ridiculous and heartbreaking.

hardJudge.note: 정답 A가 비평가 주장의 세 요소(두 감정, 동일 순간, Tammy 본인)를 모두 충족함을 직접 검산. C(두 감정이나 시간 분리)와 D(동시성이나 주체가 어머니)는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교가 필요하며, B도 그럴듯한 오답. 지문은 2019 소설이라 하나 실존 작품 식별 불가, 저작권 의심 없음. 해설 한·영 일치, 영어 자연스러움.

advisory.note: A만 Tammy 본인·동시성·두 감정을 모두 충족한다. C(시간 분리)와 D(다른 인물)는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가진 매력적 오답이고, B는 감정이 하나뿐이라 배제된다. 다만 '서로를 날카롭게 한다'는 상호 강화 요소는 A에서 암시만 될 뿐 명시되지 않는다. 출처 소설은 가상의 것으로 보이며 실제 작품 인용 흔적은 없다.

problem.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Greta, a widow who tends a small plot in a Berlin allotment garden, has just received a letter that her sister Liesel wrote in 1945. The letter was located decades later through Red Cross tracing records and has only now been delivered.

Greta read the letter twice on the bench beside the bean rows, then folded it along its old creases. Liesel had written that she was sorry, that she had taken the last of their mother's ration coupons and left without saying goodbye, that she hoped Greta could someday forgive her. A literary critic has argued that the story presents Greta's response not as a sudden act of pardon but as a slow reckoning in which she must first admit that her own long silence, rather than Liesel's theft alone, kept the sisters apart.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's claim?

Greta read the letter twice on the bench beside the bean rows, then folded it along its old creases. Liesel had written that she was sorry, that she had taken the last of their mother's ration coupons and left without saying goodbye, that she hoped Greta could someday forgive her. A literary critic has argued that the story presents Greta's response not as a sudden act of pardon but as a slow reckoning in which she must first admit that her own long silence, rather than Liesel's theft alone, kept the sisters apart.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's claim?
options: Later in the story, Greta pins the letter to the wall of her garden shed and tells a neighbor that Liesel's apology came too late to matter, since the theft of the coupons was unforgivable.
Later in the story, Greta finds a 1952 address for Liesel in her own old diary and recalls that she once chose not to write, before she slowly begins a reply that starts with an apology of her own.
Later in the story, Greta immediately writes back that she forgives Liesel completely, explaining that the hardships of 1945 excused whatever either sister had done.
Later in the story, Greta learns from the Red Cross that Liesel had tried to send several other letters after 1945, all of which were lost in transit before reaching Berlin.
problem.explanation: 비평가의 주장은 두 가지다: 용서가 즉각적이지 않고 점진적이라는 점, 그리고 그레타가 자신의 침묵도 단절의 원인이었음을 인정한다는 점이다. B는 그레타가 언니의 주소를 알고도 편지하지 않았던 사실을 떠올리고, 천천히 자기 사과로 답장을 시작하므로 두 요소를 모두 충족한다. A는 그레타가 리젤의 절도만 탓하고 자기 책임을 인정하지 않으므로 주장과 어긋난다. C는 용서가 즉각적이어서 '느린 성찰'과 모순된다. D는 침묵의 책임을 리젤 쪽의 분실된 편지로 돌릴 뿐 그레타 자신의 침묵 인정과는 무관하다.
problem.explanationEn: The critic's claim has two parts: Greta's forgiveness is gradual rather than sudden, and she must admit that her own silence helped keep the sisters apart. B satisfies both, since Greta remembers that she had Liesel's address and chose not to write, and then slowly starts a reply that opens with her own apology. A doesn't work because Greta blames only the theft and accepts no responsibility herself. C contradicts the "slow reckoning" part of the claim, since her pardon comes immediately. D explains the silence through Liesel's lost letters, so it says nothing about Greta admitting her own part.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In a Berlin allotment garden, widow Greta receives a letter from her sister written in 1945 and finally delivered through Red Cross traces, demanding forgiveness across decades of silence.

hardJudge.note: 비평가 주장의 두 요소(점진적 용서 + 자기 침묵 인정)를 B만 동시에 충족함을 직접 검산. C는 용서는 하나 '즉각적'이라 배제, D는 침묵 원인을 리젤 쪽으로 돌려 배제, A는 용서 자체를 부정하여 배제. 두 조건 결합 판단이 필요하고 오답 중 C·D가 부분 근거를 가져 medium에 적합. 한·영 해설 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 B는 '1952 주소, 쓰지 않기로 선택, 천천히, 자기 사과'로 비평가 주장의 두 요소를 모두 명시적으로 짚어 줘서 훑어 읽어도 바로 고를 수 있다. A와 C는 주장과 정면으로 어긋나 쉽게 걸러진다. 부분적 근거로 그럴듯해 보이는 오답은 D 하나뿐이다(침묵을 다루지만 리젤 쪽 문제다). 'medium' 기준인 부분적으로 맞는 오답 2개를 충족하지 못한다.

problem.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Kariuki, a street vendor, rides the same matatu (minibus) each morning as Benson, a motorcycle taxi driver whose bike is being repaired.

At every stop, while the conductor shouted for passengers, Kariuki opened his tin of glass beads on his knee. "Red for the blood of the people," he murmured, threading. "White for peace." Benson watched, then held out his hand. On the first day he had said he only wanted to make bracelets to sell to tourists at the Kenyatta Avenue lights, where riders waited with nothing to do. Kariuki had shrugged and given him a needle anyway. Now, by the third week, Benson's fingers moved more slowly than before, and he no longer counted aloud how many shillings each strand might bring.

A student argues that the story presents Benson's interest in beadwork as gradually changing from a way to earn money into a way of connecting with a heritage he had lost touch with.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the student's argument?

The following text is adapted from a short story. Rashid, an aging dyer at a riverside tannery in Fez, is teaching his grandson Karim, who will soon leave for university in Rabat.

Rashid lowered the hide into the vat of saffron dye and held it there, counting under his breath. Karim watched from the edge of the stone basin, arms folded. "You could write the times down for me," Karim said. Rashid did not answer. He lifted the hide, turned it so the light fell across its grain, and placed Karim's hand flat against the wet leather. "Feel where it drinks," he said. Karim pulled his hand back, then, after a moment, set it down again and left it there longer than he needed to.

A literary critic argues that, in this scene, Karim's reluctance is beginning to give way to an unspoken acceptance of what his grandfather is trying to pass on to him.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's interpretation?

problem.explanation: 목표는 곤살루의 일상을 깨뜨린 사건을 설명하는 것이다. A는 갑작스러운 폭풍이 전차 객차를 물에 잠기게 한 사건을 제시하므로 목표에 맞는다. B는 깨지기 전의 평소 일상만 설명할 뿐 그 일상을 깨뜨린 사건은 언급하지 않는다. C는 작가가 노선을 정한 배경이라 이야기 속 사건이 아니다. D는 출판 정보와 주인공만 소개하고 사건은 빠져 있다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to describe the event that breaks Gonçalo's usual routine. A does this by naming the sudden storm that floods his tram carriage. B only describes the routine itself, not what disrupts it. C gives background on how the author chose the route, which isn't an event in the story. D just gives publication details and names the main character, without any event.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On a lurching Lisbon tram line, commuter Gonçalo watches his daily routine shatter when a sudden summer storm floods the carriage, forcing strangers into unexpected vulnerability.

hardJudge.note: 정답 A 검산 완료: 목표(일상을 깨는 사건 서술)에 맞는 유일한 선택지. B는 평소 일상만, C는 작가 배경, D는 출판 정보로 사건이 빠져 있어 규칙을 알면 즉시 배제되지만 모두 노트에 근거한 그럴듯한 오답임. 한·영 해설 모두 정답과 글자 참조가 일치하며 모순 없음. 작가·작품은 가상으로 보이며 저작권 문제 없음. 단일 규칙·일단계 추론으로 easy 난이도에 적합.

advisory.note: 목표(일상을 깨는 사건)를 충족하는 선택지는 A뿐이다. 오답은 평소 일상(B), 작가 배경(C), 출판 정보(D)라는 전형적인 함정이다. 사소한 점: D의 문장이 다소 어색하다("In 'The Number 28,' ... Gonçalo is the main character of a short story"). 다만 판정에는 영향이 없다.

In "The Third Cup," Tigist roasts the beans, grinds them by hand, and pours the coffee into small cups for her guests.
In "The Third Cup," Tigist's guests sense that she is about to leave home, though no one says so aloud.
In "The Third Cup," Tigist lives in a village in the Ethiopian highlands, the setting chosen by an Ethiopian writer.
problem.explanation: 목표는 의식 중 Tigist가 하는 행동을 설명하는 것이다. B는 원두를 볶고, 손으로 갈고, 컵에 따르는 그녀의 구체적 행동을 메모 그대로 제시하므로 정답이다. A는 폭풍이라는 배경 사건을 말할 뿐 그녀의 의식 행동이 아니다. C는 손님들의 느낌에 초점을 두고, D는 배경과 작가 정보만 담아 목표와 무관하다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to describe what Tigist actually does during the coffee ceremony. B lists her concrete actions from the notes: roasting the beans, grinding them by hand, and pouring the coffee for her guests, so it is correct. A describes the storm, which is something happening around her, not what she does in the ritual. C focuses on what the guests feel, and D only gives the setting and the author, so neither one meets the goal.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — At her family's Ethiopian highland coffee ceremony, Tigist prepares the ritual brew while an unexpected storm darkens the sky, each guest sensing something unspoken about her imminent departure.

hardJudge.note: B는 메모의 '볶고, 갈고, 따른다'는 의식 중 행동을 그대로 담아 목표를 충족한다. A는 Tigist의 행동(watches)이지만 의식 행동이 아닌 배경 사건, C는 손님의 감지, D는 배경·작가 정보로 모두 전형적 오개념형 오답이다. 한국어·영어 해설 결론 및 글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 가상의 작품으로 저작권 문제 없음. 단일 규칙(목표 일치)으로 한 단계 추론, easy 적합.

advisory.note: B만이 의식 중 Tigist의 행동(볶기, 손으로 갈기, 따르기)을 담고 있다. 오답들은 폭풍·손님의 감정·배경으로 그럴듯하게 주의를 돌리는 전형적 선택지다. 사소한 점: A의 'Tigist watches'는 메모에 없는 내용이지만 오답이므로 문제되지 않는다. 가상의 작품으로 보인다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
The school boat bumped against the bamboo pier, and Teacher Rosario climbed out with her satchel held above the spray. On the schoolhouse steps lay a carabao calf, legs folded, chewing as if it had been hired to guard the door. She clapped; it blinked. She pushed; it sighed. By then the children had arrived and were watching her closely. Rosario looked at the workbook in her satchel, printed in Manila, its first lesson about measuring snowfall. Then she sat down beside the calf. "Who can tell me," she asked, "how many steps this animal is blocking, and how much it weighs compared to all of you?"

Text 2
Readers often celebrate the carabao scene as proof of Rosario's sudden, playful inventiveness, as though the calf alone sparks her new approach. But the story has already shown us her doubts about lessons written far from the island. The calf does not create her impulse to teach from the world around her; it simply gives her an excuse she has been waiting for to act on it.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely interpret Rosario's decision to sit beside the calf and begin questioning the children in Text 1?

On the schoolhouse steps lay a carabao calf, legs folded, chewing as if it had been hired to guard the door. She clapped; it blinked. She pushed; it sighed. But the story has already shown us her doubts about lessons written far from the island. problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely interpret Rosario's decision to sit beside the calf and begin questioning the children in Text 1?
options: As a sign that she has lost control of the classroom and is giving in to the children's excitement
As an example of spontaneous creativity that comes about only because of the calf's unexpected arrival
As a moment when she takes up a welcome opportunity to drop lessons she had already found poorly suited to the island
As a reluctant compromise she makes only after her efforts to move the calf have failed
problem.explanation: Text 2의 저자는 송아지가 Rosario의 충동을 '만들어 낸' 것이 아니라, 섬과 맞지 않는 교재에 대해 이미 품고 있던 의심을 실행할 '핑계'를 주었을 뿐이라고 본다. Text 1에서 눈 내린 양을 재는 마닐라 교재를 바라보는 장면이 이 해석을 뒷받침하므로 정답은 C이다. B는 Text 2가 명시적으로 반박하는 통념(송아지만이 계기)이다. D는 Text 1에서 송아지를 밀어내지 못한 점과는 맞지만, '마지못한' 타협이라는 해석은 반가운 기회라는 Text 2의 시각과 반대이다. A는 Text 2 어디에도 통제력 상실이라는 판단이 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The author of Text 2 argues that the calf doesn't create Rosario's urge to teach from her surroundings. Instead, it just gives her the excuse she has been waiting for to act on doubts she already had about lessons written far from the island. In Text 1, she looks at the Manila workbook with its snowfall lesson right before she sits down, which supports this reading, so C is correct. B states the popular view that Text 2 explicitly rejects, the idea that the calf alone sparks her approach. D fits the detail that Rosario couldn't move the calf, but calling her choice "reluctant" contradicts Text 2's view that she welcomes the chance. A doesn't work because Text 2 never suggests that Rosario has lost control of her class.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Teacher Rosario arrives by school boat to her isolated Philippine island classroom only to discover a stray carabao calf has claimed the schoolhouse steps, disrupting everything.

hardJudge.note: Text 2의 핵심 주장("송아지는 충동을 만들지 않고, 기다려 온 핑계를 줄 뿐")과 Text 1의 마닐라 교재(눈 측정 단원) 응시 장면을 연결하면 C가 명확히 도출됨. B는 Text 2가 명시적으로 반박하는 통념, D는 Text 1의 '밀어도 안 움직임' 세부와 부분 일치하나 '마지못한'이 "waiting for"와 충돌, A는 근거 없음 — 오답 구성이 medium 기준에 부합. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답 및 선택지 글자 참조가 일치하고 모순 없음. 영어 해설은 자연스럽고 한글 미포함. 지문은 창작물로 저작권 우려 없음.

advisory.note: C는 Text 2의 'excuse she has been waiting for'와 'doubts about lessons written far from the island'를 바꿔 말한 것이다. B(통념)와 D(송아지를 밀어내지 못한 장면)는 부분적으로 근거가 있어 그럴듯하게 비교된다. A는 다소 약하지만 말이 되는 오답이다. 중간 난이도에 맞다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
In the following excerpt from a novel, Masako, the daughter of a fisherman in an Edo-period coastal village, practices net-weaving. A marriage to a merchant in the castle town has already been arranged for her, though her father does not know she has accepted it.
Her father guided her fingers through the knot again, his calloused thumb pressing hers against the twine. "Tighter," he said. "A loose knot lets the whole catch slip away." Masako pulled until the cord bit her skin. She told herself she was learning only to please him, that the skill would be useless behind a merchant's counter. Yet when the finished row lay taut and even across her lap, she found she could not stop looking at it.

Text 2
A literary critic comments on the novel.
Some readers take Masako's net-weaving scenes as proof that she secretly wants to stay in the village, as if the novel were quietly arguing against her marriage. This reading overlooks how firmly the author keeps Masako's choice intact: she never wavers in her plan to leave. What the weaving scenes reveal is not a hidden wish to remain but the cost of departure—Masako can value what her father gives her and still give it up. The novel's tension lies in that coexistence, not in any reversal.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to Masako's reaction to the finished row of netting in Text 1?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
In the following excerpt from a novel, Masako, the daughter of a fisherman in an Edo-period coastal village, practices net-weaving. A marriage to a merchant in the castle town has already been arranged for her, though her father does not know she has accepted it.
Her father guided her fingers through the knot again, his calloused thumb pressing hers against the twine. "Tighter," he said. "A loose knot lets the whole catch slip away." Masako pulled until the cord bit her skin. She told herself she was learning only to please him, that the skill would be useless behind a merchant's counter. Yet when the finished row lay taut and even across her lap, she found she could not stop looking at it.

Text 2
A literary critic comments on the novel.
Some readers take Masako's net-weaving scenes as proof that she secretly wants to stay in the village, as if the novel were quietly arguing against her marriage. This reading overlooks how firmly the author keeps Masako's choice intact: she never wavers in her plan to leave. problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to Masako's reaction to the finished row of netting in Text 1?
options: By claiming that it shows Masako has begun to doubt the arranged marriage and will likely remain in the village
By claiming that it shows Masako's pride is directed mainly at earning her father's approval rather than at the net itself
By claiming that it shows Masako's dismissal of the skill as useless is an accurate judgment the novel endorses
By claiming that it shows Masako's attachment to the craft can exist alongside her firm decision to leave it
problem.explanation: Text 2의 비평가는 그물 짜기 장면이 마을에 남고 싶다는 숨은 욕망이 아니라, 아버지가 준 것을 소중히 여기면서도 떠나기로 한 결정은 흔들리지 않는다는 '공존'을 보여준다고 말한다. 따라서 완성된 그물에서 눈을 떼지 못하는 Masako의 반응을 결심과 애착이 함께 있는 것으로 볼 것이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 Text 2가 명시적으로 반박하는 해석(마음이 흔들려 남을 것이라는 해석)이다. B는 Text 1에서 Masako가 스스로 하는 말("only to please him")과 맞닿아 있지만, 그녀가 그물 자체를 바라본다는 점과 비평가의 초점을 놓친다. C는 그 기술이 쓸모없다는 Masako의 말을 그대로 받아들이지만, 비평가는 그녀가 그 기술을 소중히 여긴다고 강조한다.
problem.explanationEn: The critic in Text 2 argues that the weaving scenes don't reveal a hidden wish to stay. Instead, they show that Masako can value what her father teaches her while her decision to leave stays firm. So the critic would read her inability to stop looking at the finished row as attachment existing alongside that decision, which makes D the answer. A is the very reading Text 2 rejects, since the critic says Masako never wavers. B echoes Masako's own claim that she is learning "only to please him," but it misses that she is looking at the net itself, and it ignores the critic's point about value and loss existing together. C takes Masako's dismissal of the skill as useless at face value, but the critic stresses that she truly values the craft.

hardJudge.note: Text 1 reaction("could not stop looking at it") + Text 2 claim(value and still give it up; coexistence, not reversal) → D 정확. A는 Text 2가 명시적으로 반박하는 독법, B는 Text 1의 "only to please him"과 부분 일치하나 그물 자체에 대한 시선과 비평가 초점 불일치, C는 "useless" 발언에 근거하나 비평가는 가치 부여 강조. 두 텍스트 연결 및 오답 비교 요구로 medium 적합. 한·영 해설 모두 동일 결론·글자 참조, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 원문 창작으로 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 D는 Text 2에 나오는 '공존' 논지와 바로 맞아떨어진다. A는 Text 2가 명시적으로 반박하는 해석이다. B와 C는 Text 1에서 Masako가 스스로 하는 말에 기대고 있어 그럴듯한 오답으로 기능한다. 중간 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Karim lifted his hides from the vat, and the indigo ran off them like evening sky. Hassan barely looked. "Your blue is muddy again," he said. "I enter this contest only because someone must stop you from boasting. If the guild cancelled it tomorrow, I would sleep until noon and thank God." Karim laughed and called him a liar. Hassan spat into the river and began stirring his own vat harder than he needed to.

Text 2
In the riverside tannery scenes of the novel, the two old dyers almost never say anything kind to each other. A careless reader might take their constant complaints at face value. But the novelist keeps showing gestures that contradict the men's words: a vat stirred too fiercely, a glance held a moment too long. For these men, insults are how they express a bond that age will soon end and that neither can bring himself to name.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely interpret Hassan's statement that he would happily see the contest cancelled?

problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely interpret Hassan's statement that he would happily see the contest cancelled?
options: As a sincere admission that years of competing have left him tired and eager to retire
As a remark that hides how much the yearly contest means to him, as his action at the vat suggests
As a remark meant mainly to upset Karim before the judges examine the two men's hides
As evidence that Hassan, unlike Karim, has already come to terms with the end of their rivalry

A는 Text 2가 경고한 '액면 그대로의' 해석이다. C는 경쟁 상황에서는 그럴듯하지만, Text 2는 모욕을 상대를 흔드는 전술이 아니라 유대의 표현으로 본다. D는 Text 2가 두 사람 모두 끝을 입에 올리지 못한다고 말한 것과 반대된다.
problem.explanationEn: The author of Text 2 warns against taking the dyers' complaints at face value and points to gestures, like stirring a vat too fiercely, that contradict what they say. So Hassan's claim that he'd be glad to see the contest cancelled would be read as hiding how much the contest matters to him, and his hard stirring in Text 1 backs this up. That makes B correct. A is exactly the face-value reading Text 2 rejects. C sounds plausible in a competition, but Text 2 sees the insults as a way of expressing a bond, not as a tactic to rattle an opponent. D contradicts Text 2's point that neither man can bring himself to name the coming end.

A는 액면 해석, C는 Text 2의 '유대 표현' 틀과 어긋남, D는 '둘 다 끝을 입에 올리지 못한다'와 모순. 두 텍스트 연결이 필요하고 오답들이 부분적 근거를 가져 medium에 적합. 사소한 점: 정답 B의 'yearly'는 두 텍스트 어디에도 명시되지 않은 추가 정보이나 정답 판별에 영향은 없음. 해설 한·영 일치, 영어 자연스러움, 한글 혼입 없음.

advisory.note: Text 2의 렌즈(말과 몸짓의 모순)를 Text 1의 '통을 필요 이상 세게 젓기'에 연결하는 두 단계 추론. A는 액면 해석, C는 경쟁 맥락상 그럴듯함, D는 '끝'이라는 Text 2 어휘를 부분적으로 활용해 비교가 필요함. 다만 Text 2에 'a vat stirred too fiercely'가 Text 1과 거의 그대로 겹쳐 단서가 다소 노골적이므로 medium 하단에 가까움.

problem.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Every morning before dawn, Hoa arranges her pho ingredients along the counter of her Hanoi stall in the same order: star anise, charred ginger, sliced shallots, then the herbs, always left to right. Regular customers joke that they could set their watches by her ladle. But this morning a monsoon arrives without warning, and water surges through the alley, sweeping her bowls of herbs into the gutter and knocking the shallots to the floor. Hoa stands motionless for a long moment. Then, instead of trying to rebuild her row, she pulls whatever is still within reach into the broth: a handful of rescued ginger, the anise, a few muddy scallions she rinses quickly in rainwater. Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: The following text is adapted from a short story. Every morning before dawn, Hoa arranges her pho ingredients along the counter of her Hanoi stall in the same order: star anise, charred ginger, sliced shallots, then the herbs, always left to right. But this morning a monsoon arrives without warning, and water surges through the alley, sweeping her bowls of herbs into the gutter and knocking the shallots to the floor. Then, instead of trying to rebuild her row, she pulls whatever is still within reach into the broth: a handful of rescued ginger, the anise, a few muddy scallions she rinses quickly in rainwater. When the first soaked customer ducks under her awning and asks whether she is open, she ladles him a bowl without apology. The detail suggests that Hoa's careful ordering of ingredients ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: was something her regular customers depended on more than the flavor of the soup itself.
had always made her stall unprepared for the sudden weather of the monsoon season.
was a habit she could set aside when circumstances required, rather than a condition for serving her customers.
was a source of pride that the flood permanently destroyed, leaving her unwilling to cook.
problem.explanation: 홍수 전 Hoa는 매일 같은 순서로 재료를 배열하지만, 홍수 후에는 그 줄을 다시 세우지 않고 손에 닿는 재료로 국물을 만들어 사과 없이 손님에게 대접한다. 이 두 정보를 연결하면 정돈된 순서는 장사의 필수 조건이 아니라 상황에 따라 내려놓을 수 있는 습관이었다는 C가 정답이다. A는 단골들이 그녀의 규칙성에 대해 농담한다는 점에 근거하지만, 맛보다 순서에 더 의존했다는 내용은 지문에 없다. B는 폭우가 예고 없이 왔다는 점에 기대지만, 재료 배열 습관이 대비 부족의 원인이라는 근거는 없다. D는 그녀가 잠시 멈춰 섰다는 점에서 출발하지만, 결국 요리해 손님에게 내주므로 지문과 모순된다.
problem.explanationEn: Before the flood, Hoa lays out her ingredients in the same order every day. After the flood, though, she doesn't rebuild that row. She cooks with whatever she can reach and serves her customer without apologizing. Putting those two facts together shows that the ordering was a habit she could drop when she had to, not something she needed in order to serve food, so C is correct. A builds on the regulars joking about her routine, but nothing in the text says they cared about the order more than the flavor. B builds on the storm arriving without warning, but the text never says her arranging habit left her unprepared. D builds on the moment she stands still, but it contradicts the passage, since she goes on to cook and serve.

A(맛보다 순서 의존)·B(대비 부족 원인)는 근거 없음, D는 '요리해 대접함'과 직접 모순. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 결론과 선택지 참조가 일치하고 자연스러움. 사소한 지적: 지문 끝 "The detail suggests"는 어떤 detail인지 선행어가 불명확해 표준 SAT 문구("which suggests that")보다 어색하며, 'scallions'가 앞서 언급된 shallots/herbs와 달리 새로 등장하는 점도 약간 거슬림. 또 정답 C가 가장 길고 'rather than' 구조로 단독 돌출되어 길이 단서가 될 소지가 있음. 그래도 두 정보 연결이 필요하고 A·B가 부분 근거를 가지므로 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 정답 C는 홍수 전 습관과 홍수 후 즉흥 조리·무사과 서빙을 연결해야 도출되며, 2단계 추론에 해당한다. 오답 A·B·D는 각각 지문의 단서(단골 농담, 예고 없는 폭우, 잠시 멈춤)에 기대고 있다. 다만 D는 명백히 모순되고 C가 다른 선택지보다 눈에 띄게 길고 구체적이어서, medium 중에서도 쉬운 쪽에 가깝다. 'The detail suggests'의 'detail'이 무엇을 가리키는지 다소 모호하지만 허용 범위다.

The column, it seemed, was not really meant to be solved; rather, by filling the board, Mr. Adebayo was ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: testing which pupils could work quickly enough to finish the sums before the bell rang.
punishing the restless pupils for paying more attention to the market than to the lesson.
using up the last of the school's chalk so that the next teacher would have to request more.
stretching out the final lesson he would ever teach, unwilling to let it come to an end.
problem.explanation: 지문은 이것이 마지막 수업이고, 문제들이 '실제로 풀라고 낸 것이 아니다'라고 말한다. 따라서 칠판을 채우는 행동은 끝나가는 수업을 붙잡아 두려는 작별의 몸짓으로 보는 것이 가장 자연스러우며, 정답은 D이다. A는 제시간에 끝낼 수 없다는 지적과 '풀라고 낸 것이 아니다'라는 서술에 어긋난다. B는 학생들이 산만하다는 점과 연결되지만, 그가 평소와 달리 꾸짖지 않았다는 내용과 모순된다. C는 분필이 닳았다는 세부 사항만 붙잡았을 뿐 그런 의도를 뒷받침하는 근거가 지문에 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The text tells you this is Mr. Adebayo's last lesson and that the sums were "not really meant to be solved." So filling the board is best read as a farewell gesture, a way of holding on to a lesson that is about to end. That makes D the answer. A doesn't fit, because the sums can't be finished in time and the text says they weren't meant to be solved. B links to the restless pupils, but it conflicts with the detail that he didn't scold them this time. C picks up on the crumbling chalk, but nothing in the text suggests he wanted to use up the supply.

hardJudge.note: 정답 D 검산 완료: '마지막 수업' + '풀라고 낸 것이 아니다'라는 두 단서를 연결해야 하며, A(제시간 완료 불가), B(꾸짖지 않음), C(근거 없음)는 각각 지문 세부와 충돌하거나 뒷받침되지 않음. 한·영 해설 결론과 글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 오답 B·A가 부분적 근거를 가져 비교가 필요하고 C도 말이 되므로 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 문맥상 D가 정답이다. 마지막 수업이라는 설정, 풀라고 낸 문제가 아니라는 서술, 평소와 달리 꾸짖지 않은 점이 함께 D를 뒷받침한다. A와 B는 지문 세부 사항(제시간에 끝낼 수 없다는 지적, 학생들이 산만함)에 겉으로는 기대고 있지만 직접 반박되므로, 두 정보를 연결해야 배제할 수 있다. C는 근거가 약해 매력도가 낮다. 전체적으로 medium 수준에 맞다.
