problem.stimulus:
The following text is adapted from a short story set in Lagos in the 1920s.

For eleven years after Adebayo's death, Oluwatoyin had kept the boy's copybook in a drawer and never once opened it. When the young clerk at his door introduced himself as Adebayo's cousin and asked, shyly, whether the old teacher might help him prepare for the civil service examination, Oluwatoyin's first impulse was to refuse; he had sworn off pupils since that fever season. Yet that evening he cleared the dining table, set out two lamps, and, after a long hesitation, took the copybook from the drawer and laid it open beside the clerk's papers. His actions suggest that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: he has begun to let his grief over Adebayo become a part of his renewed teaching rather than a reason to avoid it.
he has decided that the clerk is a more capable student than Adebayo was and needs no extra guidance.
he intends to use Adebayo's copybook to show the clerk exactly which answers will appear on the examination.
he has finally put his sorrow behind him and no longer thinks about the student he lost.
problem.explanation: 오루와토인은 학생을 받지 않겠다고 맹세했지만 결국 수업을 준비한다. 게다가 11년 동안 열어 보지 않던 아데바요의 공책을 꺼내 사촌의 공부 자료 옆에 펼쳐 놓는다. 이 행동은 슬픔을 피하지 않고 새 가르침 속으로 받아들이고 있음을 보여 주므로 A가 정답이다. D는 그의 변화를 포착했지만, 공책을 펼친 것은 아데바요를 의식적으로 기억하는 행동이므로 '더 이상 생각하지 않는다'는 진술과 모순된다. B의 능력 비교와 C의 시험 답 유출은 지문에 근거가 없다.
problem.explanationEn: Oluwatoyin had sworn off teaching, but he still prepares a lesson. He also takes out Adebayo's copybook, which he hasn't opened in eleven years, and lays it open beside the cousin's papers. These actions show that he is bringing his grief into his teaching instead of avoiding it, so A is correct. D notices that he has changed, but opening the copybook is a deliberate act of remembering Adebayo, so it contradicts the claim that he no longer thinks about the boy. Nothing in the text supports B's comparison of the two students' abilities or C's idea that he is leaking exam answers.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In 1920s Lagos, retired teacher Oluwatoyin receives an unexpected visitor who reminds him of a former student lost to illness, reigniting both sorrow and unexpected grace.

hardJudge.note: 정답 A는 '학생을 받지 않겠다고 맹세'→'수업 준비', '11년간 열지 않은 공책'→'펼쳐 놓음'의 두 정보를 연결해야 도출되며, D는 변화를 포착한 부분적 근거가 있어 비교가 필요하다. 다만 B·C는 지문과의 연결이 약해 비교적 쉽게 배제되므로 오답 2개 이상이 부분 근거를 갖는다는 기준은 다소 느슨하게 충족된다(C는 '공책을 시험 대비에 활용'이라는 표면적 연결만 있음). 해설(한·영)은 결론·선택지 참조가 일치하고 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 창작 지문으로 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 A는 맞다. 맹세를 깨고 수업을 준비한 것과 공책을 펼친 것을 연결하면 A가 나온다. 하지만 부분 근거가 있는 오답은 D 하나뿐이다. D는 변화는 포착했지만 공책을 펼친 행동과 모순된다. B(능력 비교, 지도 불필요)와 C(시험 답 유출)는 지문과 거의 무관하고, B는 테이블을 정리한 행동과도 어긋나서 바로 배제된다. 오답 중 최소 2개는 비교해 봐야 배제되어야 한다는 medium 기준에 못 미친다.

problem.passage:
Every dawn at the small port of Húsavík, the harbor master carried a tin of fish scraps behind the ice house and set it down for the cats that departing sailors had left behind. The adults of the town described him as gruff and perfectly content with his solitude ______ who watched him crouch among the cats without saying a word, had already understood that the old man was lonely.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Every dawn at the small port of Húsavík, the harbor master carried a tin of fish scraps behind the ice house and set it down for the cats that departing sailors had left behind. The adults of the town described him as gruff and perfectly content with his solitude ______ who watched him crouch among the cats without saying a word, had already understood that the old man was lonely.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , so five-year-old Björn,
, five-year-old Björn,
, but five-year-old Björn;
, but five-year-old Björn,
problem.explanation:
이 문장은 독립절 두 개로 되어 있다. 하나는 "The adults ... described him as gruff and ... content with his solitude"이고, 다른 하나는 "five-year-old Björn ... had already understood that the old man was lonely"이다. 두 번째 절의 주어 Björn과 동사 had understood 사이에는 비제한적 관계절 "who watched him ... word"가 끼어 있다. 어른들의 판단(고독에 만족함)과 Björn의 이해(외로워함)가 서로 반대되므로 두 절은 대조 관계이다. 정답 D는 쉼표와 대조 접속사 but으로 두 절을 잇고, Björn 뒤의 쉼표로 삽입절을 연다. 이 쉼표는 word 뒤의 쉼표와 짝을 이룬다.
A: '쉼표+등위접속사'라는 구두점 방식은 맞다. 하지만 so는 인과 관계를 나타낸다. 어른들이 그를 만족한 사람으로 봤기 때문에 Björn이 외로움을 알아챘다는 논리는 성립하지 않으므로 의미가 맞지 않는다.
B: 접속사 없이 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이은 콤마 스플라이스이다.
C: 세미콜론이 절 경계가 아니라 주어 Björn과 그를 꾸미는 관계절 사이에 들어가 있다. 그 결과 세미콜론 뒤의 "who watched ... lonely"는 독립절이 될 수 없다. 또한 word 뒤의 쉼표와 짝을 이루지도 못한다.
problem.explanationEn:
This sentence is made of two independent clauses. The first is "The adults ... described him as gruff and ... content with his solitude." The second is "five-year-old Björn ... had already understood that the old man was lonely." In the second clause, the subject (Björn) is separated from its verb (had understood) by the nonrestrictive clause "who watched him ... word." The adults believe he is content alone, while Björn understands that he is lonely, so the two clauses contrast. Choice D joins the clauses with a comma plus the contrasting conjunction "but." Its comma after "Björn" opens the inserted clause, and the comma after "word" closes it.
A: Using a comma plus a coordinating conjunction is the right strategy, but "so" signals cause and effect. The adults' view did not cause Björn's insight, so the logic doesn't work.
B: Joining two independent clauses with only a comma creates a comma splice.
C: The semicolon is not at the boundary between the clauses. It falls between "Björn" and the relative clause that describes him, which leaves "who watched ... lonely" as a fragment that isn't an independent clause. It also fails to pair with the comma after "word."

hardJudge.note: 두 독립절("The adults ... described him as ... content with his solitude" / "five-year-old Björn ... had already understood ...")이 명확하고, 어른들의 판단과 Björn의 이해가 정반대이므로 대조 관계가 분명함. D(쉼표+but, 이후 Björn 뒤 쉼표로 비제한 관계절 개시, word 뒤 쉼표와 짝)가 유일한 정답으로 검산됨. B는 콤마 스플라이스, C는 주어와 관계절 사이에 세미콜론이 놓여 절 경계가 아닌 위치임. A는 구두점은 적법하나 so의 인과 의미가 문맥과 불일치. 해설은 정답을 정확히 뒷받침하며 모순 없음. 참고: A는 문법적으로는 허용 가능한 형태이므로 실제 SAT 경계 문항 기준으로는 의미 판단에 의존하는 오답이라는 점을 유의(레시피 요구사항에는 부합). 주어와 동사 사이 삽입 관계절을 절 경계와 구분하고, 절 간 논리관계로 접속사를 선택해야 하므로 medium을 넘는 사고 요구.

advisory.note: 대조 관계(but vs so)와 삽입 관계절의 짝 쉼표를 함께 판단해야 해서 medium보다 사고 단계가 하나 더 있다.

problem.passage:
On the rooftop above Shubra, Rashad scraped dried seed from the bottom of the old ceramic bowl his pigeons had eaten from for as long as he could remember. He had always assumed it was a cheap market purchase. The faded script pressed into its cracked underside ______ spelled out the name of his grandfather Mahmoud, a man who had stopped speaking to the family long before Rashad was born, along with a date: 1961.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: On the rooftop above Shubra, Rashad scraped dried seed from the bottom of the old ceramic bowl his pigeons had eaten from for as long as he could remember. He had always assumed it was a cheap market purchase. The faded script pressed into its cracked underside ______ spelled out the name of his grandfather Mahmoud, a man who had stopped speaking to the family long before Rashad was born, along with a date: 1961.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , in fact,
; in fact,
. In fact,
, in fact
problem.explanation:
정답 A. 빈칸 앞 'The faded script pressed into its cracked underside'는 주어(+수식어구)일 뿐 동사가 없고, 빈칸 뒤 'spelled out ...'는 주어가 없는 서술부다. 즉 두 독립절의 경계가 아니라 한 절의 주어와 동사 사이에 'in fact'가 삽입된 구조이므로, 삽입어 앞뒤에 쉼표를 하나씩 찍어야 한다.
B: 세미콜론은 두 독립절을 이을 때 쓰는데, 앞부분에 동사가 없어서 독립절이 아니다. 'in fact'를 절의 경계로 잘못 본 오답이다.
C: 마침표를 찍으면 앞부분이 동사 없는 조각문이 되고, 뒷부분도 주어 없는 조각문이 된다. B와 같은 오개념에서 나온 오답이다.
D: 쉼표가 삽입어 앞에만 있고 뒤에는 없어서 비대칭이다. 그 결과 쉼표 하나가 주어와 동사 사이를 부적절하게 끊는다.
problem.explanationEn:
The answer is A. Look at what comes before the blank: "The faded script pressed into its cracked underside." That is only a subject with a modifier. It has no main verb ("pressed into" is a participle that describes "script"). The part after the blank, "spelled out the name...", is a predicate with no subject. So the blank isn't a boundary between two independent clauses. "In fact" is an interrupter placed between the subject and its verb, so it needs a comma on both sides.
B is wrong because a semicolon has to join two independent clauses, and the first part isn't one. This choice treats "in fact" as if it marked a clause boundary.
C is wrong for the same reason. A period would leave a fragment with no verb before it and a fragment with no subject after it.
D is wrong because it puts only one comma around the interrupter. That lopsided comma ends up splitting the subject from its verb.

hardJudge.note: 정답 A 검산 확인: 빈칸 앞은 'The faded script [pressed into its cracked underside]'로 과거분사 축약관계절이 붙은 주어구이며 동사가 없고, 뒤 'spelled out …'는 주어 없는 서술부이므로 'in fact'는 주어-동사 사이 삽입어 → 양쪽 쉼표(A)가 유일한 정답. B·C는 독립절이 아닌 곳에 세미콜론/마침표를 찍어 조각문 생성, D는 비대칭 쉼표로 주어-동사를 끊음. 해설도 이와 정확히 일치. 체크리스트 4(콤마 스플라이스 오답)는 미충족: 설계상 빈칸 앞이 독립절이 아니므로 어떤 선택지도 콤마 스플라이스가 될 수 없고, 오답 B·C·D 중 콤마 스플라이스는 없다. 난이도는 'pressed'를 본동사로 오독하기 쉬운 garden-path 구조를 분사 수식으로 판별해야 하는 점에서 medium을 넘는 추가 사고를 요구하나, 삽입어 유형 중 가장 전형적 패턴에 가까워 hard로서는 다소 경계선.

advisory.note: 정답 A가 맞다. 주어가 길고, 'pressed'가 과거분사인데 동사처럼 읽혀서 앞부분을 독립절로 착각하게 만든다. 이 함정 덕분에 'in fact'가 절과 절 사이에 낀 것인지 단순 삽입어인지 가려내는 사고가 실제로 필요하다. 다만 체크리스트 4번(오답 중 콤마 스플라이스)은 충족하지 못했다. 이 문장에는 독립절 경계가 아예 없어서, 어떤 선택지도 콤마 스플라이스가 될 수 없다. B와 C는 조각문을 만드는 오답이다. 5번(쉼표 비대칭)은 D가 충족한다.

problem.passage:
Klaus arrived in the spring of 1946 carrying one cardboard suitcase and a letter from a parish priest in Linz. Ernst, who had been the first to open the door, watched the newcomer study the peeling wallpaper with obvious dismay. Having lived in the boarding house on Gumpendorfer Strasse since before the war, ______ which stair creaked loudly enough to wake the landlady and which tap ran only cold.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Klaus arrived in the spring of 1946 carrying one cardboard suitcase and a letter from a parish priest in Linz. Ernst, who had been the first to open the door, watched the newcomer study the peeling wallpaper with obvious dismay. Having lived in the boarding house on Gumpendorfer Strasse since before the war, ______ which stair creaked loudly enough to wake the landlady and which tap ran only cold.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the hallway's oldest radiator reminded Klaus
Ernst quietly warned Klaus
Ernst's handwritten list quietly warned Klaus
the boarding house itself quietly warned Klaus
problem.explanation: 정답 B. 분사구문 "Having lived in the boarding house ... since before the war"의 의미상 주어는 전쟁 전부터 하숙집에 살아온 사람, 즉 Ernst이다. 주절 주어가 Ernst이어야 수식이 맞다. A: 라디에이터는 수식어와 관계없는 엉뚱한 명사이고 '살아온' 주체가 될 수 없다. C: Ernst의 손글씨 목록은 Ernst와 비슷하지만 그의 결과물일 뿐 사람이 아니므로 하숙집에서 살 수 없다. D: 단수 동사 warned와 수는 맞지만, 하숙집 자체가 '그 하숙집에서 살아왔다'는 것은 의미상 불가능하다. 네 선택지 모두 문법적으로는 완전한 문장이 되므로 수식 관계만으로 판단해야 한다.
problem.explanationEn: The correct answer is B. The opening phrase "Having lived in the boarding house ... since before the war" describes a person who has lived there for years, and that person is Ernst. So the subject of the main clause must be Ernst. A: the radiator has nothing to do with the modifier, and it can't have "lived" anywhere. C: Ernst's list is connected to Ernst, but it's something he made, not a person, so it can't have lived in the boarding house. D: the singular subject agrees with the verb, but it makes no sense to say the boarding house has lived in the boarding house. All four choices are grammatical sentences, so you can only find the answer by checking what the opening phrase logically describes.

hardJudge.note: 문두 분사구문 "Having lived in the boarding house ... since before the war"의 의미상 주어는 전쟁 전부터 거주한 사람이어야 하며, 지문에서 문을 연 거주자로 설정된 Ernst(B)만 적합. A·C·D 모두 단수 주어+과거 동사로 수일치·시제로는 구별 불가하고, 각각 "warned/reminded Klaus which stair creaked..."로 이어져 문법적으로 완전한 문장을 이룸. 특히 C는 "Ernst's handwritten list"로 소유격 안에 Ernst를 넣어 핵심 명사(list)가 사람이 아님을 식별해야 하는 범주 함정으로 설계됨. 해설은 정답을 정확히 뒷받침하며 모순 없음. 독창적 서사로 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 분사구문의 의미상 주어는 Ernst이다. C(소유격 Ernst's + 저작물)는 사람 대 사물 범주를 이용한 함정이고, D와 A는 사물 주어이다. 선택지 모두 단수 과거형이라 수일치만으로는 정답을 가릴 수 없다. 앞 문장의 '처음 문을 연 사람이 Ernst'라는 단서 덕분에 문맥상 추론이 필요하다. 다만 구조 자체는 전형적인 dangling modifier 문항에 가깝다.

problem.passage:
Taiwo read the letter twice beneath the awning while the noon heat pressed down on Balogun Market. The solicitor's words were crisp and generous: the letter promised her a berth on a steamer bound for Liverpool and a room in her late uncle's London house______ it said nothing about who would sit each morning behind her mother's indigo stall, folding cloth the way her mother had always assumed Taiwo one day would.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Taiwo read the letter twice beneath the awning while the noon heat pressed down on Balogun Market. The solicitor's words were crisp and generous: the letter promised her a berth on a steamer bound for Liverpool and a room in her late uncle's London house______ it said nothing about who would sit each morning behind her mother's indigo stall, folding cloth the way her mother had always assumed Taiwo one day would.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , so it
, it
, but it
but; it
problem.explanation:
정답 C. 빈칸 앞 절(편지가 배편과 방을 약속함)과 뒤 절(어머니의 노점을 누가 지킬지는 언급하지 않음)은 둘 다 독립절이며, 너그러운 제안과 빠진 부분이 대조를 이룬다. 따라서 쉼표에 대조 접속사 but을 더한 ', but'이 알맞다.
A: 쉼표와 등위접속사 조합이라 구두점 형식은 맞지만, so는 인과를 나타낸다. 제안이 있었기 때문에 노점 이야기를 하지 않았다는 뜻이 되어 논리가 맞지 않는다.
B: 쉼표 하나로 두 독립절을 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 된다.
D: 세미콜론이 절 경계가 아니라 접속사 but 바로 뒤에 놓여 but이 앞 절에 어색하게 붙는다. 그래서 문장이 잘못 쪼개진다.
problem.explanationEn:
C is correct. Both sides of the blank are independent clauses. The first says the letter offers passage and a room, and the second says it ignores who will run her mother's stall. That generous offer set against what the letter leaves out is a contrast, so a comma plus the coordinating conjunction "but" is the right choice.
A uses the correct punctuation pattern (comma + coordinating conjunction), but "so" signals cause and effect. It wrongly suggests that the letter left out the stall because it made the offer.
B joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice.
D places the semicolon right after "but" instead of at the boundary between the clauses. This leaves the conjunction stranded at the end of the first clause and splits the sentence awkwardly.

hardJudge.note: 두 절 모두 독립절("the letter promised her a berth ... and a room ..." / "it said nothing about ..."), 관대한 제안과 누락된 부분의 대조가 문맥상 분명하여 ', but it'이 정답으로 성립. A는 so의 인과 논리가 어긋나는 오답, B는 콤마 스플라이스, D는 세미콜론이 접속사 뒤 비경계 위치에 놓인 오답으로 체크리스트 전 항목 충족. 앞 절이 콜론 뒤에 놓이고 복합 목적어(a berth ... and a room ...)로 길어져 절 경계 식별에 추가 분석이 필요하며, 구두점 형식이 동일한 A/C 사이에서 논리 관계(인과 vs 대조)로 결정해야 하므로 medium 수준을 넘는 사고를 요구함. 해설은 정답과 오답 근거를 모순 없이 뒷받침함. 독창적 서사 텍스트로 저작권 우려 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 C는 맞고 해설도 일관된다. 다만 전형적인 medium 수준의 절 경계 문항이다. 콤마 스플라이스(B)와 세미콜론 위치 오류(D)는 곧바로 소거된다. 실제로 판단할 것은 A(so)와 C(but) 중 어느 접속사가 맞는지뿐인데, 'generous ... said nothing'의 대조가 분명해서 쉽게 풀린다. 이 정도로는 여러 구두점 전략(세미콜론·마침표 등)을 비교해야 하는 hard 수준에 미치지 못한다. 난이도는 주로 긴 지문에서 온다.

problem.passage:
For thirty years, Amr and Samir had released their pigeons at dawn from neighboring rooftops in Shubra, watching the flocks circle above the minarets before settling back onto the wire coops. Now Amr's daughter, Nadia, insisted that he move with her to Alexandria after her wedding. The speckled birds that Amr had raised since boyhood ______ could not make the journey, and so, without saying anything, he began carrying their feed sacks across the low wall to Samir's roof.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: For thirty years, Amr and Samir had released their pigeons at dawn from neighboring rooftops in Shubra, watching the flocks circle above the minarets before settling back onto the wire coops. Now Amr's daughter, Nadia, insisted that he move with her to Alexandria after her wedding. The speckled birds that Amr had raised since boyhood ______ could not make the journey, and so, without saying anything, he began carrying their feed sacks across the low wall to Samir's roof.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: ; however,
, however;
however,
, however,
problem.explanation:
정답 D. 빈칸 앞 'The speckled birds that Amr had raised since boyhood'는 주어(명사구+관계절)일 뿐 완전한 절이 아니고, 빈칸 뒤 'could not make the journey'는 그 주어의 동사다. 따라서 however는 한 절 내부의 삽입어이므로 앞뒤 모두 쉼표로 감싸야 한다.
A: 세미콜론은 두 독립절 사이에 쓰는데, 앞부분은 동사가 없는 주어뿐이라 불완전하다. 삽입어를 절 경계로 착각한 오류다.
B: however 뒤에 세미콜론을 두면 'could not make the journey...'를 별개의 절처럼 다루게 되고, 주어와 동사가 끊긴다. 뒷부분을 경계로 오인해 구두점을 찍은 오류다.
C: however 뒤에만 쉼표가 있어 삽입 표시가 비대칭이다. 삽입어는 앞뒤 쉼표가 짝을 이루어야 한다.
problem.explanationEn:
The answer is D. Look at what comes before the blank: "The speckled birds that Amr had raised since boyhood." That's only a subject (a noun phrase with a relative clause), not a complete clause. Its verb comes after the blank: "could not make the journey." So "however" is an aside dropped into the middle of one clause, between the subject and its verb. An aside like this needs a comma on both sides.
A is wrong because a semicolon has to join two independent clauses. The part before it has no main verb, so it's a fragment. This choice mistakes the aside for a break between clauses.
B is wrong because the semicolon after "however" cuts the subject off from its verb. It treats "could not make the journey..." as if it were a separate clause.
C is wrong because it puts a comma only after "however." That leaves the aside lopsided, since it needs matching commas on both sides.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞은 긴 주어(명사구+관계절 'that Amr had raised since boyhood')만 있고 뒤는 그 주어의 동사 'could not make the journey'이므로 however는 절 내부 삽입어 → ', however,'(D)가 정답. 관계절 안의 'Amr had raised'가 독립절처럼 보이는 미끼 구조라 절 경계 판별 사고가 추가로 요구됨. 해설도 각 오답을 구조적으로 정확히 설명. 다만 체크리스트 4항(콤마 스플라이스 오답)은 미충족: 설계상 앞뒤가 독립절이 아니므로 A·B는 fragment/주어-동사 단절 오류이지 콤마 스플라이스가 아님. C의 선택지 앞 공백 두 칸은 사소한 표기 문제.

advisory.note: 빈칸은 주어와 동사 사이에 있으므로 however는 삽입어이고, 쉼표 한 쌍으로 감싼 D가 정답입니다. 주어에 관계절(that Amr had raised)이 붙어 있어 빈칸 앞이 완전한 절처럼 보이는 함정이 있습니다. 그래서 단순한 medium 문항보다는 판단이 더 필요합니다. 다만 선택지 어디에도 두 독립절을 쉼표로만 잇는 구조가 없으므로, 콤마 스플라이스 오답이 있어야 한다는 레시피 4번 항목을 충족하지 못합니다. C는 쉼표가 비대칭인 오답으로 5번 항목을 충족합니다.

problem.passage:
The rain had finally thinned to a drizzle over the Mumbai rooftops when Priya stepped out to assess the damage. Deepak's marigolds, she noted with satisfaction, had been flattened overnight. Leaning over the low wall between their rooftops, a dripping trowel still in her hand, ______ all while pretending not to notice that Deepak had paused his watering to watch her.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: The rain had finally thinned to a drizzle over the Mumbai rooftops when Priya stepped out to assess the damage. Deepak's marigolds, she noted with satisfaction, had been flattened overnight. Leaning over the low wall between their rooftops, a dripping trowel still in her hand, ______ all while pretending not to notice that Deepak had paused his watering to watch her.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: Priya counted the broken stems with exaggerated care,
the monsoon wind scattered the broken stems with exaggerated care,
Priya's gaze counted the broken stems with exaggerated care,
the flattened bed displayed its broken stems with exaggerated care,
problem.explanation:
분사구 "Leaning over the low wall..., a dripping trowel still in her hand"는 담장 너머로 몸을 기울이고 손에 모종삽을 든 사람, 즉 Priya를 수식한다. 따라서 주절 주어는 Priya여야 한다. A가 정답이다.
B: 'the monsoon wind'는 수식어와 아무 상관없는 명사다. 바람은 몸을 기울이지도, 모종삽을 들지도 못한다.
C: 'Priya's gaze'는 Priya와 관련은 있지만 사람이 아니라 사람에게 딸린 것이다. 시선에는 손이 없으니 모종삽을 들 수 없다.
D: 'the flattened bed'는 단수라서 동사와 수는 맞고 지문 속 소재와도 이어진다. 하지만 짓눌린 화단이 담장 너머로 몸을 기울일 수는 없다. 네 선택지 모두 문법적으로는 완전한 절이므로, 수식 대상이 누구인지 의미로 판단해야 답을 고를 수 있다.
problem.explanationEn:
The opening modifier, "Leaning over the low wall between their rooftops, a dripping trowel still in her hand," describes a person who is leaning and holding a trowel. That person is Priya, so the main clause has to start with Priya as its subject. That makes A correct.
B: "The monsoon wind" has nothing to do with the modifier. Wind can't lean over a wall or hold a trowel.
C: "Priya's gaze" is connected to Priya, but it belongs to her rather than being her. A gaze has no hand, so it can't hold a trowel.
D: "The flattened bed" is singular, so it agrees with the verb, and it comes from the scene. But a flower bed can't lean over a wall. All four choices are grammatically complete clauses, so you can only pick the answer by deciding who the modifier actually describes.

hardJudge.note: 문두 분사구 "Leaning over the low wall..., a dripping trowel still in her hand"의 논리적 주어는 사람(Priya)이며, A만 이에 일치한다. B·C·D는 모두 주어+동사를 갖춘 문법적으로 완전한 절이고 모두 단수이므로 수일치로는 가려낼 수 없다. 특히 C(Priya's gaze)는 소유격 함정으로 SAT 전형 오답 패턴이며 수식 대상 추론을 실제로 요구한다. 해설은 각 오답 배제 근거를 정확히 제시하고 모순이 없다. 다만 수식어 속 'her hand'/'watch her'가 사람 주어 단서를 제공해 난이도가 다소 완화되는 점과, B·D의 'with exaggerated care'가 의미상 부자연스러워 정답 유추가 쉬워지는 점은 소폭 감점 요인이나 hard 기준은 충족한다.

advisory.note: 분사구 뒤에 독립 부가어(a dripping trowel still in her hand)가 붙어 있고, 소유격을 이용한 함정 선택지 C(Priya's gaze)가 들어 있어 전형적인 medium 문항보다 의미적 판단이 더 필요하다. 모든 선택지가 과거시제 단수 주어라서 수일치나 시제로는 답을 가를 수 없다. 빈칸 뒤 'all while pretending...'과도 문법적으로 잘 이어진다.

problem.passage:
The Lake Street platform was crowded that October morning in 1962, and the wind off the lake rattled the tin sign above the stairs. Samuel, who had moved to the neighborhood only the week before, kept his back to the two women behind him as they murmured about "that mixed family" on Washburne Avenue. Pretending to study the timetable posted on the iron pillar in front of him, ______ until a boy in a Cubs cap tapped his elbow and asked, with frank curiosity, whether his mother really painted pictures for the Art Institute.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: The Lake Street platform was crowded that October morning in 1962, and the wind off the lake rattled the tin sign above the stairs. Samuel, who had moved to the neighborhood only the week before, kept his back to the two women behind him as they murmured about "that mixed family" on Washburne Avenue. Pretending to study the timetable posted on the iron pillar in front of him, ______ until a boy in a Cubs cap tapped his elbow and asked, with frank curiosity, whether his mother really painted pictures for the Art Institute.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the timetable's fine print held Samuel's gaze while the whispers grew sharper,
Samuel held his gaze on the fine print while the whispers grew sharper,
the crowded platform held Samuel's gaze on the fine print while the whispers grew sharper,
the women behind him held their gaze on the fine print while the whispers grew sharper,
problem.explanation:
정답 B. 분사구문 "Pretending to study the timetable posted on the iron pillar in front of him"의 의미상 주어는 주절의 주어와 같아야 한다. 시간표를 보는 척할 수 있는 건 사람뿐이고, 지문에서 그 사람은 여자들에게 등을 돌린 채 수군거림을 못 들은 척하는 Samuel이다. B만 Samuel을 주어로 두었다.
A: 수식어구 바로 앞에 나오는 무생물 명사(timetable)를 주어로 삼았다. 시간표의 글씨가 무언가를 보는 척할 수는 없으므로 현수 수식어(dangling modifier) 오류다.
C: 문장 앞부분에서 배경으로 깔린 명사(platform)를 주어로 삼았다. 승강장은 행위자가 아니다.
D: 사람이라서 문법적으로는 그럴듯해 보이지만, 여자들은 Samuel의 '뒤'에서 수군거리는 당사자들이다. 'in front of him'의 기둥에 붙은 시간표를 보는 척하며 수군거림을 견디는 인물은 Samuel이므로 수식어구의 실제 행위자와 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn:
The answer is B. A participial phrase at the start of a sentence has to describe the subject of the main clause that follows. Only a person can pretend to study a timetable. In this passage, that person is Samuel: he keeps his back to the whispering women and acts as if he can't hear them. Choice B is the only option that puts Samuel in the subject position.
A is wrong because it makes "the timetable's fine print" the subject. That's the nearest noun to the phrase, but print can't pretend to do anything, so the modifier dangles.
C is wrong because it makes "the crowded platform" the subject. The platform is just part of the setting, and it can't perform the action either.
D is wrong because it makes the women the subject. They are people, so this choice looks grammatically fine at first. However, the women are behind Samuel, and they're the ones doing the whispering. The person pretending to read the timetable on the pillar in front of him while the whispers grow sharper is Samuel, not the women.

hardJudge.note: 분사구문 "Pretending to study the timetable ... in front of him"의 의미상 행위자는 Samuel이며, B만 주절 주어를 Samuel로 둠. A(timetable, 인접 무생물), C(platform, 배경 명사)는 명백한 현수 수식어. D(the women)는 사람이라 문법적으로 그럴듯하나, 'in front of him'·'behind him'·'kept his back to' 등 지문 전체의 공간·행위 정보를 추적해야 배제 가능하므로 의미상 행위자 판별을 요구함. 정답 삽입 시 "Samuel held his gaze ... while the whispers grew sharper, until a boy ... tapped his elbow" 구조도 자연스럽고 'his mother'의 지시도 일관됨. 해설은 정답을 정확히 뒷받침하며 모순 없음. 1962년 시카고 Lake Street 역, Art Institute 등 배경 설정에 사실 오류 없음. 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: B가 정답이다. 오답 D는 사람이 주어라서 문법적으로는 성립한다. 하지만 여자들은 Samuel 뒤에서 수군거리는 당사자들이므로, 문맥을 따라가 실제 행위자를 판별해야 걸러진다. 그래서 전형적인 medium 문항보다 한 단계 더 사고해야 한다. A와 C는 무생물이 주어라서 쉽게 걸러진다.

problem.passage:
Every Saturday night in the cinder-block gym behind the union hall, Carl Mabry and Donnie Pruitt circled each other while miners still gray with coal dust stamped on the bleachers. Everyone in town expected the old grudge between their fathers to finally boil over on the mat. Carl had pinned Donnie three weekends running______when the referee raised Carl's arm that night, Carl bent down and pulled his rival to his feet before he acknowledged the cheering crowd.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Every Saturday night in the cinder-block gym behind the union hall, Carl Mabry and Donnie Pruitt circled each other while miners still gray with coal dust stamped on the bleachers. Everyone in town expected the old grudge between their fathers to finally boil over on the mat. Carl had pinned Donnie three weekends running______when the referee raised Carl's arm that night, Carl bent down and pulled his rival to his feet before he acknowledged the cheering crowd.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , nevertheless,
; therefore,
; nevertheless,
, and however,
problem.explanation:
먼저 두 절의 논리 관계부터 파악한다. 앞 절은 Carl이 세 주 연속 Donnie를 이겼다는 내용이고, 앞 문장에서 마을 사람들은 두 집안의 묵은 원한이 터지기를 기대했다. 그런데 뒤 절에서 Carl은 승리를 인정받는 순간 관중에게 답하기도 전에 라이벌을 일으켜 세운다. 앞의 예상과 정반대인 행동이므로 두 절은 '대조' 관계다. 두 독립절을 대조의 접속부사로 이으려면 세미콜론과 nevertheless를 함께 써야 하므로 C가 정답이다.
A: 접속부사 nevertheless는 접속사가 아니므로 콤마만으로 두 독립절을 이으면 콤마 스플라이스(comma splice)가 된다.
B: 구두점(세미콜론)은 맞지만 therefore는 인과 관계를 나타낸다. 연승한 것이 상대를 일으켜 세운 '이유'가 아니라 예상을 뒤집는 대조이므로 논리가 맞지 않는다.
D: 등위접속사 and와 대조 접속부사 however를 겹쳐 쓴 불필요한 중복이다. 게다가 and는 대조가 아니라 단순 나열을 나타낸다.
problem.explanationEn:
Start by working out how the two clauses relate. The first clause says Carl had beaten Donnie three weekends in a row. The sentence before it says the town expected the families' old grudge to boil over. The second clause shows the opposite of that expectation: as soon as Carl wins, he helps his rival up before he even responds to the crowd. So the relationship is contrast. When you join two independent clauses with a conjunctive adverb, you need a semicolon before it. That's why "; nevertheless," (C) is correct.
A is wrong because "nevertheless" is a conjunctive adverb, not a conjunction. Joining two independent clauses with only a comma before it creates a comma splice.
B uses the correct punctuation, but "therefore" signals cause and effect. Carl's winning streak isn't the reason he helps Donnie up; his gesture goes against what everyone expected.
D is wrong because it stacks the conjunction "and" on top of the conjunctive adverb "however," which is redundant. Also, "and" signals simple addition, not contrast.

hardJudge.note: 정답 C 검산: 두 독립절(앞: 3주 연속 핀, 뒤: when절+주절)을 세미콜론+nevertheless로 연결하는 구조가 문법적으로 타당하며, 앞 문장의 '원한이 터지리라는 기대'와 Carl의 스포츠맨십 행동이 대조를 이루므로 논리도 맞다. A는 콤마 스플라이스, B는 인과 접속부사로 논리 불일치, D는 and+however 중복으로 각 오답 설계가 체크리스트에 부합한다. 대조 관계를 빈칸 문장 내부가 아니라 앞 문장의 마을 사람들의 기대를 통해 추론해야 하므로 단순 medium보다 문맥 추론 단계가 추가된다. 허구 지문으로 사실 오류·저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 C는 맞음: 세미콜론 + nevertheless가 대조 관계를 나타내며 두 독립절을 바르게 잇는다. 해설은 정답과 일치하고 오류가 없다. 오답 구성은 레시피대로다(콤마 스플라이스, 인과 접속어, and+however 중복). 다만 난이도가 hard 수준인지는 의문이다. 오답 중 문법이 맞는 것은 B 하나뿐이고, B는 인과 대 대조만 판단하면 바로 걸러진다. 대조 관계도 '연승 → 관대한 행동'이라는 전형적인 패턴이라 쉽게 보인다. 원한에 대한 예상을 이용한 장치가 조금 있지만, 일반적인 medium 수준의 접속부사·구두점 문항보다 사고를 크게 더 요구하지는 않는다.

problem.passage:
Rain drummed on the thatched roof of the houseboat as Radha handed the fisherman a dry cloth. Thomas wrung the water from his shirt and stared at the brown current for a long while. When he finally spoke, he explained that since his son had drowned two monsoons earlier, his routine had not changed at all: "Each morning I still mend two nets, row out past the temple steps, and ______ beside the empty place in the boat until the light comes." Radha said nothing, but she thought of the second plate she continued to set out at dinner.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Rain drummed on the thatched roof of the houseboat as Radha handed the fisherman a dry cloth. Thomas wrung the water from his shirt and stared at the brown current for a long while. When he finally spoke, he explained that since his son had drowned two monsoons earlier, his routine had not changed at all: "Each morning I still mend two nets, row out past the temple steps, and ______ beside the empty place in the boat until the light comes." Radha said nothing, but she thought of the second plate she continued to set out at dinner.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: sat
sitting
had sat
sit
problem.explanation:
정답 D(sit): 빈칸은 인용문 안의 병렬 구조 "I still mend ..., row ..., and ___"의 세 번째 항목이다. 따옴표 안에서 Thomas는 지금도 반복하는 습관을 현재시제로 말하고 있고("Each morning", "still", "comes"), 주어 I에 맞춰 현재형 sit을 써야 mend, row와 병렬이 맞는다.
A(sat): 따옴표 밖 서술부(spoke, explained)의 과거시제에 끌려 고른 오답이다. 인용문은 직접 화법이라 원래 말한 시제(현재)를 그대로 유지해야 하므로 인용문 시제와 어긋난다.
B(sitting): 시제는 문제 될 것이 없어 보이지만 mend, row가 정동사인데 이 항목만 분사이다. 병렬 항목 하나만 형태가 달라 구조가 깨진다.
C(had sat): 주절의 "had drowned", "had not changed"와 같은 과거완료에 맞춘 것으로, 문장 속 한 절과는 맞지만 인용문 전체가 현재의 습관을 말한다는 맥락과 어긋난다.
problem.explanationEn:
Choice D, "sit," is correct. The blank is the third item in a parallel series inside the quotation: "I still mend ..., row ..., and ___." Inside the quotation marks, Thomas describes a habit he still keeps today, so he speaks in the present tense ("Each morning," "still," "comes"). The present-tense verb "sit" goes with the subject "I" and matches "mend" and "row."
Choice A, "sat," copies the past tense of the narration outside the quotation ("spoke," "explained"). But a direct quotation keeps the speaker's own tense, which here is present, so "sat" clashes with the rest of the quotation.
Choice B, "sitting," breaks the parallel structure. "Mend" and "row" are finite verbs, and "sitting" is a participle, so only this item has a different form.
Choice C, "had sat," matches the past perfect verbs in the narrator's clause ("had drowned," "had not changed"). It fits that one clause but not the context of the quotation, which describes a present habit.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸은 직접 인용문 내 "I still mend ..., row ..., and ___" 병렬의 세 번째 항목으로, 현재 습관("Each morning", "still", "until the light comes")에 맞는 현재형 sit(D)이 정답. 서술부의 과거(spoke, explained)·과거완료(had drowned, had not changed)와 인용문 내부 현재시제를 분리해 판단해야 하므로 전형적 단일문장 동사형 문항보다 문맥 추적이 추가로 요구됨. A는 서술부 시제에 끌린 오답, B는 병렬 형태 파괴, C는 과거완료 절에 국소적으로 맞지만 인용문 맥락과 불일치. 해설·정답·형식 모두 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 이 문항은 인용문 밖 서술의 과거시제(spoke, explained), 과거완료(had not changed), 인용문 안의 현재 습관(still, comes)을 함께 보고 판단해야 한다. 오답 A와 C는 각각 문맥 속 다른 시제에 끌리도록 만든 함정이어서, 단순 병렬 문항보다 한 단계 더 생각해야 한다. 다만 mend, row와 병렬을 맞추기만 해도 D를 바로 고를 수 있어 hard 수준으로는 경계선에 있다.

problem.passage:
Each evening the tannery vats along the river fell quiet beneath the copper light of the setting sun, and the smell of lime and dye drifted over the water. Having tucked another folded banknote into the tin she kept hidden beneath the drying racks, ______ wondering whether her father, who had worked these same pits for forty years, would have called her journey to Marrakech a betrayal or a beginning.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Each evening the tannery vats along the river fell quiet beneath the copper light of the setting sun, and the smell of lime and dye drifted over the water. Having tucked another folded banknote into the tin she kept hidden beneath the drying racks, ______ wondering whether her father, who had worked these same pits for forty years, would have called her journey to Marrakech a betrayal or a beginning.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: Fatima lingered among the stacked hides,
the tin rested among the stacked hides, with Fatima
the tannery vats stood silent around Fatima,
Fatima's father seemed to linger among the stacked hides, with Fatima
problem.explanation:
'Having tucked another folded banknote…'는 지폐를 깡통에 넣은 사람을 수식하는 분사구문이다. 따라서 주절의 주어가 바로 그 행위자여야 한다. 'the tin she kept'의 she와 문맥상 그 사람은 Fatima이므로, Fatima를 주어로 둔 A가 정답이다. 이어지는 분사 wondering도 Fatima를 자연스럽게 수식한다.
B: 수식어구 바로 안에 있는 무생물 tin을 주어로 삼았다. 깡통이 지폐를 넣었다는 뜻이 되므로 현수 수식어(dangling modifier)다.
C: 앞 문장의 배경 명사 vats를 주어로 삼았다. 통이 지폐를 넣은 셈이 되어 틀렸다.
D: 같은 사람이라 그럴듯한 아버지를 주어로 삼았다. 그러나 지폐를 모으는 사람은 Fatima이고, 아버지는 'her father'로 따로 언급되는 다른 인물이므로 행위자가 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn:
The opening phrase "Having tucked another folded banknote into the tin she kept hidden…" describes whoever put the money away. A modifier like this must be followed directly by the person who performed the action. The pronoun "she" and the context show that this person is Fatima, so choice A is correct. The later phrase "wondering…" also fits Fatima.
B makes "the tin" the subject. The tin is the inanimate noun closest to the modifier, but this wording says the tin tucked the banknote away, which is a dangling modifier.
C makes "the tannery vats" the subject. They are background nouns from the first sentence, and vats can't hide money.
D makes Fatima's father the subject. He is a person, so this choice seems plausible, but Fatima is the one saving money. The passage mentions her father separately ("her father"), so he can't be the one who tucked the banknote away.

hardJudge.note: 문두 분사구문 'Having tucked…the tin she kept…'의 행위자는 'she'=Fatima이며, A만이 이를 주절 주어로 둔다. B(tin, 인접 명사), C(vats, 앞 문장 배경 명사), D(father, 'with Fatima'로 문법적 외형을 갖춘 그럴듯한 인물)는 모두 현수 수식어. 특히 B·D는 'with Fatima wondering'으로 뒤의 분사를 흡수해 표면적으로 자연스럽게 읽히므로, 수식어의 의미상 주체를 지문 전체(she, her father가 별개 인물임)에서 추적해야 한다는 점에서 medium 이상의 사고를 요구한다. 해설은 정답·오답 근거를 정확히 설명하며 모순 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 A는 맞다. 오답 B(tin)와 C(vats)는 무생물이어서 분사의 행위자가 될 수 없다는 점이 바로 보인다. D(father)는 her father/she로 지시 대상이 구분되어 쉽게 걸러진다. 결국 전형적인 현수 수식어 medium 문항이고, 어려움은 지문 길이와 장식적 묘사에서만 온다. 정답 주어를 찾으려고 문장 전체를 추적할 필요가 거의 없다.

problem.passage:
As the ferry pulled away from the dock, Delroy pressed a bottle of dark island rum into Marcus's hands and grinned the way he had when they were boys. The gift was meant as pure affection, a reminder of the nights they had spent laughing on the old jetty______ heard in it only a quiet rebuke for the twelve years he had stayed away, and he said nothing as the water widened between them.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: As the ferry pulled away from the dock, Delroy pressed a bottle of dark island rum into Marcus's hands and grinned the way he had when they were boys. The gift was meant as pure affection, a reminder of the nights they had spent laughing on the old jetty______ heard in it only a quiet rebuke for the twelve years he had stayed away, and he said nothing as the water widened between them.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , Marcus
; however, Marcus
; therefore, Marcus
; and however, Marcus
problem.explanation: 앞 절은 선물이 '순수한 애정'으로 의도되었다는 내용이고, 뒤 절은 Marcus가 그것을 '책망'으로 받아들였다는 내용이므로 두 절은 대조 관계다. 두 독립절을 세미콜론으로 나누고 대조의 접속부사 however를 쓴 B가 정답이다. A: 콤마만으로 두 독립절을 이은 콤마 스플라이스다. C: 구두점은 맞지만 therefore는 인과를 나타내므로 대조 관계와 맞지 않는다(애정이 있었기 때문에 책망으로 들었다는 말이 되어 버린다). D: and와 however를 함께 써서 연결어가 불필요하게 겹치고, 세미콜론 뒤 'and however'는 문법적으로도 성립하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Start with the logic. The first clause says the gift was meant as pure affection. The second says Marcus heard only a rebuke in it. Those two ideas contrast. Both are independent clauses, so you can join them with a semicolon followed by a contrast word like "however," which makes B correct. A is a comma splice: a comma alone can't join two independent clauses. C gets the punctuation right, but "therefore" shows cause and effect, which would mean the affection caused Marcus to hear a rebuke. That doesn't make sense. D stacks two connectors, "and" and "however," which is redundant and ungrammatical after a semicolon.

hardJudge.note: 정답 B 검산: 앞 절(선물은 순수한 애정으로 의도됨)과 뒤 절(Marcus는 책망으로 들음)은 '의도 vs 수용'의 대조이며, 세미콜론+however+콤마는 표준 형식. A는 콤마 스플라이스, C는 인과 접속부사로 논리 불일치, D는 and/however 중복. 대조 관계가 'meant as'/'heard in it only'라는 암시적 단서로만 제시되고, 앞 절 뒤에 긴 동격구("a reminder of the nights...jetty")가 삽입되어 절 경계 판별이 추가로 요구되므로 의미 판단 선행형 hard 특성에 부합. 해설은 정답과 오답 근거를 정확히 뒷받침하며 모순 없음. 창작 문학 지문으로 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: 대조 관계는 'meant as pure affection'과 'heard only a quiet rebuke'의 의도와 수용 차이를 읽어야 드러나서, 표면 단서만으로는 판단하기 어렵다. 앞 절에 관계사절과 동격구가 들어 있어 독립절의 경계를 찾기도 다소 어렵다. 다만 D의 'and however'는 오답이 너무 쉽게 드러나서 변별력이 약하다.

problem.passage:
At the mountain bus depot outside Real del Monte, Alejandra turned her grandmother's silver ring over in her palm. Tucked inside the velvet box was a note in faded ink: "This ring is not mine to give; it belongs to the woman your grandfather loved first." For years Alejandra had believed the family story of a single, faithful marriage without question. Now she reread the line twice, pressed the ring onto her finger, and ______ toward the idling bus as though the whole valley had shifted beneath her.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: At the mountain bus depot outside Real del Monte, Alejandra turned her grandmother's silver ring over in her palm. Tucked inside the velvet box was a note in faded ink: "This ring is not mine to give; it belongs to the woman your grandfather loved first." For years Alejandra had believed the family story of a single, faithful marriage without question. Now she reread the line twice, pressed the ring onto her finger, and ______ toward the idling bus as though the whole valley had shifted beneath her.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: stumbles
stumbling
stumbled
had stumbled
problem.explanation:
정답 C. 빈칸은 "reread ... pressed ... and ______"로 이어지는 병렬 구조의 세 번째 동사이며, 서술은 단순과거로 진행된다. 따라서 단순과거 stumbled가 앞의 두 동사와 형태·시제 모두 일치한다.
A(stumbles): 따옴표 속 인용문의 현재시제(is, belongs)에 이끌린 선택이다. 인용문은 쪽지 내용이라 현재형이지만 서술은 과거형이므로 틀렸다.
B(stumbling): 병렬 항목 중 하나만 분사 형태로 바꾼 것이다. 주어 she에 이어지는 정동사 자리가 필요하므로 병렬이 깨진다.
D(had stumbled): 앞 문장의 "had believed"(과거완료)와는 맞지만, 이 행동은 Now 이후 다시 읽고 반지를 끼운 뒤에 일어난 일이므로 과거완료로 앞선 시점을 표시하면 사건 순서가 어긋난다.
problem.explanationEn:
C is correct. The blank is the third verb in a parallel series: "reread ... pressed ... and ______." The story is narrated in the simple past, so "stumbled" matches the other two verbs in both form and tense.
A ("stumbles") picks up the present tense of the quoted note ("is," "belongs"). The note is in present tense because it is quoting what was written, but the narration around it is in the past, so the present tense doesn't fit here.
B ("stumbling") switches just one item in the series to a participle. Like the other two verbs, this one needs to be a finite verb with "she" as its subject, so B breaks the parallel structure.
D ("had stumbled") matches the past perfect in the earlier sentence ("had believed"). But the stumbling happens after she rereads the note and puts on the ring. The past perfect would wrongly place it before those actions.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸은 "reread … pressed … and ___" 병렬의 세 번째 정동사이며 서술 시제는 단순과거이므로 C(stumbled)가 유일하게 적합. A는 인용문의 현재시제(is, belongs)에 이끌린 함정으로 서술 시제와 충돌(체크리스트 3은 '인용문 시제를 이용한 함정'으로 해석해 충족 처리), B는 병렬 항목 하나만 분사형으로 바뀌어 정동사 결여, D는 앞 문장의 had believed와 국소적으로 호응하나 'Now' 이후의 사건 순서상 과거완료가 부적절. 인용문 vs 서술, 병렬, 앞 문장의 과거완료라는 세 층위의 시제 판단을 요구하므로 medium 이상. 해설은 정답을 정확히 뒷받침하며 모순 없음.

advisory.note: 병렬 동사(reread, pressed, ___)를 단순과거로 맞춰야 한다. 오답 유인이 두 갈래로 설계되어 있다. 하나는 인용문 속 현재시제(is, belongs)이고, 다른 하나는 앞 문장의 과거완료(had believed)다. 그래서 문맥 전체에서 시제를 추적해야 하고, medium보다 약간 높은 수준이다. 다만 병렬 구조가 분명해서 hard 상한에는 미치지 못한다.

problem.passage:
The bidding on the last lot, a sun-bleached saddle with a cracked horn, had stalled at forty dollars when Buck noticed the woman at the edge of the corral. She wore a gray felt hat pulled low, but the way she tilted her head as she listened was something he had not seen in thirty years. Lowering the microphone from his mouth and squinting past the glare off the stock trailers, ______ that it was Ellen Marsh, the girl who had once carved both their initials into the schoolhouse fence.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: The bidding on the last lot, a sun-bleached saddle with a cracked horn, had stalled at forty dollars when Buck noticed the woman at the edge of the corral. She wore a gray felt hat pulled low, but the way she tilted her head as she listened was something he had not seen in thirty years. Lowering the microphone from his mouth and squinting past the glare off the stock trailers, ______ that it was Ellen Marsh, the girl who had once carved both their initials into the schoolhouse fence.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the glare off the trailers made Buck realize
the stalled bidding on the saddle gave Buck the realization
the woman in the gray hat let Buck realize
Buck realized
problem.explanation:
문장 앞의 분사구 "Lowering the microphone ... and squinting past the glare ..."의 의미상 주어는 마이크를 내리고 눈을 찡그린 사람, 즉 경매사 Buck이다. 따라서 콤마 바로 뒤 주어 자리에 Buck이 와야 하므로 정답은 D "Buck realized"이다.
A: 수식어구 바로 앞에 나온 무생물 명사 'glare'를 주어로 삼았다. 그러면 눈부심이 마이크를 내리고 눈을 찡그린 꼴이 되어 현수 수식어(dangling modifier) 오류가 생긴다.
B: 지문 앞부분의 배경 정보인 '멈춘 입찰(stalled bidding)'을 주어로 삼았다. 입찰은 마이크를 내릴 수 없다.
C: 'woman'도 사람이라 문법적으로는 그럴듯해 보이지만, 마이크를 든 사람은 경매사 Buck이지 그녀가 아니다. 행위자가 잘못 지정되었다.
problem.explanationEn:
The opening phrase "Lowering the microphone from his mouth and squinting past the glare..." must describe the noun that comes right after the comma. The person lowering the microphone is the auctioneer, Buck, so Buck has to be the subject. That makes D, "Buck realized," the correct answer.
A puts "the glare," the nearest non-living noun, in the subject position. That would mean the glare lowered the microphone, which is a dangling modifier.
B uses the background detail from the start of the passage, the stalled bidding, as the subject. Bidding can't lower a microphone or squint.
C might look right because the woman is also a person, but she isn't holding the microphone. Buck is, so C gives the action to the wrong person.

hardJudge.note: 분사구문 "Lowering the microphone ... and squinting past the glare ..."의 의미상 행위자는 마이크를 든 경매사 Buck이므로 D가 유일하게 올바름. A는 직전 명사 glare(인접 명사 오류), B는 앞 문장의 배경 명사 stalled bidding, C는 사람 명사 woman을 주어로 내세워 '사람이면 된다'는 단순 판단을 유도하는 그럴듯한 오답으로, 지문 전체에서 누가 마이크를 들고 있는지 추적해야만 소거 가능. 해설은 정답과 각 오답의 오류 유형을 정확히 설명하며 모순 없음. 형식·저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 정답은 D이다. 'Buck realized'만 분사구의 의미상 주어와 일치하며, 나머지 세 선택지는 모두 현수 수식어 오류를 만든다. 다만 마이크를 내리는 행위자가 Buck이라는 점이 너무 분명하다. 무생물인 A·B는 바로 제거되고, C의 woman도 '마이크를 든 사람'이라는 단서 하나로 탈락한다. 결국 전형적인 medium 수준의 현수 수식어 문항이며, 난이도는 문장 길이와 서사적 배경에서만 나온다. 행위자를 추적하기 어렵게 만드는 장치, 예를 들어 사람 명사 두 개가 모두 행위자로 그럴듯한 상황 같은 것이 없다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
In the allotment chapters of Mara Lindqvist's novel *Beet Rows*, the refugee Anke and her elderly mentor, Herr Vogt, hardly exchange a full sentence. He shows her how deep to set the leek seedlings by pressing her fingers into the soil, and she thanks him by leaving a jar of pickled beets at his shed door. Because the novel builds their trust almost wholly through such gestures, it seems to argue that spoken language is a barrier to human connection, one the two characters are lucky to escape.

Text 2
Readers sometimes forget how much of *Beet Rows* is told in words before Anke ever reaches the garden. In the opening chapters, Vogt's letters to his late wife describe the plot she tended for forty years and his fear of letting it go to weeds. When he later guides Anke's hands through the leek bed, the gesture moves us only because we already know what that soil means to him. The novel's silent scenes carry meaning that its written passages have stored up.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim made in Text 1 about what the novel suggests regarding spoken language?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
In the allotment chapters of Mara Lindqvist's novel *Beet Rows*, the refugee Anke and her elderly mentor, Herr Vogt, hardly exchange a full sentence. He shows her how deep to set the leek seedlings by pressing her fingers into the soil, and she thanks him by leaving a jar of pickled beets at his shed door. Because the novel builds their trust almost wholly through such gestures, it seems to argue that spoken language is a barrier to human connection, one the two characters are lucky to escape.

Text 2
Readers sometimes forget how much of *Beet Rows* is told in words before Anke ever reaches the garden. In the opening chapters, Vogt's letters to his late wife describe the plot she tended for forty years and his fear of letting it go to weeds. When he later guides Anke's hands through the leek bed, the gesture moves us only because we already know what that soil means to him. The novel's silent scenes carry meaning that its written passages have stored up.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim made in Text 1 about what the novel suggests regarding spoken language?
options: By arguing that the wordless scenes owe their power to things the novel has already told in words, so they do not show that language stands in the way of connection
By arguing that the scarcity of dialogue between Anke and Vogt shows that the novel presents speech as something its characters are better off without
By arguing that Vogt's letters to his late wife reveal how long she tended the plot and how much he fears it going to weeds
By arguing that the novel's account of planting leeks and pickling beets misrepresents how allotment gardens in Berlin are actually worked
problem.explanation: 정답 A: Text 2의 전제는 침묵 장면의 의미가 앞서 편지(언어)로 쌓인 맥락에서 나온다는 것이다. 그러면 '말은 연결의 장벽'이라는 Text 1의 해석은 성립하지 않는다. 이 반응은 Text 2의 전제에서 추론해야만 나온다. B는 Text 1의 주장을 되풀이할 뿐 Text 2의 관점과 맞지 않는다. C는 Text 2의 세부 내용만 반복하고 Text 1의 주장에 대한 반응이 되지 못한다. D는 원예 관행이 정확한가라는, 두 지문 모두 다루지 않은 쟁점을 끌어온다.
problem.explanationEn: A is correct. Text 2 assumes that the silent garden scenes matter only because of what the novel has already told in words, mainly Vogt's letters. If that's true, the wordless moments depend on language, so they can't show that language is a barrier. You have to infer this response from Text 2's premise. B just repeats Text 1's claim, and Text 2 would reject that claim. C restates details from Text 2 but never connects them to Text 1's claim about language. D raises a question neither text discusses: whether the novel gets Berlin gardening practices right.

hardJudge.note: Text 2는 Text 1을 직접 언급하지 않으며, 침묵 장면의 힘이 앞선 편지(언어)에서 저장된 의미에서 나온다는 전제에서 '언어가 연결의 장벽이 아니다'라는 반응을 스스로 추론해야 한다. A는 Text 2의 전제 범위를 넘지 않게 조절되어 있고, B는 Text 1 반복, C는 Text 2 세부 반복(반응 아님), D는 본문 밖 쟁점. 사소한 점: Text 1은 '말(spoken)'을, Text 2는 '편지(written)'를 다루나 A가 'told in words/language'로 묶어 처리해 추론 범위 안에서 무리 없음. 가상의 소설이라 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 A는 옳고, 레시피 체크리스트 다섯 항목도 모두 충족한다. 다만 hard 문항으로 보기는 어렵다. Text 2의 마지막 문장("silent scenes carry meaning that its written passages have stored up")이 A를 거의 그대로 말해 주기 때문에 추론해야 할 폭이 작다. 오답도 쉽게 걸러진다. B는 Text 1을 그대로 반복하고, C는 Text 2의 세부 내용을 나열할 뿐 Text 1에 대한 반응이 아니며, D는 두 지문 밖의 쟁점이다. 그래서 강도 미세조정(calibrated_claim_strength)이나 관점 혼동형 함정이 없다. 한 가지 덧붙이면, Text 1은 '말(spoken)'을 문제 삼고 Text 2는 '글(편지)'을 근거로 든다. 이 차이를 함정으로 활용할 수 있었는데 그러지 않았다. 전형적인 medium 수준이다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
In Lucia Ferrante's novel The Stoop on Sackett Street, set in 1910s Brooklyn, Rosa watches from her tenement stoop as her younger sister, Nina, leaves to board a steamer for California. Nina calls up to her twice, but Rosa says nothing and only raises a hand. Critic Daniel Ames argues that this wordless moment is the emotional center of the book. In his view, Rosa's refusal to speak shows a longing to escape that she cannot admit, and the scene therefore shows that the novel treats family duty as a trap that silences immigrant daughters.

Text 2
Scholar Teresa Valli also considers the departure scene central to Ferrante's novel, but she points out how Rosa behaves elsewhere in the book. When Rosa turns down a suitor who offers to take her to Chicago, and again when she agrees to run her father's fruit stand, she also says nothing. In both cases, the narrator describes her afterward as "settled" and "at ease." Valli concludes that in Ferrante's novel, Rosa falls silent when she has made a choice she accepts, not when she is hiding a regret.

Based on the texts, with which part of Ames's argument in Text 1 would Valli (Text 2) most likely disagree?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
In Lucia Ferrante's novel The Stoop on Sackett Street, set in 1910s Brooklyn, Rosa watches from her tenement stoop as her younger sister, Nina, leaves to board a steamer for California. Nina calls up to her twice, but Rosa says nothing and only raises a hand. Critic Daniel Ames argues that this wordless moment is the emotional center of the book. In his view, Rosa's refusal to speak shows a longing to escape that she cannot admit, and the scene therefore shows that the novel treats family duty as a trap that silences immigrant daughters.

Text 2
Scholar Teresa Valli also considers the departure scene central to Ferrante's novel, but she points out how Rosa behaves elsewhere in the book. When Rosa turns down a suitor who offers to take her to Chicago, and again when she agrees to run her father's fruit stand, she also says nothing. In both cases, the narrator describes her afterward as "settled" and "at ease." Valli concludes that in Ferrante's novel, Rosa falls silent when she has made a choice she accepts, not when she is hiding a regret.
problem.question: Based on the texts, with which part of Ames's argument in Text 1 would Valli (Text 2) most likely disagree?
options: The claim that Ferrante's novel presents family duty as a trap for immigrant daughters
The claim that Rosa's not speaking as Nina leaves reveals a desire she cannot express
The claim that Nina calls up to Rosa twice before leaving for the steamer
The claim that the departure scene is the emotional center of Ferrante's novel
problem.explanation:
정답 B: Ames의 결론(가족 의무=덫)은 'Rosa의 침묵은 말하지 못한 탈출 욕망을 드러낸다'는 해석에 기대고 있다. Valli는 소설 속 다른 장면에서 Rosa의 침묵이 받아들인 선택 뒤의 평온함을 나타낸다고 보여 주므로, 바로 이 근거가 되는 가정을 직접 공격한다.
A: 결론 자체다. Valli의 관찰은 결론을 간접적으로 약하게 만들 뿐, 그녀가 직접 문제 삼는 것은 결론을 떠받치는 침묵의 해석이다. 또 다른 근거로 결론이 성립할 가능성도 Valli는 배제하지 않는다.
C: Nina가 두 번 부른다는 것은 줄거리의 부수적 세부일 뿐이고, Valli는 이를 다루지 않는다.
D: Valli도 이 장면이 중심적이라고 명시적으로 동의한다("also considers the departure scene central").
problem.explanationEn:
Choice B is correct. Ames's conclusion that the novel treats duty as a trap depends on his reading of Rosa's silence as hidden longing to escape. Valli shows that elsewhere in the novel, Rosa falls silent after choices she accepts, and the narrator then calls her "settled" and "at ease." That evidence goes straight at Ames's interpretation of the silence, which is the assumption his argument rests on.
Choice A is incorrect because it is Ames's overall conclusion. Valli's evidence weakens it only indirectly, by undercutting its support. The specific point she challenges is how the silence should be read. Choice C is incorrect because Nina calling up twice is a minor plot detail that Valli never questions. Choice D is incorrect because Valli explicitly agrees that the departure scene is central.

hardJudge.note: Text 1의 결론(가족 의무=덫)과 근거(침묵=억눌린 탈출 욕망)가 분리되어 있고, Text 2는 침묵의 의미 해석이라는 가정 하나만을 반박하며 장면의 중심성(D)에는 명시적으로 동의한다. 정답 B는 결론이 아닌 가정이며, A(결론)와의 구분이 논증 구조 파악을 요구해 medium 이상이다. 검증: Valli의 "not when she is hiding a regret"이 Ames의 "longing to escape that she cannot admit"과 직접 충돌함을 확인. 다만 Text 2의 반박이 비교적 명시적이라 추론 부담은 중간 정도이고, C는 논증이 아닌 줄거리 세부라 변별력이 약한 선택지다. 가상의 소설·비평가 사용으로 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: Valli의 반박은 침묵을 숨긴 욕망으로 보는 해석(B)을 직접 겨냥한다. 결론 A는 그 해석에서 나온 것이어서 매력적인 오답이 된다. D는 Valli도 동의하는 부분이다. 학생은 Valli가 Ames의 결론에 어떻게 반응할지 직접 추론해야 하고, 결론과 근거도 구분해야 한다. 다만 A를 오답으로 확정하려면 결론과 가정을 구분해야 하는데, 이 지점이 다소 미묘하다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
In reviewing Hana Lee's novel The Fourteenth Floor, the critic Jae-won Park argues that a reconciliation scene in fiction convinces readers only when the characters themselves bring it about. If a storm, an accident, or a sudden darkness is what pushes estranged people to speak, Park contends, the novelist has let circumstance do the work that the characters' choices should do, and the resulting closeness feels borrowed rather than earned.

Text 2
In Lee's novel, a power outage leaves the widow Min-ja and her daughter Soo-jin, who rarely visits, sitting together in a dark Seoul apartment while rain drums on the windows. Unable to see each other's faces, the two finally admit what they have each resented for years. Critic Mi-rae Cho praises the scene as the most persuasive reconciliation in the book, arguing that it is precisely the blackout and the noise of the rain, which strip away the women's usual excuses for leaving, that make their honesty believable.

Based on the texts, how would Park (Text 1) most likely evaluate Cho's assessment of the outage scene in Text 2?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1

If a storm, an accident, or a sudden darkness is what pushes estranged people to speak, Park contends, the novelist has let circumstance do the work that the characters' choices should do, and the resulting closeness feels borrowed rather than earned.

Text 2
In Lee's novel, a power outage leaves the widow Min-ja and her daughter Soo-jin, who rarely visits, sitting together in a dark Seoul apartment while rain drums on the windows. Unable to see each other's faces, the two finally admit what they have each resented for years. Critic Mi-rae Cho praises the scene as the most persuasive reconciliation in the book, arguing that it is precisely the blackout and the noise of the rain, which strip away the women's usual excuses for leaving, that make their honesty believable.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would Park (Text 1) most likely evaluate Cho's assessment of the outage scene in Text 2?
options: Park would agree with it, since Cho shows that the darkness and rain make the women's long-delayed honesty believable to readers.
Park would partly agree with it, since the women do eventually speak for themselves even though the outage first brings them together.
Park would reject it, since the very feature Cho praises—the outage forcing the conversation—is what Park thinks makes closeness feel unearned.
Park would endorse it, since a blackout in a crowded apartment complex is a realistic event that grounds the scene in everyday life.
problem.explanation:
정답 C: Park의 기준은 화해가 인물의 선택에서 나와야 하며, 폭풍·어둠 같은 외부 상황이 대화를 강제하면 친밀감이 '빌려온 것'처럼 느껴진다는 것이다. Cho는 바로 그 정전과 빗소리가 정직함을 믿을 만하게 만든다고 칭찬하므로, Park의 기준에서는 Cho가 칭찬하는 요소가 오히려 결함이 된다.
A: Cho 자신의 기준(상황이 정직함을 가능하게 함)으로 평가한 것이다. Park는 바로 그 점을 문제 삼는다.
B: 두 기준을 섞은 평가다. 인물이 결국 직접 말한다는 점을 Park의 기준에 끌어오지만, Park는 대화를 촉발한 것이 상황이라면 화해가 얻어낸 것이 아니라고 본다. Cho도 정전이 결정적이라고 강조한다.
D: 일반 상식(사실적인 설정이면 좋다)에 따른 평가로, Park의 기준은 사건의 현실성이 아니라 화해의 원인이 누구에게 있는지에 관한 것이다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, C: Park's standard is that a reconciliation is convincing only when the characters' own choices bring it about. When a storm or sudden darkness forces the conversation, Park says the closeness feels "borrowed rather than earned." Cho praises the scene specifically because the blackout and rain drive the women to be honest. By Park's standard, the feature Cho praises is the scene's flaw.
A applies Cho's own standard, that the circumstances make the honesty believable. This is exactly the point Park objects to.
B blends the two critics' standards. Yes, the women speak for themselves, but Park cares about what causes the conversation, and Cho stresses that the outage causes it.
D uses a common-sense standard, that a realistic setting is a good thing. Park's standard isn't about whether the event is realistic. It's about whether the characters or the circumstances produce the reconciliation.

hardJudge.note: Park's criterion (characters, not circumstance, must produce reconciliation; storm/darkness → 'borrowed' closeness) is explicit in Text 1, and Cho's praise rests precisely on the blackout and rain forcing honesty, so C follows only from Park's standard. A applies Cho's own criterion, B blends the two (crediting the women for 'eventually speaking' while ignoring that the outage triggered it), D invokes an external realism standard. Explanation matches the key with no errors. Minor caution: Text 1's listing of 'storm' and 'sudden darkness' maps almost verbatim onto Text 2's rain and blackout, which makes the stance inference fairly direct; difficulty rests mainly on resisting B's partial-credit blend rather than on subtle inference. Fictional critics/novel, no copyright concern.

advisory.note: 정답 C는 맞다. 다만 Text 1이 'storm', 'sudden darkness'를 직접 예로 들고, Text 2의 정전·빗소리가 이와 거의 그대로 겹친다. 그래서 Park의 기준을 대입하는 데 추론이 거의 필요 없는 표면 대응 문항이며, 전형적인 medium 수준이다. B는 두 관점을 섞은 함정이지만 Park가 '촉발 요인'을 문제 삼는다는 점이 분명해 쉽게 배제된다. D의 'crowded apartment complex'는 본문에 없는 세부라 너무 쉽게 걸러진다. 선택지 사이에 미묘한 강도 차이도 없다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
In Marisol Abad's novel The Tide Schedule, the aging teacher Mr. Reyes spends forty years competing with Mr. Dalisay, the younger teacher on the island's school boat. Near the end, Reyes quietly hands Dalisay his worn lesson ledger. Critic Lorna Vibal reads this as surrender: with retirement near, Reyes gives up the rivalry that has defined him and admits that Dalisay has won.

Text 2
Critic Ben Aquino points out that Reyes's ledger is not a clean record of his own lessons. Its margins are full of notes reacting to Dalisay's methods: "D. tried this with fractions—better," "Answer D.'s tide-chart lesson next week." Aquino argues that for decades each man built his teaching partly in reply to the other, so their rivalry worked as a long, unspoken collaboration.

Based on the texts, how would Aquino (Text 2) most likely respond to Vibal's reading of the ledger scene (Text 1)?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
In Marisol Abad's novel The Tide Schedule, the aging teacher Mr. Reyes spends forty years competing with Mr. Dalisay, the younger teacher on the island's school boat. Near the end, Reyes quietly hands Dalisay his worn lesson ledger. Critic Lorna Vibal reads this as surrender: with retirement near, Reyes gives up the rivalry that has defined him and admits that Dalisay has won.

Text 2
Critic Ben Aquino points out that Reyes's ledger is not a clean record of his own lessons. Its margins are full of notes reacting to Dalisay's methods: "D. tried this with fractions—better," "Answer D.'s tide-chart lesson next week." Aquino argues that for decades each man built his teaching partly in reply to the other, so their rivalry worked as a long, unspoken collaboration.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would Aquino (Text 2) most likely respond to Vibal's reading of the ledger scene (Text 1)?
options: He would agree that the scene shows Reyes finally accepting that his retirement means the rivalry has to end.
He would point out that the margins of the ledger show both teachers improving their lessons over many years.
He would argue that the school boat setting, more than the ledger, carries the main symbolic weight of the ending.
He would argue that calling the gesture an admission of defeat assumes the ledger belonged to one competitor, when it was really a record both men had shaped.
problem.explanation:
정답 D: Text 2의 전제는 장부가 두 사람이 서로에게 응답하며 함께 만든 기록이라는 것이다. 그렇다면 장부를 건네는 것을 '패배 인정'으로 읽는 Vibal의 해석은 장부가 승패가 있는 경쟁에서 한쪽에만 속한 소유물이라고 가정하고 있는 셈이다. Aquino는 바로 이 가정을 반박할 것이다. 이 반응은 Text 2에 직접 쓰여 있지 않고, Text 2의 전제로부터 추론해야만 나온다.
A: Text 1의 해석(은퇴, 경쟁의 끝)을 그대로 되풀이한다. Aquino는 이 장면을 끝이 아니라 협력이 완성되는 순간으로 볼 것이다.
B: Text 2의 결론(여백 메모, 서로의 개선)만 다시 말할 뿐, Vibal의 '항복' 해석에 대한 반응이 아니다.
C: 배라는 배경의 상징성은 Text 2가 전혀 다루지 않은 쟁점이다.
problem.explanationEn:
D is correct. Text 2 starts from the idea that the ledger is a record both men built together, with each one answering the other's lessons. Vibal reads the handover as Reyes admitting defeat, but that only works if the ledger belonged to one competitor in a contest someone could win. Aquino would challenge exactly that assumption. Text 2 never says this response outright; you have to infer it from what Text 2 assumes.
A is wrong because it simply repeats Text 1's reading (retirement ends the rivalry). Aquino would see the scene as completing a collaboration, not ending a contest.
B is wrong because it only restates Text 2's own evidence. It never actually answers Vibal's "surrender" reading.
C is wrong because Text 2 says nothing about the symbolism of the boat setting. That issue is brought in from outside the texts.

hardJudge.note: Text 2는 Vibal을 언급하지 않으며, 정답 D는 '장부=공동 기록'이라는 Aquino의 전제에서 '패배 인정' 해석의 숨은 가정(장부가 한쪽 소유)을 도출해야 하므로 명시되지 않은 반응을 추론하는 hard 특성을 충족한다. A는 Text 1 반복, B는 Text 2 내용 재진술(Vibal에 대한 반응 아님), C는 본문 외 쟁점(배 배경 상징)으로 오답 설계가 적절하다. 'a record both men had shaped'는 Dalisay가 직접 쓴 것은 아니지만 그의 방법이 내용을 형성했다는 점에서 허용 범위. 해설도 정답을 정확히 뒷받침한다. 가상 소설·비평가 설정으로 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 D는 Text 2의 전제(장부는 두 사람이 함께 만든 기록)를 바탕으로 Vibal 해석의 숨은 가정(장부는 한 사람의 소유물)을 반박하는 것으로, 추론이 필요하다. B는 Text 2 내용과 겹쳐 그럴듯한 오답이지만 Vibal 해석에 대한 반응이 아니다. 다만 D가 다른 선택지보다 눈에 띄게 길고 구체적이라 길이만으로 정답이 드러날 위험이 있다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
In the dawn scene of Linh Tran's novel The Long Simmer, set in a Hanoi street-food alley, Duc's grandmother teaches him to char ginger and skim the beef-bone broth. The scene opens in the dark, with the pot already steaming from its overnight simmer. When Duc's father stirs bouillon powder into a second pot, she remarks, "Of course—bones are so slow, and customers never notice." Because this mock approval plainly rebukes her son, the scene sets the old woman's tradition against the father's shortcuts, and the novel finally condemns him as a man who has given up his inheritance.

Text 2
Readers who hear only scorn in the grandmother's line overlook an earlier chapter. There, recalling the rationing years, she says almost the same words about the powder she herself once stirred into her broth, and she laughs as she says them. Her son laughs too. The phrase is a family joke, used to poke fun at oneself, and it shows Duc that every cook is tempted by shortcuts. Whatever the novel finally decides about the father, this line cannot show it. Still, the scene clearly shows the grandmother passing her broth technique on to Duc.

Based on the texts, which element of the argument in Text 1 would the author of Text 2 most likely challenge?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
In the dawn scene of Linh Tran's novel The Long Simmer, set in a Hanoi street-food alley, Duc's grandmother teaches him to char ginger and skim the beef-bone broth. The scene opens in the dark, with the pot already steaming from its overnight simmer. When Duc's father stirs bouillon powder into a second pot, she remarks, "Of course—bones are so slow, and customers never notice." Because this mock approval plainly rebukes her son, the scene sets the old woman's tradition against the father's shortcuts, and the novel finally condemns him as a man who has given up his inheritance.

Text 2
Readers who hear only scorn in the grandmother's line overlook an earlier chapter. There, recalling the rationing years, she says almost the same words about the powder she herself once stirred into her broth, and she laughs as she says them. Her son laughs too. The phrase is a family joke, used to poke fun at oneself, and it shows Duc that every cook is tempted by shortcuts. Whatever the novel finally decides about the father, this line cannot show it. Still, the scene clearly shows the grandmother passing her broth technique on to Duc.
problem.question: Based on the texts, which element of the argument in Text 1 would the author of Text 2 most likely challenge?
options: The assumption that the grandmother's ironic remark expresses scorn toward Duc's father
The assumption that the novel ultimately condemns Duc's father for giving up his inheritance
The assumption that the scene's opening in darkness stresses the long overnight simmer
The assumption that the scene shows the grandmother teaching Duc how to make the broth
problem.explanation:
정답 A: Text 1의 결론(소설이 아버지를 단죄함)은 할머니의 반어적 말이 아들을 '꾸짖는다'는 전제에 기대고 있다. Text 2는 할머니가 앞 장에서 자신을 두고 같은 말을 하며 웃었고 아들도 함께 웃었다는 점을 들어, 그 말이 자기 자신을 비꼬는 가족 농담이라고 본다. 즉 Text 2는 바로 이 전제를 공격한다.
B(결론 자체): Text 2는 'Whatever the novel finally decides about the father'라고 하여, 결론을 직접 부정하지 않고 판단을 보류한다. 문제 삼는 것은 이 대사가 결론의 근거가 될 수 있느냐는 점뿐이다.
C(부수적 세부): 새벽 어둠과 밤샘 끓이기에 관한 묘사는 Text 2가 전혀 다루지 않는다.
D(동의하는 부분): Text 2의 마지막 문장은 할머니가 Duc에게 육수 기술을 전수한다는 점에 분명히 동의한다.
problem.explanationEn:
Choice A is correct. Text 1's conclusion, that the novel condemns the father, depends on the idea that the grandmother's ironic line "plainly rebukes her son." Text 2 goes after exactly this idea. In an earlier chapter, she says nearly the same words about her own shortcuts and laughs, and her son laughs with her. So the line is a self-mocking family joke, not scorn.
Choice B is the conclusion itself. Text 2 does not reject it. It says "whatever the novel finally decides about the father" and argues only that this line can't support that judgment.
Choice C is a minor detail from Text 1 that Text 2 never mentions.
Choice D is something Text 2 agrees with. Its final sentence says the scene clearly shows the grandmother passing her technique on to Duc.

hardJudge.note: Text 1은 전제(반어가 아들을 꾸짖음)와 결론(소설이 아버지를 단죄)을 'Because…' 구조로 명확히 구분하고, Text 2는 앞 장의 자기비하 농담 근거로 전제만 공격하며 결론은 'Whatever the novel finally decides'로 보류하고 전수 장면(D)에는 동의한다. B는 결론 자체를 공격 대상으로 오인하게 하는 강도 조절 함정, D는 동의 부분, C는 미언급 세부로 기능이 분명하다. 가상 소설이라 저작권·사실 문제 없음. 정답 A 타당.

advisory.note: 핵심 함정은 B다. Text 2는 결론에 대한 판단을 보류하면서("Whatever the novel finally decides") 결론의 근거만 공격한다. 이처럼 근거 공격과 결론 부정을 구분해야 하므로 medium보다 한 단계 높은 사고가 필요하다. 다만 Text 2가 "hear only scorn"이라고 공격 대상을 거의 그대로 밝히고 있어, 정답 A는 비교적 직접적으로 찾을 수 있다. 그래서 hard 수준으로는 경계선에 있다. D는 Text 2가 동의하는 부분을 오답으로 둔 것으로, 레시피 4번을 충족한다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Seam Below is a 2019 novel by Ruth Carver.
- It is set in 1974 in Harlan Ridge, a coal-mining town in eastern Kentucky.
- Years before the story opens, mine foreman Dale Pruitt, drunk at his dying brother Wes's bedside, promised to bury Wes beside their father.
- Their father's grave lies in a hillside cemetery that was submerged when a reservoir was built in 1971.
- In 1974, Wes's widow arrives in Harlan Ridge and asks Dale to keep his word.

The student wants to explain why Dale cannot fulfill the obligation at the center of the novel. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Seam Below is a 2019 novel by Ruth Carver.
- It is set in 1974 in Harlan Ridge, a coal-mining town in eastern Kentucky.
- Years before the story opens, mine foreman Dale Pruitt, drunk at his dying brother Wes's bedside, promised to bury Wes beside their father.
- Their father's grave lies in a hillside cemetery that was submerged when a reservoir was built in 1971.
- In 1974, Wes's widow arrives in Harlan Ridge and asks Dale to keep his word.
problem.question: The student wants to explain why Dale cannot fulfill the obligation at the center of the novel. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In Ruth Carver's The Seam Below, mine foreman Dale Pruitt, drunk at his dying brother's bedside, promised years earlier to bury Wes beside their father.
In Ruth Carver's The Seam Below, Dale Pruitt once vowed to bury his brother Wes beside their father, but the father's grave has lain underwater since a reservoir flooded its cemetery in 1971.
In Ruth Carver's The Seam Below, set in the coal town of Harlan Ridge in 1974, Wes's widow arrives and asks Dale Pruitt to keep his word.
In Ruth Carver's The Seam Below, Dale Pruitt once vowed to bury his brother Wes beside their father, but the mining company Dale works for moved the father's grave to an unmarked site in 1971.
problem.explanation:
정답 B: 목표는 Dale이 의무를 이행할 수 없는 이유를 설명하는 것이다. B는 아버지 곁에 묻어 주겠다는 약속과, 아버지의 무덤이 1971년 저수지 건설로 물에 잠겼다는 사실을 함께 제시한다. 그래서 약속이 이제는 지킬 수 없는 것이 된 까닭이 드러난다.
A: 약속 내용만 담고 있어 지킬 수 없는 이유는 빠져 있다. 목표의 절반만 달성한다.
C: 배경(1974년 Harlan Ridge)과 미망인의 요청이라는 두 사실을 결합했지만, 둘 다 이행이 불가능한 이유와는 관계가 없다.
D: 형식은 B와 같지만 '광산 회사가 무덤을 표식 없는 곳으로 옮겼다'는 내용은 노트에 없다. 실제 원인인 수몰을 왜곡했다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer B: Your goal is to explain why Dale can't fulfill his obligation. B puts two facts together: his promise to bury Wes beside their father, and the fact that the father's grave has been underwater since a reservoir flooded the cemetery in 1971. Together, these show exactly why the promise can no longer be kept.
A: It only describes the promise. It never says why the promise is impossible to keep, so it does just half the job.
C: It combines two facts from the notes (the setting and the widow's request), but neither one explains why the obligation can't be fulfilled.
D: It uses the same sentence structure as B, but the notes never say a mining company moved the grave. That detail is made up, and it replaces the real cause, the flooding.

hardJudge.note: B는 약속(노트3)과 무덤 수몰(노트4)을 인과·대조 관계로 결합해 '이행 불가 이유'라는 목표를 정확히 충족한다. A는 약속만(한쪽만), C는 관련 없는 두 사실, D는 노트에 없는 내용(광산 회사의 이장)으로 그럴듯한 형식의 매력적 오답이다. 수험자는 노트3·4를 무덤이 물속에 있어 매장이 불가능하다는 함의로 연결해야 하므로 단순 사실 선택을 넘는 추론이 필요하다. 가상 작품으로 저작권·사실오류 문제 없음. 해설의 논리와 정답 일치.

advisory.note: 정답은 맞다. 다만 구조가 전형적인 medium 수준이다. A는 약속만 담고 이유가 빠져 있고, C는 목표와 관계없는 사실들을 담았으며, D는 노트에 없는 내용을 넣었다. 그래서 오답이 쉽게 걸러진다. 정답 B만 '약속+불가능한 이유'라는 인과를 담고 있어 추가적인 종합 판단이나 범위 조정이 필요 없다. D는 날조된 내용이 노트와 정면으로 어긋나 바로 탈락한다. 'cannot fulfill'이라는 표현이 B의 underwater와 곧바로 맞물려 hard 수준의 변별력이 부족하다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- "The Cap" is a 2019 short story by the fictional author Mara Elkins.
- In the story, a weary hiker named Thorne stops for the night at a crowded trail shelter in the Appalachian Mountains.
- A stranger at the shelter hands Thorne a handmade wool cap without explaining why.
- Thorne, aware of his matted hair and torn jacket, assumes the gift is a silent comment on how ragged he looks.
- The stranger had actually knitted the cap to share warmth with whoever arrived cold, as hikers often share space in shelters.
- Elkins grew up near the trail and has said she wrote the story during a snowstorm.

The student wants to emphasize the gap between what the stranger intended and what Thorne perceived. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- "The Cap" is a 2019 short story by the fictional author Mara Elkins.
- In the story, a weary hiker named Thorne stops for the night at a crowded trail shelter in the Appalachian Mountains.

problem.question: The student wants to emphasize the gap between what the stranger intended and what Thorne perceived. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In Mara Elkins's "The Cap," Thorne, conscious of his matted hair and torn jacket, accepts a handmade wool cap from a stranger at an Appalachian trail shelter.
In Mara Elkins's 2019 short story "The Cap," a weary hiker named Thorne spends a night at a crowded trail shelter, where he encounters a stranger.
In Mara Elkins's "The Cap," Thorne reads a stranger's handmade wool cap as a silent remark on his ragged appearance, though it was knitted simply to share warmth with any cold arrival.
In Mara Elkins's "The Cap," a story Elkins wrote during a snowstorm near the trail where she grew up, a stranger gives a hiker a handmade wool cap.
problem.explanation:
정답 C: Thorne의 해석(초라한 외모에 대한 무언의 지적)과 낯선 이의 실제 의도(추위에 떨며 도착한 누구에게나 온기를 나누려는 것)를 한 문장 안에서 대비시킨다. 그래서 둘 사이의 간극이 드러난다.
A: 헝클어진 머리, 찢어진 재킷처럼 세부 사항은 있지만 Thorne이 모자를 어떻게 해석했는지, 낯선 이가 무엇을 의도했는지는 빠져 있다. 지나치게 세부적이라 간극을 보여 주지 못한다.
B: 발표 연도, 대피소, 만남 등 줄거리를 넓게 소개할 뿐 모자도, 오해도 나오지 않는다. 지나치게 포괄적이라 초점을 잃었다.
D: 작가의 성장 배경과 집필 상황이라는 목표와 무관한 항목을 내세운다. 의도와 인식의 차이는 전혀 다루지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, C: This sentence puts Thorne's reading of the cap (a silent remark on how ragged he looks) right next to the stranger's real purpose (sharing warmth with anyone who arrives cold). Placing the two side by side shows the gap between them.
A: It gives details about Thorne's hair and jacket, but it never says how he interpreted the cap or what the stranger meant by it. It's too narrow to show the gap.
B: It sums up the setting and the meeting in broad terms but never mentions the cap or the misunderstanding. It's too general and loses the focus.
D: It highlights notes that don't serve the goal: where Elkins grew up and when she wrote the story. It says nothing about intention versus perception.

hardJudge.note: 목표(의도-인식 간극 강조)가 명확하며, C만이 Thorne의 해석과 낯선 이의 실제 의도라는 두 메모를 대비 구조("though")로 통합한다. A는 외모 세부에 치우쳐 해석·의도 모두 누락(지나치게 구체적), B는 줄거리 개관(지나치게 포괄적), D는 작가 배경이라는 무관 정보. 오답들이 모두 노트 기반으로 그럴듯하고, A가 "conscious of his matted hair"로 Thorne의 자의식을 암시해 유인력이 있다. 허구 작가/작품으로 저작권·사실 오류 없음. 해설은 정답과 오답 분석이 일관되며 모순 없음.

advisory.note: 정답은 C 하나뿐이다. 의도와 인식을 둘 다 담고 대비하는 선택지가 C밖에 없다. 하지만 이 때문에 정답이 너무 쉽게 드러난다. A·B·D는 모두 '오해'나 '의도'를 아예 언급하지 않으므로 키워드 대조만으로 지울 수 있다. 결국 전형적인 medium 수준이고, 확실성 판별이나 관계 방향 판단 같은 hard 특성은 요구하지 않는다. 덧붙여 D의 'wrote during a snowstorm near the trail'은 노트에 없는 결합이다(노트에는 성장 장소가 트레일 근처라는 것과 눈보라 속에서 썼다는 것이 따로 나온다). 오답 선택지라서 치명적이지는 않다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Leila Haddad's 2019 novel The Indigo Vat follows Karim, a master dyer at a riverside tannery in Fez, Morocco.
- In the novel's central scene, the ceremonial cloth tears as it is unveiled at the town's annual Indigo Festival.
- Literary scholar Amina Berrada has argued that the tear likely represents grief that Karim's family has never spoken aloud.
- In a 2022 reading-group study, about 60% of participants linked the tear to the death of Karim's father; the rest linked it to the tannery's economic decline.
- In interviews, Haddad has confirmed that the scene was inspired by a real accident she witnessed at a festival in 2009.

The student wants to report the novel's central event as a plain fact while signaling that one critic's interpretation of that event remains open to debate. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
