problem.question: The student wants to report the novel's central event as a plain fact while signaling that one critic's interpretation of that event remains open to debate. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In The Indigo Vat, the ceremonial cloth tears as it is unveiled at the Indigo Festival, an event that represents grief Karim's family has never spoken aloud, as scholar Amina Berrada has demonstrated.

In The Indigo Vat, the ceremonial cloth seems to tear as it is unveiled at the Indigo Festival, an event that, according to scholar Amina Berrada, likely represents grief Karim's family has never spoken aloud.
In The Indigo Vat, the ceremonial cloth tears as it is unveiled at the Indigo Festival, an event that, according to scholar Amina Berrada, likely reflects a real accident Haddad witnessed in 2009.

In The Indigo Vat, the ceremonial cloth tears as it is unveiled at the Indigo Festival, an event that, according to scholar Amina Berrada, likely represents grief Karim's family has never spoken aloud.
problem.explanation:
정답 D: 천이 찢어지는 사건은 노트에 줄거리상 사실로 나와 있으므로 단정적으로 서술하고, Berrada의 해석은 'according to ... likely'로 한정해 학자 한 명의 잠정적 견해임을 드러낸다. 목표의 두 조건을 모두 충족한다.
A: 해석을 'represents ... as ... has demonstrated'로 서술해 잠정적 주장('likely')을 입증된 사실로 과장했다.
B: 해석의 확실성 수준은 맞지만, 소설 속에서 실제로 일어나는 사건을 'seems to tear'로 불필요하게 약화했다.
C: 확실성 수준의 형식은 맞지만 내용을 혼동했다. 2009년 실제 사고는 Berrada의 해석이 아니라 Haddad 본인이 인터뷰에서 확인한 사실이다.
problem.explanationEn:
D is correct. The cloth tearing is something that definitely happens in the novel's plot, so D states it plainly. It then limits Berrada's reading with "according to" and "likely," which shows the interpretation is one critic's tentative view. That meets both parts of the goal.
A is wrong because it turns Berrada's tentative claim into a proven one ("represents... as Berrada has demonstrated"). That overstates how certain the interpretation is.
B handles the interpretation correctly, but it weakens a plot fact for no reason. The cloth doesn't just "seem" to tear in the novel. It actually tears.
C uses the right level of certainty but mixes up the content. The connection to a real 2009 accident is something Haddad herself confirmed in interviews. It isn't Berrada's interpretation, and it isn't open to debate.

hardJudge.note: 노트에 확정적 진술(천이 찢어짐, Haddad의 인터뷰 확인)과 잠정적 진술(Berrada의 'likely', 독서모임 60%)이 함께 제시됨. 정답 D는 사건을 단정('tears')하고 해석을 'according to… likely'로 한정해 목표의 두 조건을 정확히 충족. A는 'has demonstrated'로 과잉 일반화, B는 'seems to tear'로 사실의 확실성을 과도하게 축소, C는 Haddad의 확인 사실을 Berrada의 해석으로 오귀속. 해설은 각 선지 판단을 정확히 뒷받침하며 모순 없음. 사실(사건)과 해석(비평)의 확실성 수준을 동시에 교정해야 하고, 출처 귀속 오류 선지까지 걸러야 하므로 전형적 medium보다 추가 사고를 요구함. 가상의 소설·학자로 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 D가 맞다. 사건은 단정적으로 서술하고, 해석은 'according to Berrada… likely'로 한정해 잠정적 견해로 표시한다. A는 확실성을 과장했다('demonstrated'). 엄밀히는 과잉 일반화라기보다 확실성 과장이지만 체크리스트 3번은 충족으로 본다. B는 사실을 'seems'로 약화했고, C는 출처를 잘못 돌렸다. 다만 선택지 네 개가 거의 같은 문장이고 차이가 한두 단어(seems, demonstrated, 내용 교체)뿐이라, 표지어만 대조하면 풀린다. 독서모임 통계(60%)는 확실성 대비를 위한 방해 정보로 넣은 것으로 보이지만 어느 선택지에도 쓰이지 않는다. 그래서 확실성 구분을 넘는 여러 출처 종합이나 목적 범위 판단은 실제로 요구되지 않는다. 전형적인 medium 수준이다.

- Years before the story begins, one of Lucia's students, a boy named Tonio, drowned during a typhoon crossing.
- At Tonio's funeral, Lucia promised his mother that she would one day teach his younger sister to read.

The student wants to explain why a certain character's arrival carries special weight for the protagonist. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

- Its protagonist, Lucia Ramos, teaches aboard a boat that serves as a floating school for children on small islands in the Visayas.
- Years before the story begins, one of Lucia's students, a boy named Tonio, drowned during a typhoon crossing.
- At Tonio's funeral, Lucia promised his mother that she would one day teach his younger sister to read.
- In the story's central scene, Tonio's sister, now twelve, appears at the door of Lucia's classroom on the boat.
problem.question: The student wants to explain why a certain character's arrival carries special weight for the protagonist. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: When Tonio's sister appears at the door of her floating classroom, Lucia is suddenly faced with the vow she made years earlier to the drowned boy's mother: to teach the girl to read.
When Tonio's sister, now twelve, appears at the door of the classroom, the story reaches its central scene aboard Lucia's school boat.
When Marisol Abad published "The Tide Ledger" in 2019, its protagonist, Lucia Ramos, taught aboard a floating school serving islands in the Visayas.
When Tonio's sister appears at the door of her floating classroom, Lucia recalls promising the girl herself, at Tonio's funeral, that she would teach her to swim.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 소녀가 교실 문 앞에 나타난 장면과 몇 년 전 Tonio의 어머니에게 '여동생에게 글을 가르치겠다'고 한 약속을 결합해, 이 등장이 Lucia에게 왜 특별한 무게를 지니는지(지키지 못한 약속을 마주하게 됨)를 설명한다.
B: 등장 장면 하나만 담았다. 약속에 대한 언급이 없어서 그 등장이 왜 중요한지는 설명하지 못하므로 목표를 절반만 달성한다.
C: 출판 연도와 Lucia의 직업이라는 두 사실을 합쳤지만, 둘 다 소녀의 등장이 지니는 의미와는 관계가 없다.
D: 노트와 다른 내용이다. 약속한 상대는 소녀가 아니라 어머니였고, 약속 내용도 수영이 아니라 글 읽기였다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer A: It joins two separate notes. One is the girl showing up at the classroom door. The other is Lucia's earlier promise to Tonio's mother to teach his sister to read. Put together, they explain why the arrival matters so much: it forces Lucia to face that unfulfilled vow.
B: This choice only gives the scene where the girl arrives. Without the promise, it never explains why her arrival matters to Lucia, so it only does half the job.
C: This choice combines two facts, the publication year and Lucia's job, but neither one has anything to do with why the girl's arrival is significant.
D: This choice changes what the notes say. Lucia made the promise to the mother, not to the girl, and she promised to teach reading, not swimming.

hardJudge.note: A는 등장 장면(노트5)과 익사 사건(노트3)·장례식 약속(노트4)을 결합해 '왜 무게가 있는가'라는 인과적 목표를 충족. B는 등장+중심 장면만 담아 의미 설명 부재(한쪽만), C는 목표와 무관한 배경 사실 조합(시제 왜곡도 있음), D는 약속 상대·내용을 노트와 다르게 변형. 해설은 각 선택지 판정 근거를 정확히 제시하며 모순 없음. '지키지 못한 약속'은 '아직 이행되지 않은 약속'으로 읽히므로 노트와 충돌하지 않음. 가상 작품·작가로 저작권 문제 없음. 세 개 노트를 서사적 인과로 묶어야 하고 B가 '중심 장면'이라는 표면 단서로 유혹하는 점에서 medium 이상의 통합 사고 요구.

advisory.note: '등장 장면 + 약속'을 결합하는 전형적인 medium 구조입니다. 오답 B는 사실 하나만 담았고, C는 목표와 무관한 사실을 담았으며, D는 노트와 다른 내용을 담아 셋 다 쉽게 제거됩니다. 확실성 수준 판단이나 관계 방향 판단 같은 hard 특성은 없고, 여러 사실을 종합하는 것도 2개 수준에 그칩니다.

problem.explanation:

A(지나치게 세부적): 여정의 경로와 원인(주 2회 운항)만 자세히 전달할 뿐, 비평가의 해석이라는 핵심이 빠져 있다.
C(지나치게 포괄적): 수상 경력, 등장인물, 줄거리를 두루 개관하지만 여정이 섬에 관해 무엇을 드러내는지는 말하지 않아 초점을 잃었다.
D(무관한 항목 강조): 매점의 물품과 낡은 지도는 쇠퇴를 암시할 수는 있지만 디미트리의 여정이나 비평가의 견해와는 관련이 없다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer B: Your goal is to emphasize what critics think Dimitri's trip reveals about the setting. B ties the trip (eighteen hours, for a postcard) to the critics' reading of it (the island is slowly disappearing from shipping schedules), so it does exactly that.
A (too detailed): It explains the route and why the trip takes so long (the ferry runs only twice a week), but it leaves out the critics' interpretation, which is the whole point of the goal.
C (too broad): It surveys the prize, the main character, and the plot, but it never says what the trip reveals about the island, so it loses focus.
D (irrelevant note): The kiosk's goods and faded maps may hint at decline, but they have nothing to do with Dimitri's journey or with what critics say about it.

hardJudge.note: 목표(비평가의 해석 + 여정 + 배경)를 충족하는 선택지는 B뿐이며, 여정 사실(18시간, 엽서)과 비평 노트를 결합해야 하므로 통합이 요구된다. D는 '배경의 쇠퇴'를 암시하는 세부(낡은 지도)로 그럴듯한 유인을 제공해 목표 범위(비평가의 견해·여정)를 정확히 읽어야 배제할 수 있다. 다만 B가 비평가 노트를 거의 그대로 재진술하므로 난이도 상승 폭은 중간 정도이며, '비평가' 언급 유무만으로도 정답이 식별될 수 있다는 점에서 hard로서는 다소 약한 편이다. 가상의 작품·작가로 사실 오류·저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 B만 'critics'와 해석을 담고 있어 키워드 매칭으로 바로 고를 수 있다. A는 그럴듯한 오답이지만 critics가 없어서 쉽게 제외된다. D의 지도는 쇠퇴를 암시하는 미끼이긴 하나 여정과 관계가 없다. 결국 전형적인 medium 수준이고, 확실성 구분이나 관계 방향 판단 같은 추가 사고를 요구하지 않는다.

problem.passage:
For six summers, Werner had left a basket of runner beans on the low fence between his allotment and Sibylle's every Saturday, and every Saturday she had returned it filled with red currants. This July the exchange went on, but neither of them stayed to talk; the basket simply appeared on the fence and later disappeared. Werner's beds now produced far more than he could eat, and Sibylle, who had planted her own beans in May, no longer needed his. ______ he kept filling the basket each week, not for the sake of what it held but because setting it on the fence was the only thing he still knew how to say to her.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: For six summers, Werner had left a basket of runner beans on the low fence between his allotment and Sibylle's every Saturday, and every Saturday she had returned it filled with red currants. This July the exchange went on, but neither of them stayed to talk; the basket simply appeared on the fence and later disappeared. Werner's beds now produced far more than he could eat, and Sibylle, who had planted her own beans in May, no longer needed his. ______ he kept filling the basket each week, not for the sake of what it held but because setting it on the fence was the only thing he still knew how to say to her.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Accordingly,
Instead,
Still,
For example,
problem.explanation:
정답 C(Still,). 바로 앞 문장은 바구니를 계속 채울 실용적인 이유가 사라졌다는 점을 보여 준다. 시빌레는 이제 자기 콩을 직접 길러서 베르너의 콩이 더 이상 필요 없다. 그런데도 베르너는 바구니를 계속 채운다. 마지막 문장이 강조하는 것은 채소 자체가 아니라 둘 사이의 관계를 이어 가려는 의도다. 따라서 '그렇다 하더라도'라는 양보의 뜻을 가진 Still이 가장 자연스럽다.
A(Accordingly,): '수확이 남아돌아서 그 결과 바구니를 채웠다'는 인과로 읽으면 앞 문장의 부수적 사실(남는 수확)과는 맞는 것처럼 보인다. 하지만 마지막 문장은 '담긴 것 때문이 아니다(not for the sake of what it held)'라고 그 이유를 직접 부정하므로, 지문의 핵심 강조점과 어긋난다.
B(Instead,): 앞 내용과 대비된다는 방향은 맞는다. 그러나 Instead는 앞의 행동을 다른 행동으로 바꿀 때 쓰는 대체 관계를 나타낸다. 이 지문에서는 베르너가 무언가를 그만두고 다른 일을 한 것이 아니라 하던 일을 그대로 계속하므로 논리 관계가 맞지 않는다.
D(For example,): 마지막 문장은 앞 문장의 사례가 아니다. 앞 내용과 전혀 다른 성격의 연결이다.
problem.explanationEn:
The answer is C (Still,). The sentence before the blank removes every practical reason to keep filling the basket: Sibylle now grows her own beans and no longer needs Werner's. Even so, he keeps filling it. The last sentence stresses that the basket matters as a way to stay in touch with her, not as a way to share food. "Still" expresses this "even so" contrast.
A (Accordingly,) is wrong. It treats his extra harvest as the cause, which fits a side detail in the text. But the last sentence says he fills the basket "not for the sake of what it held," which rejects that reason directly.
B (Instead,) is wrong. It does signal a contrast, but it means one action replaces another. Werner doesn't swap one action for another; he keeps doing the same thing.
D (For example,) is wrong. The last sentence isn't an example of anything said earlier.

hardJudge.note: 앞 문장에 '수확이 남아돈다'(Accordingly 유인)와 '시빌레가 더 이상 필요 없다'(핵심 양보 관계) 두 정보가 공존하고, 마지막 문장의 'not for the sake of what it held'가 인과 독해를 직접 배제하므로 Still만 성립. Instead는 대체 관계라 방향 오류, For example은 예시 아님. 해설은 정답과 오답 근거를 정확히 뒷받침하며 모순 없음. 문장이 다소 길지만 어휘는 평이하고 난이도는 논리 선별에서 발생함.

advisory.note: 앞 문장에는 Werner의 남는 수확과 Sibylle에게 더는 콩이 필요 없다는 두 사실이 함께 나온다. 남는 수확을 근거로 삼으면 Accordingly(인과)가 그럴듯해 보이는 함정이 된다. 그러나 이유를 'not for the sake of what it held'로 직접 부정하는 구절이 있어 핵심 강조점은 양보(Still)다. Instead는 대비 방향은 맞지만 대체 관계여서 틀리고, D는 예시 관계라 맞지 않는다. 어휘와 문장 길이는 적절하다. 정답은 유일하며 해설도 정확하다.

problem.passage:
Years ago, Priya and Rajesh had traded jokes on this garden bench while the pickers' baskets filled on the slopes below. Now, as mist drifted up from the valley and a kettle whistled somewhere in the line rooms, the widow and her former supervisor sat with a measured gap between them. Rajesh, who once interrupted her freely, waited until she had finished every sentence before speaking; he intended this restraint as a mark of respect for her grief. ______ to Priya, each of his careful pauses felt like a door being quietly closed.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: Years ago, Priya and Rajesh had traded jokes on this garden bench while the pickers' baskets filled on the slopes below. Now, as mist drifted up from the valley and a kettle whistled somewhere in the line rooms, the widow and her former supervisor sat with a measured gap between them. Rajesh, who once interrupted her freely, waited until she had finished every sentence before speaking; he intended this restraint as a mark of respect for her grief. ______ to Priya, each of his careful pauses felt like a door being quietly closed.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Consequently,
Even so,
In other words,
Meanwhile,
problem.explanation:
정답 B(Even so,): 바로 앞 문장의 핵심은 결과가 아니라 Rajesh의 '의도'다. 그는 자제를 슬픔에 대한 존중으로 의도했다. 그런데 마지막 문장에서 Priya는 그 침묵을 문이 닫히는 것처럼 받아들인다. 선의의 의도와 상대가 받은 상처가 어긋나므로, 앞의 내용을 인정하면서 대조하는 'Even so'가 맞다.
A(Consequently,): 그의 멈춤이 Priya가 받은 인상을 낳았다는 인과 관계로 표면적으로는 들어맞는다. 하지만 '존중하려는 의도' 때문에 '거부당한 느낌'이 생겼다고 하면 의도와 결과 사이의 엇갈림이라는 지문의 핵심이 사라진다.
C(In other words,): 두 문장 모두 그의 조심스러움을 다룬다는 점은 맞다. 하지만 마지막 문장은 앞 문장을 바꿔 말한 것이 아니다. 존중과 닫힌 문은 서로 반대되는 해석이다.
D(Meanwhile,): 안개나 주전자 소리 같은 배경 묘사와 '동시에 일어나는 일'로 잇게 만드는 함정이다. 마지막 문장은 별개의 사건이 아니라 바로 앞에 나온 그의 행동을 Priya가 어떻게 받아들였는지를 말한다.
problem.explanationEn:
B (Even so,) is correct. The key point of the previous sentence isn't what Rajesh does. It's why he does it: he means his restraint as respect for Priya's grief. The final sentence shows Priya experiencing that same restraint as a door quietly closing. His kind intention clashes with the hurt she feels, so you need a transition that accepts the first idea and then contrasts it. That's "Even so."
A (Consequently,) is tempting because his pauses really do cause her impression. But a cause-and-effect link hides the gap between his respectful intent and the rejection she feels, and that gap is the whole point.
C (In other words,) wrongly treats the last sentence as a restatement. "Respect" and "a closing door" are opposite readings of the same behavior.
D (Meanwhile,) points you back to the background details (the mist, the kettle) and suggests something happening at the same time. The last sentence actually describes how Priya reacts to Rajesh's behavior from the previous sentence.

hardJudge.note: 앞 문장의 강조점이 '행동의 결과'가 아니라 '의도(존중)'임을 파악해야 하며, 의도와 수용의 어긋남이라는 함축적 대조를 'Even so'로 잇는 구조가 타당함. D(Meanwhile)는 안개·주전자 등 배경 묘사와 동시성으로 연결되는 부수적 함정, A(Consequently)는 인과 방향 오류로 체크리스트 3·4를 각각 충족. 지문은 문학적이나 어휘·문장 길이가 과도하지 않음. 해설의 선택지별 근거도 정답과 일관됨.

advisory.note: 정답 B는 옳다. 그러나 '의도는 존중이었다'와 '닫히는 문처럼 느껴졌다'의 대비가 너무 명시적이어서, 이 문항은 전형적인 medium 수준의 양보·대조 문제에 가깝다. D(Meanwhile)는 배경 묘사와의 연결이 약해 함정으로서 끌어당기는 힘이 낮다. A(Consequently)만 어느 정도 그럴듯한 오답이다. 의도와 수용의 어긋남이 약하게나마 hard 요소이지만 추가 추론 부담은 작다.

problem.passage:
This season, Amara lowered each length of cloth into the indigo vats more slowly than his apprentices had ever seen him do, often stopping over the dark water as if he had lost track of the next step. Yet by the week's end, Youssef and Hamid could tell whether a vat was ready by its smell alone, something no earlier group of apprentices had learned before spring. ______ the old man's pauses had never been lapses at all: each one had been a lesson, held open long enough for the young men to step inside it.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: This season, Amara lowered each length of cloth into the indigo vats more slowly than his apprentices had ever seen him do, often stopping over the dark water as if he had lost track of the next step. Yet by the week's end, Youssef and Hamid could tell whether a vat was ready by its smell alone, something no earlier group of apprentices had learned before spring. ______ the old man's pauses had never been lapses at all: each one had been a lesson, held open long enough for the young men to step inside it.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Regrettably,
Nevertheless,
Evidently,
Meanwhile,
problem.explanation:
지문의 두 관찰은 서로 맞지 않는 것처럼 보인다. 하나는 아마라의 손이 유난히 느려지고 자주 멈췄다는 점(쇠퇴처럼 보임), 다른 하나는 제자들이 이전 어느 기수보다 빨리 숙련에 도달했다는 점이다. 마지막 문장은 두 관찰을 합쳐서 '그 멈춤은 실수가 아니라 가르침이었다'는 결론을 내린다. 따라서 앞의 증거에서 결론을 끌어내는 'Evidently,'(C)가 정답이다.
A 'Regrettably,'는 첫 번째 관찰(느려짐=노쇠)만 반영해 안타까움을 표현한다. 하지만 마지막 문장은 멈춤이 실수가 '아니었다'고 긍정적으로 다시 해석하므로 어조와 논리가 맞지 않는다.
B 'Nevertheless,'는 두 관찰이 상반된다는 점만 보고 단순 대조로 처리한 것이다. 마지막 문장은 앞 내용에 맞서는 진술이 아니라 두 관찰을 하나로 묶어 설명하는 결론이다.
D 'Meanwhile,'는 동시에 일어난 별개의 일을 덧붙일 때 쓴다. 앞의 증거에서 나온 결론과는 관계가 없다.
problem.explanationEn:
The text gives two observations that seem to clash. First, Amara works unusually slowly and keeps pausing, which looks like decline. Second, his apprentices master the craft faster than any earlier group. The last sentence puts these together and concludes that his pauses were never mistakes but lessons. "Evidently," is the right choice because it signals a conclusion drawn from the evidence before it.
A, "Regrettably," only reflects the first observation, reading the slowness as sad decline. But the final sentence says the pauses were NOT lapses, so the regretful tone doesn't fit.
B, "Nevertheless," treats the two observations as a simple contrast. The final sentence doesn't push back against what came before; it explains both observations at once.
D, "Meanwhile," adds a separate event happening at the same time. It has nothing to do with drawing a conclusion from the evidence.

hardJudge.note: 두 관찰(느려진 손놀림 vs. 제자들의 이례적 빠른 숙련)을 종합해 '멈춤=가르침'이라는 재해석 결론을 끌어내는 구조로, 'Evidently,'가 유일하게 성립. 'Nevertheless'는 2문장의 'Yet'과 중첩된 표면 대조를 유혹하는 적절한 오답이며, 'Regrettably'는 첫 관찰만 반영한 어조 오류, 'Meanwhile'은 시간적 병렬로 부적합. 해설은 정답·오답 근거를 정확히 서술하고 모순 없음. 원문 창작으로 저작권 의심 없음. 'Amara'를 남성(his, the old man)으로 지칭한 것은 일관되어 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 두 관찰(노쇠처럼 보이는 멈춤과 전례 없이 빠른 숙련)을 종합해서 '멈춤은 가르침이었다'는 재해석 결론에 이르러야 한다. 지문에 Yet이 이미 있어서 Nevertheless가 그럴듯한 오답이 된다. Evidently는 증거를 바탕으로 결론을 내리는 전환어로 정답이 유일하다. 빈칸 뒤 문장의 첫 단어 'the'가 소문자인데, 전환어 뒤에 오므로 문법상 문제없다.

problem.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Eight-year-old Waylon is resting with a group of adult hikers at a trail shelter in the Appalachian Mountains.

The bird lay beside the woodpile, one wing bent at a wrong angle. Waylon crouched over it while the grown-ups unpacked their stoves. "Leave it," his uncle said without looking. "Nature takes care of its own." Waylon did not leave it. He cupped his hands around the small body, and he stayed there long after the others had begun to talk about tomorrow's climb.

A literary critic argues that Waylon's intense focus on the injured bird reflects his own sense of being ignored by the adults around him.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's interpretation?
problem.stimulus:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Eight-year-old Waylon is resting with a group of adult hikers at a trail shelter in the Appalachian Mountains.

The bird lay beside the woodpile, one wing bent at a wrong angle. Waylon crouched over it while the grown-ups unpacked their stoves. "Leave it," his uncle said without looking. "Nature takes care of its own." Waylon did not leave it. He cupped his hands around the small body, and he stayed there long after the others had begun to talk about tomorrow's climb.

A literary critic argues that Waylon's intense focus on the injured bird reflects his own sense of being ignored by the adults around him.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's interpretation?
options: Later in the story, Waylon whispers to the bird that the grown-ups never listen to him either.
Later in the story, the adults spend the evening discussing which route up the mountain will be safest.
Later in the story, a hiker identifies the bird as a type of wren that is common in the Appalachian region.
In an interview, the author says she hiked Appalachian trails often when she was a child.
problem.explanation: 비평가의 주장은 새에 대한 Waylon의 집착이 어른들에게 무시당한다는 그 자신의 감정을 반영한다는 것이다. A는 Waylon이 새에게 어른들이 자기 말도 듣지 않는다고 속삭이는 장면으로, 새의 처지와 자신의 소외감을 직접 연결하므로 주장을 뒷받침한다. B는 어른들의 대화 주제만 보여 줄 뿐 Waylon의 감정과 새를 연결하지 않는다. C는 새의 종류에 관한 정보로 Waylon의 심리와 무관하다. D는 작가의 경험에 관한 것이어서 등장인물의 감정에 대한 해석을 뒷받침하지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: The critic claims that Waylon's focus on the bird reflects his own feeling of being ignored by adults. Choice A shows Waylon telling the bird that the grown-ups never listen to him either, which directly links the bird's situation to his own sense of being overlooked, so it supports the claim. Choice B only shows what the adults talk about and says nothing about how Waylon feels or why he cares about the bird. Choice C identifies the bird's species, which has nothing to do with Waylon's emotions. Choice D is about the author's life, not about the character's feelings, so it can't support this interpretation.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On an Appalachian trail shelter, eight-year-old Waylon notices an injured songbird that all the adults dismiss, his urgent attention to its suffering both tender and troubling.

hardJudge.note: 비평가 주장(새에 대한 집착 = 어른에게 무시당하는 감정의 반영)을 가장 직접 뒷받침하는 것은 A뿐이다. A는 Waylon 자신이 "어른들은 내 말도 듣지 않는다(either)"고 새에게 말하며 새의 처지와 자신의 소외감을 명시적으로 연결한다. B는 어른들이 Waylon을 배제한다는 정황은 암시할 수 있으나 Waylon의 감정이나 새와의 연결을 보여주지 않는 전형적 오답, C는 무관한 사실 정보, D는 작가 전기 정보로 해석과 무관하다. 해설(한·영) 모두 정답·선택지 참조가 일치하고 모순 없음. 단일 개념(주장-근거 연결)으로 한 단계 추론, 평이한 어휘·문장으로 easy에 적합. 저작권·사실 오류 의심 없음.

advisory.note: A만 새와 Waylon 자신의 소외감을 직접 연결한다('either'). B는 어른들이 자기들끼리만 관심을 둔다는 점을 보여 주므로 그럴듯한 오답이지만 Waylon의 감정은 다루지 않는다. C는 새에 관한 사실일 뿐이고, D는 작가의 경력이라는 전형적 함정이다. 규칙 하나로 한 단계 만에 풀 수 있어 easy에 맞다.

problem.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Asha, a young girl, is traveling with her grandmother on a houseboat in the backwaters of Kerala, India, a few weeks after her grandfather's death.

At dawn the water was the color of weak tea. Asha woke to find her grandmother already at the edge of the deck, holding a brass bowl of marigold and jasmine petals. Asha had expected her to cry, as she had at the funeral. Instead, her grandmother scattered the petals one handful at a time and watched them drift away with the slow current toward the palms. She did not try to call them back. Asha sat very still beside her. No one had been able to explain to her why the house now felt calm instead of broken, but watching the petals go, she thought she finally understood.

A student claims that in the text, Asha comes to understand acceptance by watching her grandmother rather than by being told about it. Which quotation from the text most directly supports this claim?
problem.stimulus:

At dawn the water was the color of weak tea. Asha woke to find her grandmother already at the edge of the deck, holding a brass bowl of marigold and jasmine petals. problem.question: A student claims that in the text, Asha comes to understand acceptance by watching her grandmother rather than by being told about it. Which quotation from the text most directly supports this claim?
options: "At dawn the water was the color of weak tea."
"No one had been able to explain to her why the house now felt calm instead of broken, but watching the petals go, she thought she finally understood."
"Asha had expected her to cry, as she had at the funeral."
"Asha woke to find her grandmother already at the edge of the deck, holding a brass bowl of marigold and jasmine petals."
problem.explanation: 이 주장은 두 가지를 말한다. Asha가 무언가를 이해하게 된다는 점, 그리고 그 이해가 누군가의 설명이 아니라 지켜보는 것에서 온다는 점이다. B는 아무도 설명해 주지 못했다는 내용과 꽃잎이 떠내려가는 것을 보며 마침내 이해했다는 내용을 함께 담고 있어 두 가지를 모두 뒷받침한다. A는 배경 묘사일 뿐이다. C는 Asha의 예상만 보여 줄 뿐 무엇을 이해했는지는 드러내지 않는다. D는 할머니를 처음 보는 장면이지만 이해나 설명에 관한 내용이 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The claim has two parts: Asha comes to understand something, and that understanding comes from watching, not from being told. B covers both parts. It says no one had been able to explain things to her, and that she finally understood while watching the petals float away. A only describes the setting. C shows what Asha expected, but it does not show that she understood anything. D shows Asha first seeing her grandmother, but it says nothing about understanding or explanation.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Aboard a Kerala backwater houseboat, child Asha watches her grandmother scatter flower petals at dawn and understands something about acceptance that no adult voice can articulate.

hardJudge.note: B는 주장의 두 요소(설명 받지 못함 + 지켜보며 이해함)를 모두 명시적으로 담고 있어 정답이 명확함. 오답은 배경(A), 기대(C), 첫 장면(D)으로 전형적인 오개념 유형이며 D가 '할머니를 봄'이라는 점에서 적당히 그럴듯함. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답과 선택지 참조가 일치하고 모순 없음. 지문은 창작물로 보이며 저작권 의심 없음. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나 easy에 적합.

advisory.note: B만 '설명받지 못함'과 '지켜보며 이해함'을 모두 직접 담고 있다. 오답들은 지문에 나오는 그럴듯한 문장이지만 주장의 핵심 요소가 빠져 있다. 단서가 겉으로 드러나 있고 한 단계 추론으로 풀리므로 easy 난이도에 맞다. 다만 B가 주장 속 표현을 거의 그대로 따라 써서 조금 쉬운 편이다.

problem.passage:
In a California mining camp in 1851, Ezra receives the pocket watch that belonged to his late brother, Silas. When he pries open the back cover, he finds a few pressed blue flowers and a slip of paper listing a set of coordinates. Ezra checks the coordinates against every claim map in the camp office, but none of the maps shows any claim at that spot. Silas had spent his last months walking alone into the hills each week and coming back without saying where he had gone. Because the coordinates match no recorded claim, Ezra concludes that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: In a California mining camp in 1851, Ezra receives the pocket watch that belonged to his late brother, Silas. When he pries open the back cover, he finds a few pressed blue flowers and a slip of paper listing a set of coordinates. Ezra checks the coordinates against every claim map in the camp office, but none of the maps shows any claim at that spot. Silas had spent his last months walking alone into the hills each week and coming back without saying where he had gone. Because the coordinates match no recorded claim, Ezra concludes that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: Silas must have bought the watch from another miner who had already filed a claim at that location.
the coordinates must point to the camp office, where Silas had kept the claim maps.
Silas may have found a site that he never officially registered with the camp.
the blue flowers must have been picked from land that already appeared on the camp's claim maps.
problem.explanation: 지문의 핵심 단서는 좌표가 캠프의 어떤 채굴권 지도에도 나오지 않는다는 점이다. 기록된 채굴권이 없으니, Silas가 공식 등록하지 않은 장소를 찾았을 수 있다는 C가 가장 논리적인 결론이다. A는 '이미 등록된 채굴권'이 있다고 하는데, 이는 지도에 아무 기록도 없다는 사실과 맞지 않는다. B는 캠프 사무실이 좌표의 위치라고 하지만, 사무실은 좌표를 확인한 곳일 뿐 좌표가 가리키는 곳은 아니다. D 역시 해당 땅이 지도에 이미 나와 있다고 하므로 지문의 단서와 정면으로 충돌한다.
problem.explanationEn: The key clue is that the coordinates do not match any claim on the camp's maps. If no claim was recorded there, the most logical conclusion is that Silas may have found a site he never officially registered, which is choice C. Choice A says someone had already filed a claim at that location, but that contradicts the fact that no map shows a claim there. Choice B treats the camp office as the place the coordinates point to, but the office is only where Ezra checked the maps. Choice D says the land already appeared on the claim maps, which also directly contradicts the passage.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In a California Gold Rush camp, prospector Ezra inherits his brother's pocket watch and discovers it contains dried flowers and coordinates to an unmapped claim.

hardJudge.note: 지문 단서(좌표가 어떤 채굴권 지도에도 없음 + Silas가 홀로 산에 다님)에서 한 단계 추론으로 C가 도출됨. A·D는 '이미 등록된 채굴권'을 전제해 지문과 정면 충돌, B는 좌표의 대상을 혼동한 오개념형 오답. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답 및 선택지 참조가 일치하고 모순 없음. 영어 해설 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 1851년 캘리포니아 광산 캠프·채굴권 지도 설정에 사실 오류 없음. 원문 창작으로 보이며 저작권 의심 없음. easy 난이도에 적합.

advisory.note: 단서 하나(좌표와 일치하는 기록된 채굴권이 없음)로 C를 고를 수 있고 추론은 한 단계다. C의 'may have'는 적절히 신중한 표현이다. A, D는 지도 기록과 정반대 내용이고 B는 장소를 혼동했다. 모두 그럴듯한 오개념형 오답이다.

problem.passage:
For eleven years, tram conductor Neves had considered the passenger Vitor a know-it-all who could not stop criticizing how she drove the old No. 28 car up the hills of Lisbon. Vitor, a retired clockmaker, had always assumed Neves had no real understanding of the machine she operated. Then one rainy morning the tram stalled halfway up a steep street, its brakes locked. Neves knew exactly which lever to hold, and Vitor knew how to free the stuck gear with his pocket tools; working side by side, they had the car moving in ten minutes. As the passengers cheered, Neves and Vitor looked at each other in surprise, and each realized that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: For eleven years, tram conductor Neves had considered the passenger Vitor a know-it-all who could not stop criticizing how she drove the old No. 28 car up the hills of Lisbon. Vitor, a retired clockmaker, had always assumed Neves had no real understanding of the machine she operated. Then one rainy morning the tram stalled halfway up a steep street, its brakes locked. Neves knew exactly which lever to hold, and Vitor knew how to free the stuck gear with his pocket tools; working side by side, they had the car moving in ten minutes. As the passengers cheered, Neves and Vitor looked at each other in surprise, and each realized that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the other had been right all along to doubt their skill with the tram.
the other would probably never ride or drive the No. 28 car again.
the other cared more about the cheering passengers than about the tram.
the other was far more capable than they had believed for years.
problem.explanation: 지문은 두 사람이 11년간 서로를 무능하다고 여겼지만, 고장 상황에서 각자의 전문성(레버 조작, 기어 수리)으로 함께 문제를 해결했다고 말한다. 따라서 둘이 놀라며 깨달은 것은 상대가 생각보다 훨씬 유능하다는 점이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 서로의 실력을 의심한 것이 옳았다는 내용으로, 성공적인 협력과 반대된다. B는 앞으로 전차를 타거나 운전하지 않는다는 근거가 지문에 없다. C는 승객의 환호에 대한 관심을 다루지만, 그들의 놀람은 상대의 능력에 관한 것이다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says Neves and Vitor spent eleven years thinking the other was incompetent, but when the tram broke down, each used real expertise (the lever, the gear) to fix it together. So their surprise shows they realized the other was much more skilled than they had thought, which makes D correct. A says their doubts were justified, which is the opposite of what their successful teamwork shows. B has no support, since nothing suggests either of them will stop riding or driving the tram. C is about the passengers' cheering, but their surprise is about each other's ability.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On a Lisbon tram line, conductor Neves and passenger Vitor spend years dismissing each other as incompetent until a mechanical failure forces them to collaborate brilliantly.

hardJudge.note: 지문의 "surprise"와 11년간의 상호 불신 → 성공적 협력이라는 명시적 단서로 D가 한 단계 추론으로 도출됨. A는 지문과 정반대, B·C는 근거 없음이라 규칙을 알면 즉시 배제되나 표면적으로는 그럴듯함. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답 및 오답 배제 근거가 정확하고 일치함. 오리지널 창작 서사로 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 단서(서로에 대한 오랜 오해 → 협력 성공 → 놀람)가 지문에 직접 드러나 있어 한 단계 추론으로 D를 고를 수 있다. 오답 A는 그럴듯한 반대 방향 함정이고, B와 C는 근거가 없다. 다만 Neves가 Vitor의 '능력'을 낮게 봤다는 점은 약간 암시적이다.

problem.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Halvard, a fisherman, sits in a sauna on the Norwegian coast after receiving a package from his daughter, Ingrid, who has not spoken to him in six years.

Halvard turned the gray scarf over in his hands. Years ago he had lent Ingrid money for her first apartment, and she had moved away before paying it back. Now here was a scarf, knitted stitch by stitch, with no letter inside. He decided at once that it must be her way of settling the old loan. Yet the scarf held a pattern of small boats, the same pattern his late wife had knitted into his sweaters every winter, a detail Ingrid could only have chosen with him in mind. Halvard's conclusion about the gift therefore suggests that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Halvard, a fisherman, sits in a sauna on the Norwegian coast after receiving a package from his daughter, Ingrid, who has not spoken to him in six years.

Halvard turned the gray scarf over in his hands. Years ago he had lent Ingrid money for her first apartment, and she had moved away before paying it back. Now here was a scarf, knitted stitch by stitch, with no letter inside. He decided at once that it must be her way of settling the old loan. Yet the scarf held a pattern of small boats, the same pattern his late wife had knitted into his sweaters every winter, a detail Ingrid could only have chosen with him in mind. Halvard's conclusion about the gift therefore suggests that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: he has overlooked a sign that Ingrid may be reaching out to him rather than paying off a debt.
he has noticed that Ingrid copied the pattern because she wanted to sell similar scarves.
he has realized that Ingrid sent the scarf because she plans to borrow more money from him.
he has understood that Ingrid chose the pattern because his wife had asked her to finish it.
problem.explanation: 지문은 Halvard가 목도리를 빚 갚기로 단정하지만, 아내가 그를 위해 짜던 배 무늬가 들어 있어 딸이 아버지를 생각하며 고른 선물임을 보여 준다. 따라서 그의 결론은 화해의 신호를 놓친 것이므로 A가 정답이다. B의 판매 목적은 지문에 근거가 없다. C의 추가 대출 계획도 언급되지 않으며, D의 아내의 부탁은 지문에 없는 내용이다.
problem.explanationEn: Halvard assumes the scarf is repayment for the old loan, but the text points out that it carries the boat pattern his late wife knitted for him, which Ingrid could only have chosen with him in mind. That means his conclusion misses a sign that she may be reaching out to him, so A is correct. B is wrong because nothing in the text mentions selling scarves. C is wrong because the text never says she plans to borrow more money. D is wrong because the text never says his wife asked Ingrid to finish anything.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In a Norwegian coastal sauna, fisherman Halvard receives a hand-knitted scarf from his estranged daughter and assumes it's debt repayment rather than wordless reconciliation.

hardJudge.note: 검산: Halvard는 목도리를 빚 상환으로 단정하지만, 지문은 아내가 그를 위해 짜던 배 무늬를 "Ingrid could only have chosen with him in mind"라고 명시하여 그의 결론이 딸의 화해 신호를 놓쳤음을 직접 뒷받침한다 → A 옳음. B(판매), C(추가 대출), D(아내의 부탁)는 지문에 근거가 없는 전형적 과잉 추론 오답으로, 규칙(지문 근거 기반 추론)을 알면 바로 배제되나 대출·아내 언급과 표면적으로 연결되어 그럴듯함. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 A를 일관되게 지지하고 글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 단서가 지문에 명시적으로 드러나는 한 단계 추론으로 easy에 적합. 원작 출처 추정 불가, 창작 지문으로 보임.

advisory.note: 'Yet'으로 바로 이어지는 대조 단서 하나로 A가 확정된다. 오답 B·C·D는 지문에 없는 동기를 덧붙인 선택지라 제외하기는 쉽지만, 그럴듯한 함정으로 볼 수 있다. 다만 B·C·D는 모두 Halvard가 무언가를 '알아챘다'고 진술하는데, 이는 그가 성급하게 내린 결론과 맞지 않는다. 그래서 다소 쉽게 배제될 수 있다. 서두의 사우나 설정은 내용과 상관없지만 문제가 되지는 않는다.

problem.passage:
The following text is adapted from a 2019 novel. In 1936, Jonas Brandt, an elderly widower, is on his Nebraska farm.

The envelope had come through three post offices before it found him, and the handwriting on it was unsteady. Jonas read the letter standing by the windmill. Walt Sorensen, who had worked as a hired hand on the Brandt place in the summer of 1889, was alive in Montana. "I kept to what we said by the creek," Walt wrote. "Every spring I planted one cottonwood for each year since. There are forty-seven now." Jonas folded the page and looked across his own yard, where no tree had stood for a long time. He had made the same promise, and the drought and the bank had taken the place he had meant to plant. He laughed once, quietly, and then he did not laugh again.

A literary scholar argues that in this scene the letter works as both a comfort and a rebuke to Jonas: Walt's faithfulness to the pact pleases him, but it also makes him face the fact that he broke his own word.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the scholar's interpretation?
problem.stimulus:
The following text is adapted from a 2019 novel. In 1936, Jonas Brandt, an elderly widower, is on his Nebraska farm.

The envelope had come through three post offices before it found him, and the handwriting on it was unsteady. Jonas read the letter standing by the windmill. Walt Sorensen, who had worked as a hired hand on the Brandt place in the summer of 1889, was alive in Montana. "I kept to what we said by the creek," Walt wrote. "Every spring I planted one cottonwood for each year since. There are forty-seven now." Jonas folded the page and looked across his own yard, where no tree had stood for a long time. He had made the same promise, and the drought and the bank had taken the place he had meant to plant. He laughed once, quietly, and then he did not laugh again.

A literary scholar argues that in this scene the letter works as both a comfort and a rebuke to Jonas: Walt's faithfulness to the pact pleases him, but it also makes him face the fact that he broke his own word.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the scholar's interpretation?
options: In the author's notebook, a note on the letter scene reads: "Jonas should feel only warmth here—proof at last that his old friend survived the hard years."
In the author's notebook, a note on the letter scene reads: "Walt's trees are a gift to Jonas and a measure of him at once—he cannot be glad for one without counting the other."
In the author's notebook, a note on a later chapter reads: "Jonas's abandoned promise should come back to trouble him again and again until the last page."
In the author's notebook, a note on the novel's background reads: "My grandfather spent the 1890s working as a hired hand on farms across the Dakotas."
problem.explanation:
학자의 해석은 두 요소로 이루어진다. ① 편지가 주는 위안(Walt가 약속을 지켜서 기쁨)과 ② 그 위안이 동시에 질책이 됨(Jonas 자신의 깨진 약속을 마주하게 함). 이 둘이 같은 장면에서 함께 작동한다는 주장이다. B는 편지 장면에 관한 메모에서 Walt의 나무를 '선물'이자 '자신을 재는 척도'라고 부르고, 한쪽 없이 다른 쪽도 느낄 수 없다고 적고 있어 두 요소를 모두, 그리고 서로 연결된 것으로 담아낸다. 그래서 정답이다.
A: 위안 쪽만 반영한다. 게다가 'only warmth'라고 해서 질책의 요소를 오히려 배제하므로 해석을 약화한다.
C: 질책(깨진 약속) 쪽만 반영한다. 그것도 편지 장면이 아니라 이후 장(章)에 관한 메모라서, 이 장면에서 위안과 질책이 함께 나타난다는 점을 보여 주지 못한다.
D: 작가의 가족사라는, 해석과 무관한 제3의 요소를 끌어온다. 장면이 Jonas에게 어떤 의미인지에 대해서는 아무것도 알려 주지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn:
The scholar's claim has two parts that must work together in this scene: (1) the letter comforts Jonas because Walt kept the pact, and (2) it also rebukes him because it forces him to face his own broken promise. Choice B is correct because its note is about the letter scene itself. It calls Walt's trees both a "gift" and "a measure" of Jonas and says he can't feel one without the other, so it covers both parts and links them.
Choice A covers only the comfort. By saying "only warmth," it actually rules out the rebuke, which weakens the claim.
Choice C covers only the rebuke, and it's about a later chapter, not the letter scene. So it can't show comfort and rebuke happening together here.
Choice D brings in a third factor, the author's family history. That says nothing about what the scene means for Jonas.

hardJudge.note: 지문(Jonas의 '한 번 웃고 다시 웃지 않음'이라는 양가적 반응)과 학자의 2요소 주장(위안+질책)이 정합적이며, B만이 두 요소를 '동시에·상호 연결된' 것으로 담아낸다. A는 'only warmth'로 질책을 배제해 오히려 약화, C는 질책만 다루고 장면도 다른 장(章)이라 범위 불일치(매력적 함정), D는 작가 가족사로 무관. 해설은 각 선택지 판정 근거를 정확히 제시하고 모순 없음. 가상의 작가 노트를 증거로 구성해 주장 범위와 정밀 대조해야 하므로 medium 초과 사고를 요구한다.

advisory.note: 이중 주장(위안+질책)을 모두 담은 B만 정답이다. A는 위안만 담고 'only'로 질책을 배제하며, C는 질책만 담은 데다 이 장면이 아닌 다른 장에 대한 메모다. D는 주장과 관계없는 배경 정보다. 레시피의 '변수'는 해석을 이루는 두 요소로 대응시켜 충족으로 판정했다. B가 해석을 거의 그대로 바꿔 말한 것이라 정답 판별이 다소 쉬울 수 있지만, C의 범위 함정 덕분에 hard 수준은 유지된다.

problem.passage:
In the novel Low Water, the aging fishing guide Cletus poles his skiff along a Louisiana bayou with his reluctant grandson, Remy, naming plants as they pass: "That's yaupon. Boil it when the cough sits deep. That one's elderberry—your grandmama swore by it." Remy rarely answers. Across the novel, these lessons grow longer: early chapters cover one or two plants, while the final chapters cover a dozen or more. Over the same chapters, the narrator describes Cletus as increasingly ill. One literary critic argues that Cletus's growing sense that he is dying is what drives the lengthening lessons. In her reading, each lesson is a farewell disguised as instruction, and the more certain Cletus feels that he is near death, the more he tries to pass on.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's claim about what causes the change in Cletus's lessons?
problem.stimulus: In the novel Low Water, the aging fishing guide Cletus poles his skiff along a Louisiana bayou with his reluctant grandson, Remy, naming plants as they pass: "That's yaupon. Boil it when the cough sits deep. That one's elderberry—your grandmama swore by it." Remy rarely answers. Across the novel, these lessons grow longer: early chapters cover one or two plants, while the final chapters cover a dozen or more. Over the same chapters, the narrator describes Cletus as increasingly ill. One literary critic argues that Cletus's growing sense that he is dying is what drives the lengthening lessons. In her reading, each lesson is a farewell disguised as instruction, and the more certain Cletus feels that he is near death, the more he tries to pass on.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's claim about what causes the change in Cletus's lessons?
options: The novel's final chapter contains the longest lesson in the book, and it is also the chapter in which the narrator describes Cletus as weakest.
After each of the longest lessons, the narrator notes that Cletus has to rest for hours and that his breathing is worse than it was before the lesson began.
In one late chapter, a doctor tells Cletus he is recovering, and that day his lesson covers only a single plant, even though the narrator describes the banks as crowded with plants in bloom.
The later chapters are set in late summer, when the narrator notes that more of the bayou's medicinal plants are in flower and that the heavy heat leaves Cletus short of breath.
problem.explanation:
비평가는 Cletus가 죽음이 가깝다고 느끼는 감각이 수업을 길게 만드는 '원인'이라고 주장한다. 지문이 보여 주는 것은 수업 길이와 병세가 함께 커진다는 상관관계뿐이다. C는 Cletus가 회복 중이라는 말을 들어 죽음에 대한 확신이 약해지자, 이름을 댈 식물이 많았는데도 수업이 식물 하나로 줄었다는 내용이다. 원인(죽음을 예감하는 정도)만 바뀌었을 때 결과(수업 길이)도 함께 바뀌었고, '식물이 많아서'라는 대안 설명도 배제한다. 따라서 인과 주장을 가장 직접적으로 지지한다.
A: 수업이 가장 긴 장과 병세가 가장 심한 장이 겹친다는 상관을 한 번 더 보여 줄 뿐이다. 인과를 확인하지 못하므로 상관을 인과로 오해한 오답이다.
B: 긴 수업이 Cletus를 더 지치게 하고 병을 악화시킨다는 내용이다. 이는 수업이 병세의 원인이라는 반대 방향의 인과를 시사하므로 오답이다.
D: 늦여름이라는 제3의 요인이 꽃이 핀 식물 수(긴 수업)와 더위로 인한 호흡 곤란(병세)을 함께 설명할 수 있다. 오히려 비평가의 인과 주장을 약화시키므로 오답이다.
problem.explanationEn:
The critic claims that Cletus's growing sense that he is dying is what causes his lessons to get longer. The passage only shows a correlation: the lessons get longer as his illness gets worse.

**Why C is correct:** When Cletus is told he is recovering, his sense that death is near weakens, and his lesson shrinks to a single plant. Many plants are in bloom at that moment, so a shortage of plants can't explain the short lesson. Only the proposed cause changed, and the effect changed with it. That makes C the most direct support for the causal claim.

**Why the other options are wrong:**
- **A** just shows the same correlation again: the longest lesson and the weakest Cletus appear in the same chapter. Treating this as proof of cause confuses correlation with causation.
- **B** suggests the lessons themselves wear Cletus out and make him sicker. That reverses the direction of cause.
- **D** offers a third factor, late summer. It could explain both effects: more plants in flower would make the lessons longer, and heavy heat would worsen his breathing. This actually weakens the critic's claim.

hardJudge.note: 지문은 수업 길이 증가와 병세 악화의 동시 발생만 제시하고, 비평가가 '죽음 예감 → 긴 수업'이라는 인과를 주장한다. C는 원인 변수(죽음에 대한 확신)만 약화된 상황에서 결과(수업 길이)가 줄었고, 동시에 '식물이 많아서'라는 대안 설명(식물이 만발했음에도 수업이 짧음)을 배제하므로 인과 주장을 가장 직접적으로 지지한다. A는 상관의 추가 사례(상관→인과 치환), B는 역방향 인과(수업이 병세를 악화), D는 제3요인(늦여름)으로 각각 설계 의도대로 기능한다. 가상의 소설이라 저작권 문제 없음. 한 가지 경미한 전제는 '의사의 회복 선고'가 곧 Cletus의 죽음 예감 약화로 이어진다는 추론인데, 합리적 범위 내이며 정답 판별에 지장 없음.

advisory.note: C는 원인 변수(죽음 예감)만 낮추고 대안 변수(식물 수)는 높게 유지한 반사실적 증거로, 인과 주장을 가장 직접적으로 지지한다. A는 상관 반복, B는 역인과, D는 교란 요인이다. 오답 설계가 잘 되어 있다. 의사의 말에서 Cletus의 믿음 변화를 추론해야 하는 작은 간극이 있으나 허용 범위다.

problem.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Every morning on the Lisbon tram line 28, flower vendors Mateus and Guida set up their buckets at opposite ends of the same stop, each lowering prices whenever the other did and calling out insults about wilted carnations. One afternoon a tourist shows Guida a photograph taken the day before: in it, Mateus and Guida are bent over the same bucket, laughing. Guida studies the image for a long moment, then hands the phone back without a word. A literary critic argues that the story presents the feud not as genuine hostility but as a shared performance the two vendors maintain because it draws customers to their stop.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's interpretation?
problem.stimulus: The following text is adapted from a short story. Every morning on the Lisbon tram line 28, flower vendors Mateus and Guida set up their buckets at opposite ends of the same stop, each lowering prices whenever the other did and calling out insults about wilted carnations. One afternoon a tourist shows Guida a photograph taken the day before: in it, Mateus and Guida are bent over the same bucket, laughing. Guida studies the image for a long moment, then hands the phone back without a word. A literary critic argues that the story presents the feud not as genuine hostility but as a shared performance the two vendors maintain because it draws customers to their stop.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's interpretation?
options: Later in the story, the narrator notes that tram line 28 passes through the Alfama district, where many tourists stop to photograph the old buildings.
Later in the story, Mateus quietly moves his buckets to a different tram stop after a tourist pays him for the last of his roses, and he never sees Guida again.
Later in the story, Guida again looks at the tourist's photograph showing her and Mateus laughing over a single bucket of flowers.
Later in the story, once the last tram of the day has passed, Mateus and Guida split their unsold flowers evenly before agreeing on which insults to use the next morning.
problem.explanation: 비평가의 주장은 두 요소로 이루어져 있다. (1) 반목은 진짜 적대가 아니라 함께 꾸민 연기이고, (2) 그 연기를 하는 이유는 손님을 끌기 위해서다. D는 손님(트램)이 모두 떠난 뒤 둘이 협력하고 다음 날 할 욕설을 미리 맞춘다는 내용이다. 관객이 있을 때만 싸운다는 점은 연기라는 사실과 그것이 장사를 위한 것임을 함께 보여 주므로 정답이다. A는 관광객과 노선에 관한 배경 정보일 뿐, 반목의 본질과는 관계가 없다. B는 마테우스가 떠나 다시 만나지 않는다는 내용이어서 두 사람이 연기를 함께 유지한다는 해석과 어긋나고, 오히려 주장을 약하게 만든다. C는 지문에 이미 나온 사진 장면을 다시 말한 것이다. 함께 웃은 순간이 한 번 있었다는 것만으로는 반목이 의도된 연기라는 점도, 그 목적이 손님 유치라는 점도 증명되지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The critic's claim has two parts: (1) the feud is a performance the two vendors put on together rather than real hostility, and (2) they keep it up because it brings customers to their stop. D shows them cooperating as soon as the last tram, and with it the audience, is gone. They even agree on the next day's insults ahead of time. That one finding supports both parts: the feud is staged, and it is staged for business. A is background about the route and tourists and says nothing about what the feud really is. B has the vendors splitting up for good, which goes against the idea of a performance they keep up together, so it weakens the claim. C just repeats the photograph scene that is already in the passage. One shared laugh doesn't prove the feud is deliberately staged or that it's meant to attract customers.

hardJudge.note: 비평가 주장이 '연기'와 '손님 유치 목적'의 두 요소로 구성되어 있고, D만이 관객(트램 승객)이 없을 때 협력·욕설 사전 조율이라는 두 요소를 동시에 충족한다. C는 지문의 사진 장면 재진술(함께 웃었다는 사실만으로는 목적을 증명 못함), B는 공동 유지라는 해석과 어긋나는 반박성 결과, A는 무관한 배경 정보로 오답 역할이 분명하다. 지문의 사진은 적대가 진짜가 아닐 수 있다는 암시에 그쳐 '가설만 있고 증거 없음' 조건을 크게 해치지 않는다. 해설은 정답과 오답 배제 논리를 정확히 설명한다. 다만 정답 D가 상대적으로 쉽게 식별되어 hard 상단보다는 중상 수준에 가깝다.

advisory.note: 정답 D만 '연기'와 '손님 유치 목적'이라는 두 요소를 함께 다룬다. 영업이 끝난 뒤 협력하고 다음 날 쓸 욕설을 미리 맞추는 장면이기 때문이다. 하지만 오답이 약하다. A는 관련 없는 배경 정보이고, B는 주장을 약하게 만드는 내용이며, C는 지문을 그대로 다시 말한 것이라 쉽게 걸러진다. 그래서 claim_evidence_precision_matching 요구도 낮아 전형적인 medium 수준이다. 사진 장면은 이미 지문에 나온 약한 증거라서 1번 항목은 대체로 충족된 것으로 본다.

problem.passage:
In the opening scene of a novel set at a Louisiana bayou fish camp, six-year-old Baptiste squats at the edge of the marsh grass while his uncles argue over a tangled trotline. "There's eggs in the mud pile," he says, pointing to a mound of rotting cattails near the boat slip. No one looks up. Baptiste goes on watching the mound, quiet and patient, as the men load their skiff and push off into the brown water. One literary critic argues that the scene sets up a pattern for the whole novel: what matters most in the story is often seen first by Baptiste alone, and the adults understand it only after it has already shaped what happens to them.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's claim?
problem.stimulus: In the opening scene of a novel set at a Louisiana bayou fish camp, six-year-old Baptiste squats at the edge of the marsh grass while his uncles argue over a tangled trotline. "There's eggs in the mud pile," he says, pointing to a mound of rotting cattails near the boat slip. No one looks up. Baptiste goes on watching the mound, quiet and patient, as the men load their skiff and push off into the brown water. One literary critic argues that the scene sets up a pattern for the whole novel: what matters most in the story is often seen first by Baptiste alone, and the adults understand it only after it has already shaped what happens to them.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's claim?
options: Details that only Baptiste remarks on in the early chapters reappear in the final chapters as the causes of the adults' main reversals, while details the adults discuss early on rarely matter later.
In the early chapters, Baptiste points out far more features of the marsh than any adult character does, and the adults seldom reply to what he says.
The final chapters focus on a series of sudden events, including a flood and a lost boat, that change the adults' way of earning a living for good.
Baptiste's narration uses more Cajun French words and local plant names than the dialogue of any adult in the novel, a contrast that becomes sharper as the book goes on.
problem.explanation: 비평가의 주장에는 두 요소가 함께 들어 있다. (1) 중요한 것을 Baptiste 혼자 먼저 본다. (2) 그것이 나중에 어른들의 운명을 좌우하고, 어른들은 그 뒤에야 깨닫는다. A는 두 요소를 동시에 충족한다. Baptiste만 언급한 세부가 마지막 장에서 어른들이 겪는 반전의 원인이 되고, 어른들이 언급한 세부는 대조적으로 별로 중요하지 않다. B는 Baptiste가 더 많이 알아차린다는 관찰 쪽만 다룬다. 그가 본 것이 나중에 중요해지는지는 보여 주지 않는다. C는 결말에서 어른들의 삶이 바뀐다는 결과 쪽만 다룬다. 그 원인이 Baptiste만 본 세부라는 연결이 없다. D는 어휘·방언이라는, 주장에 없는 제3의 변수를 근거로 삼고 있어 주장과 무관하다.
problem.explanationEn: The critic's claim combines two parts: (1) Baptiste alone notices what matters first, and (2) those things later shape the adults' fates before the adults understand them. Choice A covers both parts. Details only Baptiste notices end up causing the adults' main reversals, and by contrast, the details the adults discuss don't matter much later. Choice B covers only the noticing part. It shows Baptiste observes more, but not that what he sees turns out to matter. Choice C covers only the outcome part. The adults' lives change, but nothing connects those changes to details Baptiste alone saw. Choice D relies on a third variable the claim never mentions (vocabulary and dialect), so it is irrelevant.

hardJudge.note: 비평가 주장은 (1) Baptiste 혼자 먼저 본다 + (2) 그것이 어른들의 운명을 좌우하고 어른들은 사후에야 안다는 두 요소로 구성. A만 두 요소를 결합(Baptiste만 언급한 세부 → 어른 반전의 원인, 어른이 논한 세부는 무관)하며 정답 타당. B는 관찰 빈도만(요소1), C는 결과만(요소2)으로 각각 단일 변수 함정, D는 방언·어휘라는 주장 외 정보. B가 장면과 밀접해 매력적 오답으로 기능. 가상의 소설이라 저작권 문제 없음. 해설은 정답을 정확히 뒷받침하며 모순 없음. 한 가지 사소한 점: A가 '어른들이 사후에야 이해한다'를 명시적으로 서술하지는 않으나 '반전의 원인'이라는 표현으로 충분히 함의됨.

advisory.note: 주장이 두 부분(Baptiste가 혼자 먼저 봄 + 그것이 나중에 어른들의 운명을 좌우함)으로 되어 있어서 두 부분을 모두 맞춰 봐야 풀 수 있다. B(관찰만 다룸)와 C(결과만 다룸)는 한쪽 변수만 담은 매력적 오답이고, D는 주장과 무관한 변수(어휘·방언)를 쓴 오답이다. A는 '어른들은 나중에야 깨닫는다'는 부분을 간접적으로만 보여 주지만, 그래도 가장 직접적인 근거라서 정답으로 타당하다.

problem.passage:
In the novel The Low Water Hand, a work of fiction set aboard the Mississippi riverboat Corinna in the 1850s, the cardsharp Silas Venn finds an abandoned puppy shivering behind the cotton bales and, to the crew's surprise, keeps it. In the chapters that follow, the once-calculating Silas begins folding hands he could easily win against desperate passengers, quietly lends money to the boat's stewards, and even risks his own stake to cover a deckhand's debt. One student argues that the puppy is what causes Silas's transformation: caring for a helpless creature, the student claims, wears away the cold arithmetic by which Silas has always lived. Another reader is unconvinced, noting that these same chapters also include the death of Silas's longtime partner, Dutch, and the Corinna's passage through a cholera-stricken stretch of river, events that could themselves explain why Silas changes.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the student's claim?
problem.stimulus: In the novel The Low Water Hand, a work of fiction set aboard the Mississippi riverboat Corinna in the 1850s, the cardsharp Silas Venn finds an abandoned puppy shivering behind the cotton bales and, to the crew's surprise, keeps it. In the chapters that follow, the once-calculating Silas begins folding hands he could easily win against desperate passengers, quietly lends money to the boat's stewards, and even risks his own stake to cover a deckhand's debt. One student argues that the puppy is what causes Silas's transformation: caring for a helpless creature, the student claims, wears away the cold arithmetic by which Silas has always lived. Another reader is unconvinced, noting that these same chapters also include the death of Silas's longtime partner, Dutch, and the Corinna's passage through a cholera-stricken stretch of river, events that could themselves explain why Silas changes.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the student's claim?
options: The chapters in which Silas folds the most winning hands are also the chapters in which the puppy is mentioned most often.
When the puppy goes missing ashore for two chapters after Dutch's death, Silas returns to ruthless play, and his generosity resumes only once the puppy is found again.
Silas had already begun lending money to the stewards before the puppy appeared, and one grateful steward is the person who brings him the abandoned animal.
Silas's generosity first appears in the chapter immediately after Dutch's funeral, which takes place in the same week that Silas finds the puppy.
problem.explanation:
정답 B: 강아지가 사라지면 Dutch의 죽음과 콜레라 구간 같은 다른 요인이 그대로인데도 Silas가 냉혹하게 돌아가고, 강아지가 돌아오면 너그러움이 다시 나타난다. 원인으로 지목된 요인만 바뀔 때 결과도 함께 바뀌므로 대안 설명을 배제하고 인과를 직접 지지한다.
A: 강아지 언급과 패를 접는 행동이 같은 장에 함께 나온다는 상관관계일 뿐이다. 이를 인과로 보는 것은 오해이고, 다른 사건들의 영향도 배제하지 못한다.
C: 너그러움이 먼저 나타났고, 그 결과로 강아지가 Silas에게 오게 되었으므로 인과 방향이 반대다. 오히려 학생의 주장을 약화한다.
D: 변화를 Dutch의 죽음이라는 제3의 원인과 연결한다. 시기가 겹치는 것은 다른 독자의 대안 설명을 뒷받침할 뿐이다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, B: When the puppy disappears, Silas goes back to ruthless play. Dutch's death and the cholera stretch still apply during that time. When the puppy returns, so does his generosity. Only the proposed cause changes, and the effect changes with it. That rules out the alternatives and directly supports the claim that the puppy causes the change.
A: This only shows that mentions of the puppy and Silas folding hands happen in the same chapters. That's a correlation, and treating it as proof of cause is a mistake. It also can't rule out the other events.
C: This reverses the direction. Silas's generosity came first, and it led to the puppy reaching him. If anything, this weakens the claim.
D: This ties the change to a third cause, Dutch's death. The overlap in timing supports the other reader's alternative explanation, not the student's claim.

hardJudge.note: 지문은 강아지 발견과 Silas의 변화가 같은 시기에 일어났다는 동시발생만 제시하고, 인과는 학생의 '주장'으로만 틀 지어져 있으며 다른 독자가 Dutch의 죽음·콜레라라는 대안 원인을 명시함. 정답 B는 다른 요인(Dutch의 죽음)이 유지된 상태에서 강아지 유무만 바뀔 때 행동이 함께 바뀌는 준실험적 증거로, 대안 설명을 배제하며 인과를 지지하므로 가장 강한 증거임. A는 단순 공변(상관), C는 인과 방향 역전(오히려 약화), D는 제3의 원인(Dutch의 죽음)과 연결되어 대안 설명을 강화함. 세 오답이 각각 레시피의 오답 유형에 정확히 대응됨. 해설은 정답과 오답 논리를 모순 없이 뒷받침함. 가상의 소설·인물로 저작권 우려 없고 SAT 형식에 부합함. 매력적 오답 D가 시기 일치를 통해 상관과 대안 원인을 동시에 포함해 변별력이 있어, 단순 '일치하는 진술 고르기'를 넘어 인과 검증을 요구하는 hard 수준에 적합함.

advisory.note: B는 Dutch의 죽음이라는 대안 요인을 고정한 채 강아지만 없앴다가 되돌리는 증거이므로, 학생의 인과 주장을 가장 직접적으로 지지합니다. A는 상관관계를 인과로 바꿔 읽은 오답이고, C는 인과 방향이 뒤바뀐 오답입니다. D는 대안 원인(Dutch의 죽음)에 기대는 오답입니다. 엄밀히 말해 D의 원인은 '무관한' 원인이라기보다 지문에 이미 나온 경쟁 원인이지만, 5번 항목은 충족한 것으로 판단합니다.

problem.passage:
Samir crossed half of Cairo with a single gray pigeon tucked inside his shirt. The bird had escaped weeks earlier and somehow flown back to his coop, and now he meant to return it to Laila, the girl who had named it years before. Twice the pigeon wriggled loose on the crowded tram, and twice Samir crawled beneath the seats after it while the passengers laughed. Still, the soft feathers against his chest ______ him a strange courage as he climbed the stairs to her old rooftop.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Samir crossed half of Cairo with a single gray pigeon tucked inside his shirt. The bird had escaped weeks earlier and somehow flown back to his coop, and now he meant to return it to Laila, the girl who had named it years before. Twice the pigeon wriggled loose on the crowded tram, and twice Samir crawled beneath the seats after it while the passengers laughed. Still, the soft feathers against his chest ______ him a strange courage as he climbed the stairs to her old rooftop.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: gives
has given
is giving
gave
problem.explanation: 이 지문은 crossed, wriggled, crawled, laughed, climbed처럼 과거 시제로 서술되므로 빈칸의 동사도 과거형이어야 합니다. 따라서 과거형 gave를 쓴 D가 정답입니다. A는 현재형, B는 현재완료형, C는 현재진행형이라서 모두 이야기의 과거 시제와 맞지 않습니다. 게다가 A, B, C는 단수형이라서 바로 앞의 chest를 주어로 착각하게 만드는 함정이기도 합니다. 실제 주어는 복수 명사 feathers입니다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage tells its story in the past tense (crossed, wriggled, crawled, laughed, climbed), so the verb in the blank should also be in the past tense. That makes choice D, "gave," the correct answer. Choice A uses the present tense, choice B uses the present perfect, and choice C uses the present progressive, so none of them fits the past-tense narration. Choices A, B, and C are also singular forms, which might tempt you to treat "chest" as the subject. The real subject is the plural noun "feathers."

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On Cairo rooftops, pigeon keeper Samir travels across the city to deliver a single escaped bird to a girl he once knew, his journey revealing both devotion and farce.

hardJudge.note: 지문 전체가 과거 시제(crossed, wriggled, crawled, laughed, climbed)로 서술되어 빈칸에는 과거형 gave(D)가 적절함. 주어 feathers(복수)와 A·B·C의 단수형 불일치 지적도 정확함. 한·영 해설 결론·글자 참조 일치, 한글 혼입 없음. 시제 일관성이라는 단일 규칙으로 해결되고 오답은 전형적 시제 오개념이므로 easy에 적합.

advisory.note: 이 문항은 시제 일치라는 규칙 하나로 풀린다. 같은 문장의 climbed와 앞 문장들의 과거형 동사가 단서로 직접 드러난다. 정답 D만 과거형이면서 복수 주어 feathers와도 맞는다. A, B, C는 모두 현재 계열이면서 단수형이라 시제와 수 일치 두 가지 기준에서 모두 틀렸다. 해설에서 chest를 주어로 착각하게 하는 함정이라고 지적한 내용도 정확하다.

problem.passage:
Giorgi presses his ear to the cracked door of the bakery, where two women are whispering about the quiet stranger who arrived in the mountain village this spring. The story told by the old shepherds ______ that she is the village elder's forbidden daughter, sent into exile long ago and now secretly returned.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Giorgi presses his ear to the cracked door of the bakery, where two women are whispering about the quiet stranger who arrived in the mountain village this spring. The story told by the old shepherds ______ that she is the village elder's forbidden daughter, sent into exile long ago and now secretly returned.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: claims
claim
are claiming
have claimed
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "story"이고, "told by the old shepherds"는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐입니다. 따라서 동사도 단수형이어야 하므로 A의 "claims"가 정답입니다. B, C, D는 모두 복수 동사형입니다. 이 선택지들은 동사 바로 앞에 있는 복수 명사 "shepherds"에 동사를 잘못 맞춘 것입니다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "story." The phrase "told by the old shepherds" just describes the story, so it doesn't change the subject. Because the subject is singular, the verb has to be singular too, which makes A, "claims," correct. B, C, and D are all plural verb forms. They wrongly match the verb to the nearby plural noun "shepherds" instead of the real subject.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In a Soviet-era Georgian mountain village, boy Giorgi overhears whispers that the newcomer woman is actually the village elder's forbidden daughter, now returned from exile.

hardJudge.note: 주어 "story"(단수) + 분사구 수식어 "told by the old shepherds" 뒤 동사 수일치 문항. A "claims"만 단수형이며 B/C/D는 모두 복수형으로 근접 명사 "shepherds"에 끌린 전형적 오개념 선택지. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답 및 글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 단일 규칙(간섭 수식어 수일치)으로 해결 가능하여 easy에 적합. 원문 창작 지문으로 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: 주어-동사 수일치 단일 규칙 문제이고, 주어와 동사 사이에 수식구가 끼어 있다. 오답 B, C, D는 모두 가까운 복수 명사 shepherds에 동사를 맞춘 전형적 오개념이다. 쉬운 난이도에 맞는다.

problem.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story set in Brooklyn in 1913. For two years, grocer Dominic and baker Francesco have argued over who owns the stretch of sidewalk between their shops.

Dominic's father had left him one rule about people: the harder a man works to keep a kindness from being seen, the more of himself he has put into it. Dominic trusted it the way he trusted his scale. So he was stunned on the morning he saw Francesco, his rival, slip a warm loaf and a pair of mended boots through the cellar window where Tommaso, the orphan Dominic had been feeding in secret, slept. Later that day, in front of the whole stoop, Francesco loudly called the boy a thief and chased him off, as if to make sure no one would ever link the two of them. Watching, Dominic understood that, by his father's rule, ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus:
The following text is adapted from a short story set in Brooklyn in 1913. For two years, grocer Dominic and baker Francesco have argued over who owns the stretch of sidewalk between their shops.

Dominic's father had left him one rule about people: the harder a man works to keep a kindness from being seen, the more of himself he has put into it. Dominic trusted it the way he trusted his scale. So he was stunned on the morning he saw Francesco, his rival, slip a warm loaf and a pair of mended boots through the cellar window where Tommaso, the orphan Dominic had been feeding in secret, slept. Later that day, in front of the whole stoop, Francesco loudly called the boy a thief and chased him off, as if to make sure no one would ever link the two of them. Watching, Dominic understood that, by his father's rule, ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: Francesco's gifts to the boy must have mattered very little to him, since he took such care to hide them.
Francesco's gifts to the boy must have cost him far more of himself than Dominic had ever imagined.
Francesco's gifts to the boy must have come to matter to him only because hiding them had become a habit.
Francesco's gifts to the boy must have been driven mainly by his wish to win the quarrel over the sidewalk.
problem.explanation:
규칙: 친절을 숨기려 애쓸수록 그 친절에 자신을 더 많이 쏟은 것이다. Francesco는 몰래 선물하고 공개적으로 아이를 꾸짖어 관계를 철저히 숨겼다 → 숨기려는 노력이 매우 큼 → 그만큼 자신을 많이 쏟았다(B).
A: 관계의 방향을 뒤집었다. 숨길수록 덜 중요하다는 결론은 규칙과 정반대다.
C: 원인과 결과를 바꿨다. 규칙에서 숨김은 깊은 헌신을 드러내는 신호이지, 숨기는 습관이 애정을 만들어낸다는 뜻이 아니다.
D: 규칙과 무관한 제3의 요인(보도 다툼)을 결론으로 내세웠다. 게다가 몰래 한 선물로는 다툼에서 이길 수도 없다.
problem.explanationEn:
Start with the rule: the harder a man works to hide a kindness, the more of himself he has put into it. Francesco goes to great lengths to hide his: he delivers the gifts in secret, then publicly calls the boy a thief so no one will connect the two of them. Applying the rule in the same direction, his gifts must have cost him a great deal of himself. That's choice B.
A reverses the rule. It claims that more hiding means the gifts mattered less, which is the opposite of what the rule says.
C swaps cause and effect. In the rule, hiding is a sign of deep investment. It doesn't say that a habit of hiding creates the caring.
D brings in an outside factor, the sidewalk rivalry, that the rule never mentions. Also, secret gifts couldn't help Francesco win a public quarrel anyway.

hardJudge.note: 이론 문장("숨기려 애쓸수록 더 많이 쏟은 것")이 명시되어 있고, 라이벌 Francesco라는 새로운 사례에 적용한다. 핵심 추가 사고: 공개적으로 아이를 꾸짖는 장면이 적대 행위가 아니라 '숨기려는 노력'의 일부임을 인식해야 B에 도달한다(표면상 적대적 행동을 신호 강도의 증거로 재해석). A는 방향 반전, C는 원인-결과 역전, D는 무관 요인으로 오답 설계가 체크리스트에 부합한다. B의 "than Dominic had ever imagined"는 Dominic이 "stunned"했다는 서술로 뒷받침된다. 해설은 정답을 정확히 뒷받침하며 모순 없음. 저작권 의심 없음, 형식 적합.

advisory.note: 정답 B는 맞고 해설도 일관되며 체크리스트 5개 항목을 모두 충족한다. A는 방향을 뒤집은 오답, C는 원인과 결과를 바꾼 오답, D는 무관한 요인을 내세운 오답이다. 다만 규칙을 사례에 거의 그대로 대입하면 풀린다. 공개적으로 꾸짖은 행동을 '숨기려는 노력'으로 읽는 정도의 작은 추론만 필요하고, 오답의 매력도 약하다(A는 규칙과 정반대임이 바로 보임). 그래서 전형적인 medium 수준으로 보이며, hard에 필요한 추가 사고(여러 자료 통합, 반례, 근거의 충분성 평가 등)는 없다.

problem.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Florian, a clarinetist, has driven two hours to a Bavarian village to deliver sheet music to its brass band.

Florian set the folder on the conductor's stand and murmured something about the new arrangements. He did not take off his coat. When the rehearsal began, he lingered by the door of the hall, his eyes on the back row where Lena bent over the timpani, tightening a head with small, patient turns of the key.

Some readers interpret this scene as showing that the delivery is only a pretext and that Florian's true reason for making the long trip is to hear Lena play her solo. This interpretation would be most strongly supported if the story later revealed that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Florian, a clarinetist, has driven two hours to a Bavarian village to deliver sheet music to its brass band.

Florian set the folder on the conductor's stand and murmured something about the new arrangements. He did not take off his coat. When the rehearsal began, he lingered by the door of the hall, his eyes on the back row where Lena bent over the timpani, tightening a head with small, patient turns of the key.

Some readers interpret this scene as showing that the delivery is only a pretext and that Florian's true reason for making the long trip is to hear Lena play her solo. This interpretation would be most strongly supported if the story later revealed that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the timpani, as the loudest instrument in the band, was always placed in the back row of the hall so that it would not drown out the woodwinds.
Florian left the hall within minutes of handing over the folder, well before the band reached the passage in which the timpani played alone.
the village band had performed the same arrangements at its harvest festival every autumn for more than a century without any changes to the program.
the conductor had received copies of the scores by mail a week earlier, yet Florian stayed until the timpani solo ended and then drove home without speaking to anyone.
problem.explanation:
정답 D: 이 해석은 두 가지 조건이 함께 성립해야 한다. (1) 악보 배달은 꼭 필요한 일이 아니었다(구실), (2) 진짜 목적은 솔로를 듣는 것이었다. D는 악보가 이미 우편으로 도착해 있었다는 사실로 (1)을 충족하고, 솔로가 끝나자마자 떠났다는 사실로 (2)를 충족한다.
A: 팀파니가 뒷줄에 놓인다는 내용은 지문 속 'back row'와 겉으로만 연결될 뿐, Florian의 동기와는 관계가 없다.
B: 솔로를 듣기도 전에 떠났다면 오히려 해석을 약화한다. 떠나는 행동 자체가 수상해 보여 지지하는 사실처럼 보이게 만든 함정이다.
C: 악단의 역사는 배경 정보일 뿐이라 배달이 구실이었는지를 판단하는 데 아무 근거가 되지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn:
Answer D: For this interpretation to hold, two things must both be true. (1) The delivery was not actually necessary, so it was only a pretext. (2) Florian's real goal was to hear the solo. D meets condition (1) because the scores had already arrived by mail. It meets condition (2) because Florian stayed exactly until the solo ended and then left.
A: The fact that the timpani sits in the back row only echoes the passage's mention of "the back row." It tells you nothing about why Florian came.
B: If Florian left before the solo, that would actually weaken the interpretation. This choice is a trap because leaving early can look suspicious, which makes it seem like support.
C: The band's history is just background. It gives you no evidence about whether the delivery was a pretext.

hardJudge.note: 가설이 '구실(배달 불필요)'과 '진짜 목적(솔로 청취)'이라는 두 조건으로 분해되고, D만이 두 조건을 동시에 충족함을 검산 확인. B는 솔로 전 이탈로 방향 반대, A는 'back row' 표면 연결 무관 사실, C는 배경 정보로 체크리스트 전 항목 충족. 다만 D가 다른 선택지보다 눈에 띄게 길고 정보량이 많아 길이 단서로 추측 가능성이 있으며, C의 '변경 없는 프로그램'이 '새 편곡 불필요'로 약하게 읽힐 여지가 있으나 정답 판별을 흔들 정도는 아님. 전반적으로 적합.

advisory.note: 해석은 두 조건(배달이 구실이었다는 점, 진짜 목적이 솔로 감상이라는 점)으로 이루어지며 D만 둘을 모두 충족한다. B는 '떠났다'는 행동으로 지지하는 듯 위장했지만 실제로는 해석을 약화하는 함정이고, A는 'back row'와 겉으로만 연결되는 무관한 선택지다. 조건을 분해해야 하는 점이 medium보다 한 단계 높지만, D의 정답 신호가 뚜렷해서 hard로서는 경계선 수준이다.

problem.passage:
Byzantine illuminators prized ultramarine, a brilliant blue made from lapis lazuli, above nearly every other pigment. The stone came almost entirely from mines in the Badakhshan region of present-day Afghanistan, and it reached Constantinople only after a journey of thousands of kilometers through the hands of many traders. Grinding the stone into usable pigment was also slow work, since impurities had to be washed out repeatedly. ______ scribes in many monastic workshops reserved ultramarine for the robes of Christ and the Virgin, painting less sacred figures with cheaper blues such as azurite.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: Byzantine illuminators prized ultramarine, a brilliant blue made from lapis lazuli, above nearly every other pigment. The stone came almost entirely from mines in the Badakhshan region of present-day Afghanistan, and it reached Constantinople only after a journey of thousands of kilometers through the hands of many traders. Grinding the stone into usable pigment was also slow work, since impurities had to be washed out repeatedly. ______ scribes in many monastic workshops reserved ultramarine for the robes of Christ and the Virgin, painting less sacred figures with cheaper blues such as azurite.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Consequently,
Nevertheless,
Similarly,
For instance,
problem.explanation: 앞 문장들은 군청색이 먼 아프가니스탄 광산에서 오고 가공도 힘들어 매우 귀하고 비쌌다는 원인을 제시하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그 결과로 성스러운 인물에만 아껴 썼다는 내용이므로 결과를 나타내는 A가 정답이다. B는 '귀중히 여겼다'는 첫 문장과 '아껴 썼다'를 대조로 오독하면 끌리지만, 희소성과 제한적 사용은 상반되지 않는다. C는 앞 내용도 공급의 어려움이라 비슷한 사례처럼 보이지만, 뒤 문장은 또 다른 어려움이 아니라 그에 대한 대응이다. D는 뒤 문장이 구체적이어서 예시처럼 보이지만, 가공의 어려움을 예시하는 것이 아니라 그 결과를 서술한다.
problem.explanationEn: The earlier sentences give causes: ultramarine came from distant Afghan mines and was hard to process, making it scarce and costly. The final sentence describes what scribes did because of that, saving it for the most sacred figures, so the result transition in A is correct. B might tempt you if you read "prized" against "reserved" as a contrast, but rationing a precious pigment is not opposed to valuing it. C fails because the last sentence is not another similar difficulty; it is a response to the difficulties. D fails because the final sentence is specific but does not illustrate the grinding process or the trade route; it states a consequence of them.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Byzantine manuscript illumination and lapis lazuli pigment sourcing from Afghan mines in medieval scriptoriums

hardJudge.note: 원인(원거리 공급·힘든 가공) → 결과(성스러운 인물에만 사용) 관계가 명확하여 A가 정답. B는 'prized' vs 'reserved' 오독 유인, C는 앞 내용의 '어려움' 반복처럼 보이는 유인, D는 구체성 유인으로 각각 부분적 타당성이 있어 비교 배제 필요. 해설 한/영 결론·글자 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 역사적 사실(바다흐샨 산지, 아주라이트 대체) 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 빈칸 앞에 원인 두 가지(먼 공급지, 힘든 가공)가 나오고 빈칸 뒤에 결과(아껴 씀)가 나오므로 A가 명확한 정답이다. B는 '귀중히 여겼다'와 '아껴 썼다'를 대조로 오독하게 만드는 그럴듯한 오답이다. C와 D는 비교적 쉽게 배제되지만 표면적인 근거는 있어 medium 난이도로 적절하다. 지문에 '비쌌다'는 말은 직접 나오지 않으며, 해설은 이를 추론해서 쓰고 있다(문제 될 정도는 아님).

problem.passage:
Richard Wagner believed that opera should be a Gesamtkunstwerk, or "total work of art," in which music, poetry, and stage design merged into a single dramatic experience. Conventional opera houses of his day, he complained, undermined this ideal: their horseshoe-shaped tiers of boxes encouraged audiences to watch one another rather than the stage, and their visible orchestras distracted from the drama. When Wagner designed his own Festival Theatre in Bayreuth, which opened in 1876, he arranged the seats in a steeply raked, fan-shaped auditorium that gave nearly every spectator an unobstructed view of the stage. ______ he sank the orchestra beneath a curved hood, so that the music seemed to rise from an invisible source and blend with the action onstage.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: Richard Wagner believed that opera should be a Gesamtkunstwerk, or "total work of art," in which music, poetry, and stage design merged into a single dramatic experience. Conventional opera houses of his day, he complained, undermined this ideal: their horseshoe-shaped tiers of boxes encouraged audiences to watch one another rather than the stage, and their visible orchestras distracted from the drama. When Wagner designed his own Festival Theatre in Bayreuth, which opened in 1876, he arranged the seats in a steeply raked, fan-shaped auditorium that gave nearly every spectator an unobstructed view of the stage. ______ he sank the orchestra beneath a curved hood, so that the music seemed to rise from an invisible source and blend with the action onstage.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Consequently,
Similarly,
Nevertheless,
For instance,
problem.explanation: 지문은 기존 오페라 극장의 두 가지 문제(서로를 보게 하는 좌석 배치, 눈에 보이는 오케스트라)를 제시한 뒤, 바그너가 첫 문제를 부채꼴 좌석으로 해결했다고 말한다. 빈칸 뒤의 오케스트라 은폐는 두 번째 문제에 대한 같은 방향의 해결책이므로 유사한 조치를 추가하는 B가 정답이다. A는 오케스트라를 숨긴 것이 좌석 배치의 결과인 것처럼 만들지만, 두 조치는 인과 관계가 아니라 같은 목표에서 나온 병렬적 선택이다. C는 대조를 나타내지만 두 조치는 모두 몰입이라는 이상을 지지한다. D는 빈칸 뒤 문장을 앞 문장의 사례로 만들지만, 오케스트라 은폐는 좌석 배치의 한 예가 아니라 별개의 설계 요소다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage names two problems with conventional opera houses: seating that made audiences watch one another, and orchestras that were visible. It then says Wagner solved the first problem with fan-shaped seating. The sentence after the blank, about hiding the orchestra, solves the second problem in the same spirit, so B, which adds a parallel measure, is correct. A makes hiding the orchestra sound like a result of the seating plan, but the two choices weren't cause and effect; they were separate steps toward the same goal. C signals contrast, yet both measures support the same ideal of immersion. D treats the hidden orchestra as an example of the seating arrangement, but it's actually a separate design feature, not one instance of the seating.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Wagner's Bayreuth Festival architecture and Gesamtkunstwerk aesthetic synthesis of music drama visual design

hardJudge.note: 지문 구조(두 가지 문제 → 첫 번째 해결 → 빈칸 → 두 번째 해결)가 명확하여 "Similarly"가 유일하게 논리적임을 직접 검산함. A(Consequently)는 두 조치가 같은 이상에서 나왔다는 점에서 부분적 근거가 있어 비교가 필요하고, D(For instance)도 앞 문장이 설계 전반을 서술한다고 오독하면 끌릴 수 있음. C는 말은 되나 쉽게 배제됨. 바이로이트 축제극장 1876년 개관, 부채꼴 경사 좌석, 가려진 오케스트라 피트 등 사실관계 정확. 한국어·영어 해설 결론 및 선택지 글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: 정답은 B 'Similarly'다. 지문은 문제 두 가지(관객끼리 서로를 보게 만드는 박스석, 눈에 보이는 오케스트라)를 제시하고 각각에 대응하는 해결책을 병렬로 이어 가므로 B가 맞다. 오답 A(Consequently)는 두 조치가 모두 같은 이상에서 나왔다는 점에서 그럴듯해 보이고, D(For instance)는 극장 설계의 사례처럼 읽혀 정독해야 배제된다. 사실관계도 맞다: 바이로이트 축제극장은 1876년에 개관했고, 부채꼴 객석과 덮개로 가린 오케스트라 피트를 갖췄다.

problem.passage:
When Japanese woodblock prints began reaching Paris in the 1860s, many European collectors prized them chiefly as exotic curiosities, admiring their bright, flat colors. Yet the painters who studied them most closely, among them Edgar Degas and Claude Monet, were drawn less to the prints' novelty than to the way artists such as Katsushika Hokusai organized space. In Hokusai's series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, the famous peak is often pushed to the margins or shrunk to a small triangle behind a towering wave or a cooper's barrel, while foreground objects are abruptly cropped by the edge of the sheet. Such choices broke with the European convention, inherited from Renaissance linear perspective, of placing the principal subject at the center of a balanced, deep scene. Degas's off-center dancers, sliced by the frame, and Monet's high horizons suggest that these painters found in ukiyo-e not a style to imitate but a model for rethinking how a picture could be composed.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
