problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: show that minor offenses have no connection at all to later increases in serious crime on city blocks.
show that behavioral contagion drives crime in mid-sized cities but not in the larger cities that popular accounts usually describe.
show that the critical threshold for crime contagion is higher than any rate of minor offenses that Ellison examined.
do not support the claim that crime spreads in a sudden, self-accelerating way once disorder passes a critical level.
problem.explanation: 엘리슨은 임계점 전염 모형이 맞다면 기준을 넘은 블록에서 급격한 가속이 나타나야 한다고 예측했지만, 기준 위아래 블록 모두 비슷하게 점진적으로 증가했으므로 D처럼 임계점 기반의 급격한 확산 주장을 지지하지 않는다고 결론 내리는 것이 논리적이다. A는 지나치다. 심각한 범죄가 증가했다는 사실만 있을 뿐 경미한 범죄와의 관련성 전체를 부정하는 근거는 없다. B는 도시 규모를 비교한 적이 없으므로 근거가 없다. C는 그럴듯하지만 검토한 범위 밖의 더 높은 임계점을 단정할 근거가 데이터에 없다.
problem.explanationEn: Ellison predicted that if threshold contagion were real, blocks crossing the threshold would show sudden, accelerating jumps, but blocks above and below rose at the same gradual pace, so D is the logical conclusion: the data fail to support sudden, self-accelerating spread past a critical level. A overreaches, because the passage only shows that crime rose gradually; it never rules out any link between minor and serious offenses. B is unsupported because Ellison never compared city sizes. C sounds plausible, but nothing in the data shows a higher threshold exists beyond the range she examined.

quality.seed: social science research — Gladwell tipping point social epidemiology and threshold effects in crime rate behavioral contagion patterns

hardJudge.note: 지문 검산: 임계점 전염 모형의 예측(기준 초과 블록의 급격한 가속 vs. 기준 미만 블록의 안정)과 실제 결과(위아래 모두 비슷한 점진적 증가)가 불일치하므로 "급격한 자기가속적 확산 주장을 지지하지 않는다"는 D가 유일하게 타당. A는 '전혀 관련 없음'으로 과도한 일반화, B는 도시 규모 비교 부재, C는 검토 범위 밖 임계점을 단정할 근거 없음(단, 그럴듯한 오답으로 기능). 한·영 해설 모두 D를 일관되게 뒷받침하고 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 가상의 연구자 사용으로 저작권 문제 없음. Gladwell 언급은 사실과 부합. 예측-결과 대조라는 2단계 추론과 A·C의 부분적 타당성으로 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 정답 D가 맞음. 엘리슨은 임계점을 넘은 블록에서 급격한 가속이 나타날 것으로 예측했지만, 실제로는 모든 후보 기준의 위아래 블록에서 같은 속도로 점진적인 증가가 관찰됨. 이 결과는 임계점 기반 전염 주장을 지지하지 않음. 오답 분석: A는 범위를 넘어선 과잉 일반화임. 경미한 범죄와의 관련성 전체를 부정할 근거가 없고, 오히려 심각한 범죄가 증가했다는 점에서 매력도가 있음. B는 도시 규모를 비교한 적이 없어 근거가 없음. C는 '검토 범위 밖의 더 높은 임계점'이라는 그럴듯한 대안 해석임. 중간 난이도 경계선에 있음. B가 비교적 쉽게 배제되고 'do not support'라는 신중한 결론 패턴이 익숙하다는 점이 약점이지만, A와 C는 비교해야 배제되므로 대체로 적합함. 글래드웰은 실존 인물이지만 일반적인 언급 수준이라 저작권 문제는 없음.

problem.passage:
In 1950, mathematician Alan Turing proposed a simple way to judge whether a machine can think. In his test, a human judge exchanges typed messages with both a person and a computer without knowing which is which. If the judge cannot reliably tell the two apart, the machine passes ______ some researchers argue that this standard measures only imitation, not genuine understanding or consciousness.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In 1950, mathematician Alan Turing proposed a simple way to judge whether a machine can think. In his test, a human judge exchanges typed messages with both a person and a computer without knowing which is which. If the judge cannot reliably tell the two apart, the machine passes ______ some researchers argue that this standard measures only imitation, not genuine understanding or consciousness.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the test,
the test. However,
the test, however,
the test however
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'If the judge ... the machine passes the test'와 빈칸 뒤 'some researchers argue ...'는 둘 다 독립절이므로 두 절 사이에 확실한 경계가 있어야 한다. B는 마침표로 문장을 끝내고 새 문장을 'However,'로 시작하므로 맞는 문장이 된다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. C는 however가 접속사가 아닌 접속부사라서 쉼표로 감싸도 쉼표 스플라이스가 그대로 남는다. D는 문장부호가 전혀 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The part before the blank ("If the judge ... the machine passes the test") and the part after it ("some researchers argue ...") are both independent clauses, so you need a strong boundary between them. B works because the period ends the first sentence and "However," starts a new one. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. C still makes a comma splice: "however" is a conjunctive adverb, not a conjunction, so putting commas around it can't link two clauses. D has no punctuation at all, so it's a run-on sentence.

quality.seed: social science research — Turing test artificial intelligence and behavioral indistinguishability criterion for machine consciousness evaluation

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞뒤 모두 독립절이므로 마침표+However로 분리하는 B가 유일하게 올바름. A·C는 쉼표 스플라이스, D는 무종지문으로 전형적 오개념 선택지. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답과 글자 참조가 일치하며 정확함. 튜링 1950년 제안 사실 관계도 정확. 한 가지 규칙(독립절 경계)으로 풀리므로 easy에 적합.

advisory.note: 독립절 경계 규칙 한 가지로 풀 수 있다. 오답은 쉼표 스플라이스, 접속부사 오용, 무종지문으로 모두 전형적인 오개념이다. Turing(1950) 관련 사실도 정확하다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
In a well-known 1999 study, psychologists David Dunning and Justin Kruger tested students on logic and grammar. The lowest scorers greatly overestimated how well they had done. The researchers concluded that people with low skill also lack the ability to recognize their own mistakes, so they cannot see how poorly they perform.

Text 2
Some later researchers question that explanation. They point out that almost everyone tends to rate themselves as slightly above average. When this general habit is combined with ordinary statistical patterns in test scores, low scorers will appear to overestimate themselves the most, even if they are no worse than others at judging their own work.

Based on the texts, how would the authors of Text 2 most likely respond to the conclusion Dunning and Kruger reached in Text 1?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
In a well-known 1999 study, psychologists David Dunning and Justin Kruger tested students on logic and grammar. The lowest scorers greatly overestimated how well they had done. The researchers concluded that people with low skill also lack the ability to recognize their own mistakes, so they cannot see how poorly they perform.

Text 2
Some later researchers question that explanation. They point out that almost everyone tends to rate themselves as slightly above average. When this general habit is combined with ordinary statistical patterns in test scores, low scorers will appear to overestimate themselves the most, even if they are no worse than others at judging their own work.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the authors of Text 2 most likely respond to the conclusion Dunning and Kruger reached in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that low scorers cannot recognize their mistakes and adding that the problem also affects high scorers
By arguing that low scorers actually underestimate their performance rather than overestimate it
By suggesting that the pattern in the results may come from common tendencies rather than from a special weakness in low scorers
By claiming that the study's logic and grammar tests were too difficult for the students who took them
problem.explanation: Text 1은 실력이 낮은 사람들이 자신의 실수를 알아보는 능력도 부족하다고 결론짓는다. Text 2는 누구나 자신을 평균보다 약간 높게 평가하는 습관과 통계적 패턴만으로도 같은 결과가 나올 수 있으며, 낮은 점수자가 자기 평가 능력이 더 나쁜 것은 아닐 수 있다고 말하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 Text 2가 그 설명 자체를 의심한다는 점과 맞지 않는다. B는 Text 2도 낮은 점수자가 과대평가하는 것처럼 보인다는 점을 인정하므로 틀렸다. D의 시험 난이도는 Text 2에서 언급되지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Text 1 concludes that people with low skill also lack the ability to spot their own mistakes. Text 2 says the same result could come from everyone's habit of rating themselves slightly above average combined with statistical patterns, so low scorers may be no worse at judging their work. That makes C correct. A is wrong because Text 2 doubts that explanation instead of agreeing with it. B is wrong because Text 2 accepts that low scorers appear to overestimate themselves, and D is wrong because Text 2 never mentions how hard the tests were.

quality.seed: social science research — Dunning-Kruger effect metacognitive bias and incompetent individuals overestimating their own ability levels

hardJudge.note: Text 2가 Dunning-Kruger 해석을 '일반적 자기과대평가 습관 + 통계적 패턴'으로 대체 설명하므로 C가 명확히 정답. A(동의), B(과소평가), D(시험 난이도)는 지문 직접 대조로 배제 가능하며 전형적 오개념으로 그럴듯함. Dunning–Kruger 1999 연구 및 이후 통계적 비판(better-than-average 효과, 회귀 효과) 서술은 사실과 부합. 해설 한·영 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 지문은 자체 요약으로 저작권 우려 없음.

advisory.note: Dunning-Kruger 연구와 그에 대한 통계적 인공물 비판은 사실관계가 정확하다. 단서("question that explanation", "no worse than others")가 지문에 직접 나와 있어 한 단계 추론으로 풀 수 있다. 오답들은 각각 부분 동의, 방향 반전, 지문에 없는 내용이라는 전형적인 오답 유형이다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
In their work on prospect theory, psychologists Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky found that people feel the pain of losing something more strongly than the pleasure of gaining something of equal value. Because of this, they argued, loss aversion is a basic feature of human decision-making that appears in nearly every situation involving risk.

Text 2
Some researchers have tested how far loss aversion extends. In several experiments, when the amounts of money at stake were small, such as a few dollars, participants treated possible losses and gains about equally. The asymmetry Kahneman and Tversky described showed up mainly when larger sums were involved, suggesting that the effect is real but depends on the size of what is at stake.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1 about where loss aversion appears?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
In their work on prospect theory, psychologists Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky found that people feel the pain of losing something more strongly than the pleasure of gaining something of equal value. Because of this, they argued, loss aversion is a basic feature of human decision-making that appears in nearly every situation involving risk.

Text 2
Some researchers have tested how far loss aversion extends. In several experiments, when the amounts of money at stake were small, such as a few dollars, participants treated possible losses and gains about equally. The asymmetry Kahneman and Tversky described showed up mainly when larger sums were involved, suggesting that the effect is real but depends on the size of what is at stake.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1 about where loss aversion appears?
options: By arguing that loss aversion appears in every situation involving risk, since experiments with small amounts confirmed the effect.
By arguing that loss aversion does not exist, since participants in the experiments treated losses and gains about equally.
By arguing that loss aversion is stronger when amounts are small, since people care more about losing a few dollars.
By arguing that loss aversion is not present in all risky situations, since it seems to depend on how much is at stake.
problem.explanation: Text 1은 손실 회피가 위험이 따르는 거의 모든 상황에서 나타난다고 주장한다. Text 2는 금액이 작을 때는 손실과 이득을 비슷하게 취급했으며, 그 효과는 실재하지만 걸린 금액의 크기에 따라 달라진다고 말한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 소액 실험이 효과를 확인했다고 하지만, 실제로는 소액에서 효과가 없었다. B는 Text 2가 그 효과가 "real"이라고 인정한다는 점을 무시한다. C는 결과를 거꾸로 말한다. 효과는 큰 금액에서 주로 나타났다.
problem.explanationEn: Text 1 claims that loss aversion appears in nearly every situation involving risk. Text 2 reports that with small amounts, people treated losses and gains about equally, and it concludes that the effect is real but depends on the size of the stakes. That makes D correct. A is wrong because the small-stakes experiments did not confirm the effect. They showed no asymmetry. B is wrong because Text 2 says the effect is real, so it doesn't deny that loss aversion exists. C reverses the finding, since the asymmetry showed up mainly with larger sums.

quality.seed: social science research — Kahneman prospect theory decision-making and loss aversion asymmetry in risk preference under uncertainty

hardJudge.note: Text 1의 "nearly every situation involving risk" 주장에 대해 Text 2는 소액에서는 비대칭이 나타나지 않고 금액 크기에 의존한다고 명시하므로 D가 정확히 뒷받침됨. A는 소액 실험 결과를 반대로 서술, B는 "real"이라는 명시적 인정을 무시, C는 결과를 뒤집은 전형적 오개념으로 배제 가능. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 동일 결론과 선택지 참조를 유지하며 모순 없음. Kahneman·Tversky 전망이론 및 손실 회피 서술은 사실에 부합하고, 소액에서 손실 회피가 약화된다는 실험 결과도 실제 연구(예: Harinck et al.)와 일치. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론이 한 단계이므로 easy에 적합.

advisory.note: 단서가 Text 2에 직접 드러나 있고, 오답은 전형적인 오개념(과잉 일반화, 효과 부정, 방향 반전)이어서 easy 난이도에 맞음. Text 1의 'nearly every'를 D가 'all'로 바꿔 말했지만 허용 범위임.

problem.passage:
Japan's Tokugawa shogunate issued a series of edicts between 1633 and 1639 that barred most Japanese from traveling abroad, expelled Portuguese traders, and confined Dutch merchants to the tiny artificial island of Dejima in Nagasaki harbor. These measures, later called sakoku ("closed country"), lasted until 1853. Historians have long described the policy as an effort to wall Japan off from foreign commerce. Some scholars, however, argue that the shogunate's main target was not trade itself but Christianity: in their view, officials were willing to permit foreign trade as long as it was kept separate from missionary activity, which they saw as a threat to political order.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the scholars' argument?
problem.stimulus: Japan's Tokugawa shogunate issued a series of edicts between 1633 and 1639 that barred most Japanese from traveling abroad, expelled Portuguese traders, and confined Dutch merchants to the tiny artificial island of Dejima in Nagasaki harbor. These measures, later called sakoku ("closed country"), lasted until 1853. Historians have long described the policy as an effort to wall Japan off from foreign commerce. Some scholars, however, argue that the shogunate's main target was not trade itself but Christianity: in their view, officials were willing to permit foreign trade as long as it was kept separate from missionary activity, which they saw as a threat to political order.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the scholars' argument?
options: Shogunate records show that the Dutch were allowed to keep trading at Dejima after promising not to spread their religion, while the Portuguese, who would not stop missionary work, were expelled.
Shogunate records show that the amount of silk brought into Nagasaki fell sharply in the decade after the edicts, as fewer foreign ships were permitted to enter the harbor.
Shogunate records show that officials executed many Japanese Christians in the 1630s, and that the Shimabara Rebellion of 1637–1638 included many Christian peasants.
Shogunate records show that trade with Chinese merchants at Nagasaki continued throughout the sakoku period and sometimes exceeded trade with the Dutch in value.
problem.explanation: 학자들의 주장은 막부가 무역은 허용하되 선교와 분리하려 했다는 것이므로, 선교 여부에 따라 무역 허가가 갈렸음을 보여주는 증거가 필요하다. A는 선교를 포기한 네덜란드는 무역을 계속하고 선교를 고집한 포르투갈은 추방되었음을 보여 두 요소를 직접 연결한다. B는 무역 감소를 보여주므로 오히려 전통적 견해(무역 차단)에 가깝다. C는 기독교 탄압만 보여줄 뿐 무역이 허용되었는지는 말해주지 않는다. D는 무역이 지속되었음을 보여주지만 그것이 선교 문제와 관련되었다는 근거가 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The scholars claim the shogunate tolerated trade as long as it was kept separate from missionary work, so you need evidence tying trade permission to religious activity. A does exactly that: the Dutch, who agreed not to proselytize, kept trading, while the Portuguese, who would not stop missionary work, were expelled. B shows trade shrinking, which fits the traditional "walling off commerce" view more than the scholars' view. C shows hostility to Christianity but says nothing about whether trade was still allowed. D shows trade continued, but it doesn't connect that trade to the absence of missionary activity.

quality.seed: history and civics — Tokugawa shogunate sakoku policy 1633-1853 and Japan's forced isolation restricting foreign trade and Christian missionary access

hardJudge.note: 정답 검산: 학자들의 주장은 '무역은 허용, 선교는 차단'이므로 선교 포기 여부에 따라 무역 허가가 갈린 A가 유일하게 두 요소를 직접 연결함. B는 전통적 견해(무역 차단) 쪽 증거, C는 기독교 탄압만(무역 허용 여부 없음), D는 무역 지속만(선교와의 연결 없음)으로 각각 부분적 근거를 가진 적절한 오답. 한·영 해설 모두 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 사실 관계: 1633~39 쇄국령, 1639 포르투갈 추방, 1637~38 시마바라의 난, 1853 페리 내항 모두 적절. 다만 네덜란드의 데지마 이전은 1641년으로 '1633~1639 칙령'에 포함된 것처럼 서술한 점은 약간의 단순화(판정에 영향 없는 경미한 사항). 난이도: 주장 파악 + 선택지 비교의 두 단계가 요구되어 medium 적합.

advisory.note: C와 D가 각각 주장의 절반(기독교 표적 / 무역 지속)만 뒷받침하는 부분 근거 오답이라 medium에 부합한다. 다만 A가 '선교 포기 대가로 무역 허용'이라는 주장의 핵심 표현을 거의 그대로 반복하여 다소 쉽게 보일 수 있다.

problem.passage:
After French soldiers unearthed the Rosetta Stone in 1799, scholars raced to read its hieroglyphic section by comparing it with the stone's Greek translation. Many early attempts, including Thomas Young's, treated hieroglyphs mainly as symbols for ideas, granting sound values only to the few signs used to spell foreign royal names such as Ptolemy. Some historians argue that Jean-François Champollion's decisive breakthrough in 1822 came from rejecting this restriction: he concluded that phonetic signs were used throughout native Egyptian writing, not just in borrowed foreign names, and that this insight, rather than the bilingual text alone, unlocked the script.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the historians' argument?
problem.stimulus: After French soldiers unearthed the Rosetta Stone in 1799, scholars raced to read its hieroglyphic section by comparing it with the stone's Greek translation. Many early attempts, including Thomas Young's, treated hieroglyphs mainly as symbols for ideas, granting sound values only to the few signs used to spell foreign royal names such as Ptolemy. Some historians argue that Jean-François Champollion's decisive breakthrough in 1822 came from rejecting this restriction: he concluded that phonetic signs were used throughout native Egyptian writing, not just in borrowed foreign names, and that this insight, rather than the bilingual text alone, unlocked the script.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the historians' argument?
options: Champollion's notebooks show that he matched the cartouche of Ptolemy on the stone to its Greek equivalent and assigned sound values to its signs more accurately than Young had.

Champollion's notebooks show that his first successful readings came when he applied sound values from foreign royal names to cartouches of native pharaohs such as Ramesses, which the Greek text of the stone did not name.
Champollion's notebooks show that he relied heavily on the Greek section of the stone, cross-checking nearly every hieroglyphic passage against its translation before proposing a reading.
Champollion's notebooks show that he studied Coptic, a late form of the Egyptian language, for years before 1822, which helped him guess how many hieroglyphic words were pronounced.
problem.explanation: 역사학자들의 주장은 두 가지다. 샹폴리옹이 표음 기호가 외국 이름을 넘어 이집트 고유의 표기에도 쓰였다고 본 것이 돌파구였고, 그 돌파구는 이중 언어 텍스트만으로 이루어진 것이 아니라는 것이다. B는 외국 이름에서 얻은 음가를 람세스 같은 이집트 고유 파라오 이름에 적용해 성공했으며, 그 이름이 그리스어 대역문에 없었음을 보여 주므로 두 요소를 모두 직접 뒷받침한다. A는 여전히 외국 이름인 프톨레마이오스에만 머물러 영의 접근을 더 정교하게 다듬은 것에 불과하다. C는 오히려 그리스어 대역문에 의존했음을 보여 주어 주장을 약화시킨다. D의 콥트어 학습은 그럴듯한 배경이지만, 표음 기호가 고유 단어에 쓰였다는 통찰 자체를 보여 주지는 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The historians make two claims. First, Champollion's breakthrough was seeing that phonetic signs appeared in native Egyptian writing, not only in foreign names. Second, this insight did the work, not the bilingual text alone. B supports both: he took sound values from foreign names, applied them to native pharaohs' names such as Ramesses, and succeeded even though the Greek text did not name those rulers. A stays within the foreign name Ptolemy, so it only shows a sharper version of Young's approach. C shows heavy reliance on the Greek translation, which actually weakens the argument. D is a plausible piece of background, but studying Coptic does not show the specific insight that phonetic signs were used for native words.

quality.seed: history and civics — Rosetta Stone 1799 discovery and Egyptian hieroglyphic decipherment enabling Jean-François Champollion's linguistic breakthrough

hardJudge.note: 역사학자 주장의 두 요소(표음 기호가 고유 이집트 표기에도 쓰임 + 이중 언어 텍스트만으로 해독된 것이 아님)를 B가 모두 직접 뒷받침함. A(프톨레마이오스에 머무름)와 D(콥트어 배경)는 부분적 근거를 가진 오답, C는 약화 선택지로 역할 분담이 적절. 역사적 사실(1799 발견, 영의 외국 이름 한정 음가, 1822 샹폴리옹, 람세스 판독)도 통설과 부합. 해설 한·영 모두 정답과 글자 참조 일치.

advisory.note: B만 주장의 두 요소(고유 이집트 표기에 표음 기호 사용, 대역문에 의존하지 않음)를 모두 충족한다. A는 외국 이름에 머물러 정교화에 그치고, D의 콥트어는 그럴듯한 오답이며, C는 주장을 약화시킨다. 오답 중 최소 2개(A, D)가 부분적 근거를 가지므로 중간 난이도에 맞다. 람세스 카르투시 해독은 역사적 사실과도 부합한다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Some historians describe South Africa's apartheid system, which lasted from 1948 to 1994, mainly as a set of laws about where people could live. In this view, the Group Areas Act and similar laws on housing were the true core of apartheid.

Text 2
Housing laws were only one part of apartheid. The government also separated schools, hospitals, beaches, and jobs, and it controlled who could marry whom. Under the idea of "separate development," racial segregation reached into almost every area of daily life, not just where people lived.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the historians' view described in Text 1?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
Some historians describe South Africa's apartheid system, which lasted from 1948 to 1994, mainly as a set of laws about where people could live. In this view, the Group Areas Act and similar laws on housing were the true core of apartheid.

Text 2
Housing laws were only one part of apartheid. The government also separated schools, hospitals, beaches, and jobs, and it controlled who could marry whom. Under the idea of "separate development," racial segregation reached into almost every area of daily life, not just where people lived.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the historians' view described in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that housing laws were the true core of apartheid and that other laws mattered little
By arguing that apartheid's housing laws were rarely enforced and had little effect on daily life
By claiming that the view is too narrow because apartheid's segregation extended well beyond housing
By suggesting that apartheid ended much earlier than 1994 once housing laws were changed
problem.explanation: Text 1은 아파르트헤이트를 주로 주거에 관한 법으로 설명하지만, Text 2는 주거법이 '일부'에 불과하고 학교·병원·직업·결혼 등 생활 거의 전반에 분리가 미쳤다고 말한다. 따라서 Text 2의 저자는 그 견해가 너무 좁다고 반응할 것이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 Text 2가 주거법만이 핵심이라는 주장을 부정하므로 틀렸다. B는 Text 2가 주거법이 효과가 없었다고 말하지 않으므로 틀렸다. D는 종료 시점에 대한 언급이 Text 2에 없으므로 틀렸다.
problem.explanationEn: Text 1 describes apartheid mainly as a set of housing laws, but Text 2 says housing laws were "only one part" and that segregation reached schools, hospitals, jobs, and marriage. So the author of Text 2 would say the Text 1 view is too narrow, which makes C correct. A is wrong because Text 2 rejects the idea that housing alone was the core. B is wrong because Text 2 never says housing laws had little effect. D is wrong because Text 2 says nothing about when apartheid ended.

quality.seed: history and civics — South African apartheid system 1948-1994 and legalized racial segregation enforcing separate development doctrine

hardJudge.note: Text 2의 "only one part" / "not just where people lived"가 정답 C를 직접 뒷받침함. A는 Text 2와 정반대, B는 '효과 없음'이라는 미언급 주장, D는 종료 시점 미언급으로 모두 배제 가능하되 규칙 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯함. 역사적 사실(1948–1994, Group Areas Act, separate development) 정확. 한·영 해설 결론 및 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 해설 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 단일 단계 추론으로 easy에 적합.

advisory.note: 사실관계 정확(1948–1994, 집단지역법, 혼인 금지법, 'separate development'). 단서가 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계라 easy 수준에 맞음. 다만 D는 다소 약한 오답임.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Many historians argue that the printing press made the Protestant Reformation possible. Because printers could quickly produce thousands of Bibles in German and other everyday languages, ordinary people could read scripture for themselves, and this direct access led them to question church authority.

Text 2
Printed Bibles were important, but they were also expensive, and most sixteenth-century Europeans could not read. Many people learned about new religious ideas mainly by hearing sermons, songs, and conversations in town squares. Printing helped spread reform, but much of the spreading happened through spoken words rather than private reading.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1 about how ordinary people encountered scripture?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
Many historians argue that the printing press made the Protestant Reformation possible. Because printers could quickly produce thousands of Bibles in German and other everyday languages, ordinary people could read scripture for themselves, and this direct access led them to question church authority.

Text 2
Printed Bibles were important, but they were also expensive, and most sixteenth-century Europeans could not read. Many people learned about new religious ideas mainly by hearing sermons, songs, and conversations in town squares. Printing helped spread reform, but much of the spreading happened through spoken words rather than private reading.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1 about how ordinary people encountered scripture?
options: By agreeing that most ordinary people read printed Bibles on their own and that printing alone explains the Reformation
By arguing that the printing press played no role at all in spreading new religious ideas
By claiming that printed Bibles were cheap enough for nearly every household to own
By pointing out that many people could not read or afford Bibles, so they often learned reform ideas by listening instead
problem.explanation: Text 1은 평범한 사람들이 인쇄된 성경을 직접 읽었다고 주장하지만, Text 2는 성경이 비쌌고 대부분이 글을 읽지 못해 설교·노래·대화로 사상을 접했다고 말한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 Text 2가 개인적 독서를 부정하므로 틀렸다. B는 Text 2가 인쇄가 개혁 확산에 도움이 되었다고 인정하므로 지나치다. C는 Text 2가 성경이 비쌌다고 한 내용과 반대된다.
problem.explanationEn: Text 1 says ordinary people read printed Bibles for themselves, but Text 2 notes that Bibles were expensive and most people couldn't read, so they heard reform ideas through sermons, songs, and conversations. That makes D the answer. A is wrong because Text 2 questions the idea that private reading was the main route. B goes too far, since Text 2 admits that printing helped spread reform. C contradicts Text 2's statement that Bibles were expensive.

quality.seed: history and civics — Printing press proliferation sixteenth-century Europe and religious reformation enabled by mass-produced vernacular Bible distribution

hardJudge.note: 정답 D는 Text 2의 명시적 진술(비쌈·문맹·설교/노래/대화로 접함)에서 직접 도출됨. A는 Text 1 입장을 그대로 반복, B는 Text 2의 "printing helped spread reform"과 모순되는 과장, C는 "expensive"와 정반대 — 전형적 오개념 유형의 오답으로 적절. 역사적 사실(독일어 성경 인쇄, 16세기 낮은 문해율, 구두 전파) 문제 없음. 지문은 독창적 서술로 보임. 전반적으로 easy 난이도에 적합한 양호한 문항.

advisory.note: D가 Text 2의 내용(비용, 문맹, 설교·노래·대화)을 그대로 옮기고 있어 한 단계 추론으로 풀린다. B는 Text 2를 지나치게 극단적으로 읽은 오답이고, A와 C는 Text 2와 정면으로 모순되는 전형적 오답이다. 한국어 해설의 표현을 조금만 다듬으면 된다.

problem.passage:
Proposed by economists Peter Doeringer and Michael Piore in 1971, the dual labor market hypothesis divides employment into two sectors: a primary sector offering stable jobs, internal promotion ladders, and rising wages, and a secondary sector marked by high turnover and few routes upward. Crucially, the theory holds that workers in the secondary sector cannot easily move into the primary ______ experience in low-wage, short-term jobs is often read by primary-sector employers as a sign of instability rather than as evidence of skill.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Proposed by economists Peter Doeringer and Michael Piore in 1971, the dual labor market hypothesis divides employment into two sectors: a primary sector offering stable jobs, internal promotion ladders, and rising wages, and a secondary sector marked by high turnover and few routes upward. Crucially, the theory holds that workers in the secondary sector cannot easily move into the primary ______ experience in low-wage, short-term jobs is often read by primary-sector employers as a sign of instability rather than as evidence of skill.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: sector, their
sector: their
sector their
sector, because of their
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "workers ... cannot easily move into the primary sector"와 뒤 "their experience ... is often read ..."는 각각 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이며, 뒤 절은 앞 절의 이유를 설명한다. 따라서 콜론으로 연결한 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 아무 부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문이다. D는 "because of"가 전치사구를 만들어 "their experience"를 목적어로 삼으므로 뒤의 동사 "is"가 주어를 잃어 문법적으로 성립하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The text before the blank ("workers ... cannot easily move into the primary sector") and the text after it ("their experience ... is often read ...") are both independent clauses, and the second one explains the first. A colon correctly joins them, so B is the answer. A uses only a comma to join two independent clauses, which creates a comma splice. C puts the clauses together with no punctuation at all, which makes it a run-on sentence. D turns "their experience" into the object of the preposition "because of," so the verb "is" is left with no subject and the sentence is ungrammatical.

quality.seed: economics and business — Dual labor market segmentation hypothesis and wage gap persistence between primary secondary employment sectors

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞뒤 모두 독립절(주어 workers/their experience, 동사 cannot move/is read)이며 뒤 절이 앞 절의 이유를 설명하므로 콜론(B)이 적절. A는 comma splice, C는 fused sentence, D는 "because of" 전치사구로 "is"의 주어가 사라져 비문. 해설(한/영) 모두 정답·선택지 참조·논리 일치. Doeringer & Piore 1971 dual labor market 사실 정확. 독립절 식별 + 부호 규칙 적용의 두 단계 판단이 필요하고, D("because of" vs "because")가 훑어 읽으면 매력적인 오답으로 기능하며 A도 흔한 오답이므로 medium 적합.

advisory.note: Doeringer & Piore (1971) 사실관계 정확. 각 선택지를 판단하려면 절 구조를 분석해야 함. D는 그럴듯한 함정이라 medium 난이도에 적합함.

problem.passage:
Retailers once cut prices on seasonal stock according to fixed calendars, marking down every item by the same percentage on the same date. Markdown optimization software instead tracks how quickly each product is selling at each store and recommends discounts only where sales lag. Analysts at one apparel chain found that the software's recommendations were notably ______: rather than slashing prices early across the board, it often held prices steady on fast-moving items for weeks and applied deep cuts to a narrow set of slow sellers, preserving margins while still clearing inventory before the season ended.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: Retailers once cut prices on seasonal stock according to fixed calendars, marking down every item by the same percentage on the same date. Markdown optimization software instead tracks how quickly each product is selling at each store and recommends discounts only where sales lag. Analysts at one apparel chain found that the software's recommendations were notably ______: rather than slashing prices early across the board, it often held prices steady on fast-moving items for weeks and applied deep cuts to a narrow set of slow sellers, preserving margins while still clearing inventory before the season ended.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: aggressive
uniform
selective
delayed
problem.explanation: 지문은 소프트웨어가 전면적인 가격 인하 대신 잘 팔리는 품목은 가격을 유지하고, 소수의 부진 품목에만 큰 할인을 적용했다고 설명한다. 따라서 대상을 골라서 적용한다는 뜻의 C 'selective'가 가장 정확하다. A는 '큰 할인(deep cuts)'만 보면 그럴듯하지만, 소프트웨어가 대부분의 품목에서는 오히려 가격을 유지했으므로 전체적인 성격을 나타내지 못한다. B는 모든 품목을 똑같이 인하하던 기존 달력 방식을 묘사하는 말이므로 지문과 정반대이다. D는 몇 주간 가격을 유지했다는 부분과 일부 맞지만, 부진 품목에는 할인이 적용되었으므로 핵심인 '품목별 차별화'를 담지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage explains that the software didn't cut prices everywhere: it kept prices steady on fast-moving items and applied deep cuts only to a narrow set of slow sellers. That's a description of choosing targets carefully, so C, "selective," is the most precise fit. A might look tempting because of the "deep cuts," but for most items the software actually held prices steady, so "aggressive" doesn't describe its overall behavior. B describes the old fixed-calendar approach, where every item got the same markdown, so it's the opposite of what the passage says. D matches the part about holding prices for weeks, but slow sellers did get discounts, so "delayed" misses the main point that the software treated each product differently.

quality.seed: economics and business — Retail markdown optimization algorithms and dynamic price adjustment timing maximizing inventory turnover profit margins

hardJudge.note: 정답 C 'selective'는 'rather than ... across the board', 'narrow set of slow sellers'와 정확히 대응. A는 'deep cuts', D는 'held prices steady for weeks'에 부분 근거가 있어 비교가 필요하고, B는 기존 방식의 반대 개념으로 그럴듯한 오답. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 선택지 참조와 결론이 일치하며 모순 없음. 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 지문은 독창적 서술로 저작권 의심 없음. 난이도 medium 적합.

advisory.note: A(deep cuts)와 D(held steady for weeks)는 부분 근거가 있는 매력적 오답이다. B는 기존 방식과 대비되어 그럴듯한 오답이다. 콜론 뒤 설명과 'narrow set'을 연결해야 C가 나오므로 medium 수준에 맞다.

problem.passage:
Economists have long assumed that smallholder farmers would welcome futures contracts, since locking in a sale price months before harvest protects against sudden market slumps. Yet surveys of maize growers in Kenya and Zambia found that adoption remained low even where contracts were cheap and easy to access. The researchers concluded that the farmers' reluctance was ______: many had seen neighbors commit to a fixed price only to watch market prices climb sharply at harvest, and they reasonably judged that giving up such gains could cost them more than an occasional slump.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: Economists have long assumed that smallholder farmers would welcome futures contracts, since locking in a sale price months before harvest protects against sudden market slumps. Yet surveys of maize growers in Kenya and Zambia found that adoption remained low even where contracts were cheap and easy to access. The researchers concluded that the farmers' reluctance was ______: many had seen neighbors commit to a fixed price only to watch market prices climb sharply at harvest, and they reasonably judged that giving up such gains could cost them more than an occasional slump.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: unprecedented
inflexible
temporary
well-founded
problem.explanation: 콜론 뒤 내용은 농민들이 실제 이웃의 경험을 근거로 합리적으로(reasonably) 판단했다는 것이므로, 망설임이 '근거가 충분한' 것이었다는 D가 정답이다. A는 '전례 없는'이라는 뜻이지만, 지문은 이 망설임이 새로운지가 아니라 왜 생겼는지를 설명하므로 맞지 않는다. B '완고한'은 낮은 채택률이 계속된 점과는 얼핏 맞지만, 비합리적인 고집을 암시하므로 '합리적 판단'이라는 문맥과 어긋난다. C '일시적인'은 연구자들이 망설임이 사라질 것이라고 봤다는 근거가 지문에 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The text after the colon explains that the farmers based their decision on what actually happened to their neighbors and "reasonably judged" the risk, so their reluctance was justified. That makes D the correct answer. A ("unprecedented") doesn't fit because the passage explains why the reluctance exists, not whether it's new. B ("inflexible") might seem to match the continued low adoption, but it suggests stubbornness that isn't rational, which goes against the idea of a reasonable judgment. C ("temporary") has no support, since nothing in the passage says the researchers expected the reluctance to fade.

quality.seed: economics and business — Agricultural commodity futures markets and hedging strategy adoption by smallholder farmers managing price volatility

hardJudge.note: 콜론 뒤 "reasonably judged"와 이웃 경험이라는 실증적 근거가 '근거가 충분한(well-founded)'을 명확히 뒷받침한다. B(inflexible)는 낮은 채택률 지속과 부분적으로 호응해 비교가 필요하고, C(temporary)도 "long assumed"와 대비돼 그럴듯하나 지문에 근거 없음. A는 소거 가능. 해설 한·영 모두 글자 참조 일치, 모순 없음, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 케냐·잠비아 옥수수 농가 사례는 일반적 서술로 사실 오류·저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 D가 명확하다. 'reasonably judged'가 정답의 직접 단서가 되고, B는 낮은 채택률이 이어진 점과 일부 맞아 오답 유인 역할을 한다. 'Economists have long assumed'와 대비되는 구조도 있어 중간 난이도에 적합하다. 다만 A와 C는 비교적 쉽게 배제된다.

problem.passage:
Venture capital firms rarely fund promising startups alone; instead, they form syndicates, sharing both the risk and the due diligence with trusted partners. Economist Olav Sorenson and colleagues have argued that because these partnerships depend on frequent face-to-face contact and long-standing personal ties, syndication networks tend to ______ funding in a few technology hubs rather than spreading it evenly: investors favor deals near partners they already know, so capital keeps flowing to the same regions year after year.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: Venture capital firms rarely fund promising startups alone; instead, they form syndicates, sharing both the risk and the due diligence with trusted partners. Economist Olav Sorenson and colleagues have argued that because these partnerships depend on frequent face-to-face contact and long-standing personal ties, syndication networks tend to ______ funding in a few technology hubs rather than spreading it evenly: investors favor deals near partners they already know, so capital keeps flowing to the same regions year after year.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: entrench
diversify
accelerate
regulate
problem.explanation: 이 글은 신디케이트 네트워크가 자금을 고르게 퍼뜨리지 않고, 해마다 같은 지역에 자금이 계속 흘러들게 만든다고 설명한다. 따라서 소수의 허브에 자금을 고착·집중시킨다는 뜻의 A(entrench)가 가장 정확하다. B(diversify)는 위험 분산이라는 신디케이트의 특징과 연결되어 그럴듯해 보이지만, '고르게 퍼뜨리는 것이 아니라(rather than spreading it evenly)'는 표현과 정면으로 충돌한다. C(accelerate)는 자금 흐름이 늘어난다는 느낌은 주지만, 글의 핵심인 '같은 장소에 머무르는 지속성'은 담지 못한다. D(regulate)는 공식적인 통제를 뜻하므로, 개인적 유대에서 생겨나는 비공식적 패턴과 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says syndication networks keep capital flowing to the same few regions year after year instead of spreading it evenly, so you need a word meaning "firmly lock in place." That makes A (entrench) the most precise choice. B (diversify) is tempting because syndicates do share risk, but it directly contradicts "rather than spreading it evenly." C (accelerate) hints that funding grows, but it misses the key idea that funding stays in the same locations over time. D (regulate) means formal control, which doesn't fit a pattern that comes from informal personal ties.

quality.seed: economics and business — Venture capital syndication networks and geographic clustering of startup funding concentration in technology hubs

hardJudge.note: 정답 검산: 빈칸은 "rather than spreading it evenly"와 대조되고 "capital keeps flowing to the same regions year after year"로 뒷받침되므로 '소수 허브에 고착시키다'는 뜻의 entrench(A)가 가장 논리적·정밀함. B는 정면 모순, C는 '증가' 뉘앙스만 있고 지속·고착 의미 부재, D는 비공식 유대 패턴과 불일치. Sorenson & Stuart(2001)의 신디케이션 네트워크·지리적 집중 연구와 내용이 부합하여 사실 오류 없음. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 동일 결론과 글자 참조를 가지며 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 'entrench funding in'은 'concentrate'보다 약간 덜 흔한 연어이지만 의미상 문제 없음. 대조 구조 파악 + 지속성 단서 연결이라는 두 단계 판단이 필요하고 C가 부분적 근거를 가져 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 'entrench ... in a few hubs'는 다소 어색한 연어지만 수용 가능함. Sorenson & Stuart(2001)의 VC 지역 집중 연구와 맞음. B는 반대어, C·D는 부분적으로 그럴듯한 오답이라 medium 난이도에 적합.

problem.passage:
Economists studying former manufacturing hubs in the American Midwest have long noted that union membership and wage inequality moved in opposite directions after 1980. Economist Mara Delgado cautions, however, that this pattern alone does not show that falling unionization caused inequality to rise. Plant closures and automation, she argues, may have independently weakened unions and widened pay gaps, so the link between the two trends could simply ______ their shared exposure to these broader forces rather than any direct effect of one on the other.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: Economists studying former manufacturing hubs in the American Midwest have long noted that union membership and wage inequality moved in opposite directions after 1980. Economist Mara Delgado cautions, however, that this pattern alone does not show that falling unionization caused inequality to rise. Plant closures and automation, she argues, may have independently weakened unions and widened pay gaps, so the link between the two trends could simply ______ their shared exposure to these broader forces rather than any direct effect of one on the other.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: counteract
reflect
accelerate
obscure
problem.explanation: Delgado는 공장 폐쇄와 자동화라는 공통 원인이 두 추세를 각각 만들었을 수 있으므로, 둘 사이의 연관성은 그 공통 노출을 '반영할' 뿐이라고 주장한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 공통 원인이 연관성을 만든다는 논리와 반대로 상쇄를 뜻한다. C는 외부 요인이 추세를 강화했다는 인상과 맞아 보이지만, 연관성이 공통 노출을 '가속한다'는 말은 논리가 맞지 않는다. D는 인과가 가려진다는 경고 분위기와 닮았지만, 연관성은 공통 원인을 가리는 것이 아니라 오히려 그것에서 생겨난 결과이다.
problem.explanationEn: Delgado argues that plant closures and automation may have produced both trends independently, so the correlation between them could simply mirror, or reflect, that shared exposure. That makes B correct. A means to offset, which contradicts the idea that the common forces create the link. C fits the general sense that outside forces intensified the trends, but it makes no sense to say the correlation speeds up the shared exposure. D matches the cautionary tone about hidden causes, but in Delgado's view the correlation comes from the shared forces rather than hiding them.

quality.seed: economics and business — Labor union density decline and wage inequality correlation in post-industrial manufacturing regions since 1980

hardJudge.note: 검산: 공통 원인(공장 폐쇄·자동화)이 두 추세를 독립적으로 만들었을 수 있으므로 상관관계는 공통 노출을 '반영(reflect)'할 뿐이라는 교란변수 논리. "simply ______ ... rather than any direct effect" 구조와 B가 정확히 맞물림. A(상쇄)는 정반대, C(가속)는 상관관계가 노출을 가속한다는 어색한 논리, D(가리다)는 경고 어조와 닮아 매력적이지만 상관관계는 공통 원인의 결과이지 그것을 숨기는 주체가 아님. 한·영 해설 모두 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 1980년 이후 노조 가입률 하락과 임금 불평등 확대의 역방향 추세는 일반적으로 알려진 사실로 오류 없음. 가상 경제학자 인용, 원문 저작권 의심 없음. 난이도: 'simply ... rather than'이라는 단서를 정독해야 하고 D·C가 부분적 근거를 가져 비교가 필요하므로 medium 적합(다소 표준 어휘라 상단 easy 경계에 가까우나 허용 범위).

advisory.note: 교란변수(공통 원인) 논리와 'rather than any direct effect' 대비를 함께 봐야 해서 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. D(obscure)는 경고하는 분위기 때문에 그럴듯해 보이고, C(accelerate)도 일정한 매력이 있다. 중간 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
Automated valuation models (AVMs) estimate a home's price by learning from records of past sales and past appraisals. Economists studying these tools argue that an AVM inherits whatever distortions exist in its training data: the more heavily a neighborhood's historical appraisals were marked down for reasons unrelated to the condition or features of its homes, the further the model's current estimates for that neighborhood will fall below what the homes would sell for in an unbiased market. Researchers examined two neighborhoods with nearly identical housing stock. In the first, a predominantly Black area, mid-century appraisers routinely discounted homes because of residents' race, while in the second, a predominantly white area, no such discounting occurred. If the economists' argument is correct, then an AVM trained on both neighborhoods' records should ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: Automated valuation models (AVMs) estimate a home's price by learning from records of past sales and past appraisals. Economists studying these tools argue that an AVM inherits whatever distortions exist in its training data: the more heavily a neighborhood's historical appraisals were marked down for reasons unrelated to the condition or features of its homes, the further the model's current estimates for that neighborhood will fall below what the homes would sell for in an unbiased market. Researchers examined two neighborhoods with nearly identical housing stock. In the first, a predominantly Black area, mid-century appraisers routinely discounted homes because of residents' race, while in the second, a predominantly white area, no such discounting occurred. If the economists' argument is correct, then an AVM trained on both neighborhoods' records should ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: produce estimates for the first neighborhood that sit closer to unbiased market prices than its estimates for the second neighborhood do, since the first neighborhood's records contain more variation.
cause appraisers in the first neighborhood to discount homes more heavily in the future, since the model's low figures would become the source of earlier markdowns.
undervalue homes in the first neighborhood by a larger margin than it undervalues comparable homes in the second neighborhood.
value homes in the second neighborhood less accurately than those in the first, since the second neighborhood's housing stock is likely to be newer and harder to compare.
problem.explanation:
정답 C: 이론은 '과거 감정평가의 부당한 할인이 클수록 현재 AVM 추정치가 공정 시장가보다 더 낮다'는 정방향 관계다. 첫 번째 동네는 인종 때문에 체계적 할인을 받았고 두 번째는 받지 않았으므로, 모델은 첫 번째 동네를 더 크게 저평가해야 한다.
A(방향 역전): 왜곡이 많은 동네가 오히려 공정가에 더 가깝다고 하여 관계를 뒤집었다. '변동이 많다'는 근거도 이론과 무관하다.
B(인과 역전): 이론은 과거 평가 → 모델 추정치 방향인데, 이 선택지는 모델의 수치가 과거의 할인을 만들어 낸 원인이라고 하여 원인과 결과를 바꾼다.
D(제3 요인): 주택 연식·비교 가능성이라는 이론 밖의 요인을 끌어들이며, 지문은 두 동네의 주택이 거의 같다고 했다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, C: The theory gives a direct relationship. The more heavily a neighborhood's past appraisals were marked down for reasons unrelated to its homes, the further below unbiased market prices the AVM's current estimates will fall. The first neighborhood's homes were discounted because of residents' race, and the second neighborhood's homes were not. So the model should undervalue the first neighborhood by a larger margin.
A reverses the direction of the relationship. It claims the neighborhood with more biased records gets estimates closer to fair value. Its reason, more variation in the data, also has nothing to do with the theory.
B swaps cause and effect. In the theory, past appraisals shape the model's estimates. This choice instead treats the model's figures as the source of the earlier markdowns.
D brings in an outside factor, the age of the homes and how easy they are to compare. The theory doesn't mention this, and the passage says the two neighborhoods have nearly identical housing stock.

hardJudge.note: 이론 문장('과거 할인이 클수록 현재 추정치가 공정가보다 더 낮다')의 방향이 명시되어 있고, 두 동네라는 새 사례에 적용하는 구조. C가 방향을 그대로 유지하며 '거의 동일한 주택'이라는 통제 조건과 결합되어 유일하게 성립. A는 방향 역전, B는 인과 역전(모델 수치 → 과거 할인), D는 지문의 '거의 동일한 주택' 조건과 직접 충돌하는 제3 요인 도입. 해설은 각 오답의 함정 유형을 정확히 식별하고 정답 논리와 모순 없음. 사소한 점: B의 '과거 할인의 원인이 된다'는 표현이 시간적으로 다소 어색하나 오답 기능에는 지장 없음. 정답 C가 다른 선택지보다 눈에 띄게 짧아 길이 단서가 될 소지가 약간 있음(판정 영향 없음).

advisory.note: 이론의 방향(할인이 클수록 저평가도 큼)을 두 동네에 그대로 대입하면 바로 C가 나오는 직접 적용형 문항입니다. 지문이 '할인 있음/없음'으로 대비를 명시해 주기 때문에 추가로 추론할 단계가 거의 없습니다. 오답도 쉽게 걸러집니다. A는 '변동이 많다'는 엉뚱한 근거를 들고, B는 시간 순서가 어색해 인과가 뒤바뀐 것이 쉽게 보이며, D는 지문의 '주택이 거의 같다'와 정면으로 충돌합니다. 따라서 medium 수준이며, 난이도는 주로 지문 길이와 어휘에서 옵니다.

problem.passage:
Economists studying how manufacturers responded to pandemic-era disruptions surveyed firms in four industries in 2019 and again in 2023, recording the share of each industry's key components sourced from a single country. Researcher Lena Okafor hypothesizes that diversification after the pandemic was driven less by how concentrated an industry's sourcing originally was than by how long its production lines actually sat idle in 2020: in her view, only industries that endured shutdowns longer than eight weeks substantially reduced their reliance on a single country.

Industry | Single-country share, 2019 | Single-country share, 2023 | Weeks of 2020 shutdown
Medical devices | 58% | 31% | 11
Consumer electronics | 72% | 66% | 4
Auto parts | 49% | 27% | 9
Household furniture | 81% | 77% | 3

If Okafor's hypothesis is correct, the data suggest that consumer electronics firms ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus:
Economists studying how manufacturers responded to pandemic-era disruptions surveyed firms in four industries in 2019 and again in 2023, recording the share of each industry's key components sourced from a single country. Researcher Lena Okafor hypothesizes that diversification after the pandemic was driven less by how concentrated an industry's sourcing originally was than by how long its production lines actually sat idle in 2020: in her view, only industries that endured shutdowns longer than eight weeks substantially reduced their reliance on a single country.

Industry | Single-country share, 2019 | Single-country share, 2023 | Weeks of 2020 shutdown
Medical devices | 58% | 31% | 11
Consumer electronics | 72% | 66% | 4
Auto parts | 49% | 27% | 9
Household furniture | 81% | 77% | 3

If Okafor's hypothesis is correct, the data suggest that consumer electronics firms ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: made only modest changes because their 2019 single-country share was already lower than that of furniture makers.
reduced their single-country share by more than auto parts makers did because they began with a higher degree of concentration.
cut their single-country share by roughly half, as medical device makers did after a shutdown of more than eight weeks.
changed their sourcing little not because their reliance on one country was modest but because their idle period was too brief to prompt a shift.
problem.explanation:
정답 D: 전자제품은 2019년 집중도가 72%로 높았지만 셧다운은 4주뿐이었다. 오카포르의 가설은 8주를 넘는 셧다운만 큰 다변화를 부른다고 보므로, 집중도가 66%로 조금만 줄어든 것은 원래 집중도가 낮아서가 아니라 셧다운 기간이 짧았기 때문이라는 결론이 나온다.
A: 가구 업체와 비교해 초기 집중도로 설명한 것으로, 표 숫자만 보고 가설을 무시한 오답이다. 가설은 초기 집중도가 핵심 요인이 아니라고 말한다.
B: 처음 집중도가 높을수록 더 많이 다변화한다는 직관에 기댄 것으로, 실제 감소폭(6%p 대 22%p)도 표와 어긋나고 가설의 핵심 변수도 외면한다.
C: 의료기기 행(58%→31%, 11주)을 전자제품에 잘못 짝지은 오답이다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer D: Consumer electronics started out highly concentrated (72%) but sat idle for only 4 weeks, and its share fell just to 66%. Okafor's hypothesis says only shutdowns longer than eight weeks led to substantial diversification. So the small change came from the short shutdown, not from low reliance on one country.
A: This choice explains the result using 2019 concentration compared with furniture. It reads the table but ignores the hypothesis, which says starting concentration was not what drove diversification.
B: This choice relies on the intuition that firms that start more concentrated diversify more. It ignores the hypothesis, and it also contradicts the table: electronics fell 6 points, while auto parts fell 22.
C: This choice pairs electronics with the medical devices row (58% to 31%, 11 weeks), which belongs to a different industry.

hardJudge.note: 정답 D는 표(72%→66%, 4주)와 가설(8주 초과 셧다운이 핵심, 초기 집중도는 부차적)을 결합해야만 도출되며 검산상 옳다. A는 표 숫자(81% vs 72%)만 쓰고 가설을 무시한 오답, C는 의료기기 행을 잘못 짝지은 오답으로 체크리스트 3·5 충족. 다만 B는 '초기 집중도가 높을수록 더 감소'라는 직관에 기댄 것이지 가설 텍스트만 사용한 결론이 아니며, 실제 표 수치와도 모순되어 쉽게 배제됨—체크리스트 4(텍스트만 사용한 오답)에 해당하는 선택지가 없음. 해설은 정답·오답 근거를 수치와 함께 정확히 설명하며 모순 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 D를 검산함: 전자제품은 셧다운이 4주(8주 미만)였고 단일 국가 비중이 72%에서 66%로 6%p만 줄었다. 초기 집중도도 높았으므로 '집중도가 낮아서가 아니라'는 부분이 성립한다. A는 72%<81%로 표 수치 자체는 맞지만 가설을 무시해 시각 자료만 쓴 오답이다. C는 의료기기 행을 잘못 연결한 오답이다. B는 직관에 기대고 표와도 어긋나서 텍스트만 쓴 결론으로 보기 어렵다. 순수하게 텍스트만 쓴 오답이 없으므로 4번 항목은 충족하지 못한다. 정답을 고르려면 가설과 표를 함께 보고, 대안 원인(초기 집중도)을 배제해야 한다.

problem.passage:
When a shark bites down on a hagfish, the eel-shaped scavenger releases a small amount of mucus and thread-like protein fibers from pores along its body. Within a fraction of a second, these materials absorb enormous quantities of seawater, swelling into a slimy gel that can fill the attacker's mouth and gills. Video footage collected by marine biologist Vincent Zintzen and colleagues shows sharks gagging and retreating after such encounters. Researchers had long assumed that the slime's mucus alone was responsible for this rapid expansion, but experiments by Douglas Fudge's team suggest otherwise. When the threads were removed from samples, the remaining mucus dispersed into the water instead of forming a cohesive mass; the fibers, it turns out, act as a scaffold that traps water and holds the gel together.

According to the text, what did the experiments by Fudge's team reveal?

problem.explanationEn: B is the correct answer. A borrows the detail that the gel forms in a fraction of a second, but the text never compares how fast the fibers and the mucus expand. C draws on the mention of the mouth and gills, but the text doesn't say the fibers and the mucus do separate jobs. D refers to video footage collected by Zintzen's team, not Fudge's, and that footage didn't test the fibers on their own.

problem.passage:
African lungfish survive seasonal droughts by burrowing into the mud of drying riverbeds and secreting a mucus cocoon around their bodies, a dormant state known as estivation. Researchers long assumed that the fish endured these months simply by drawing down stored energy at a normal pace until the rains returned. Measurements of oxygen consumption in estivating lungfish, however, tell a different story: the fish lower their metabolic rate to a small fraction of its usual level, and genes involved in tissue repair and protection against cellular damage become more active. Rather than passively waiting out the drought, the lungfish appears to shift its body into a distinct, actively regulated state that conserves energy while guarding its organs against harm.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: African lungfish survive seasonal droughts by burrowing into the mud of drying riverbeds and secreting a mucus cocoon around their bodies, a dormant state known as estivation. problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Evidence suggests that lungfish survive drought through a controlled physiological transformation instead of merely depleting their reserves.
Evidence suggests that lungfish survive drought mainly because their mucus cocoons prevent the loss of water from their bodies.

problem.explanation: 지문은 기존 가정(저장 에너지를 평소 속도로 소모)과 달리, 폐어가 대사율을 크게 낮추고 보호 유전자를 활성화하는 능동적으로 조절된 상태로 전환한다고 주장하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 지문에 나오는 점액 고치를 언급하지만, 수분 손실 방지가 생존의 주된 이유라는 내용은 없으며 핵심 주장도 아니다. C는 저장 에너지라는 지문 속 단어를 쓰지만, 지문은 저장량이 아니라 에너지 사용 방식의 변화를 강조한다. D는 진흙 서식지를 언급하지만, 수분이 유지되는 진흙이라는 조건은 지문에 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The text contrasts an old assumption (the fish just burn stored energy at a normal pace) with new evidence that lungfish sharply lower their metabolism and switch on protective genes, which is an actively regulated state. That makes A correct. B mentions the mucus cocoon from the text, but the text never says that preventing water loss is the main reason the fish survive. C uses the idea of stored energy, but the text focuses on how the fish change their energy use, not on how much energy they store. D refers to the mud, but the text never says the mud has to stay moist.

problem.passage:
China's Loess Plateau was built grain by grain: for roughly 2.6 million years, winds blowing from Central Asian deserts dropped fine silt across the region, eventually piling it more than 100 meters deep in places. Yet this thick deposit is far from durable. Its loosely cemented particles are easily ______ by intense summer downpours, which carry them into the Yellow River and help give that river one of the highest suspended sediment loads on Earth.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: China's Loess Plateau was built grain by grain: for roughly 2.6 million years, winds blowing from Central Asian deserts dropped fine silt across the region, eventually piling it more than 100 meters deep in places. Yet this thick deposit is far from durable. Its loosely cemented particles are easily ______ by intense summer downpours, which carry them into the Yellow River and help give that river one of the highest suspended sediment loads on Earth.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: deposited
compacted
sorted
dislodged
problem.explanation: 지문은 퇴적층이 '전혀 견고하지 않다'고 말한 뒤, 폭우가 입자를 황하로 운반한다고 설명하므로, 빈칸에는 빗물이 입자를 제자리에서 떼어 낸다는 의미가 필요하다. 따라서 '떼어 내다, 이탈시키다'를 뜻하는 D가 정답이다. A는 바람이 실트를 쌓은 과정과 관련된 단어지만, 빗물이 입자를 강으로 옮겨 가는 과정과는 반대 방향을 나타낸다. B는 빗물이 흙을 다지는 것이 실제로 가능해 보이지만, 다져진다면 오히려 더 견고해지므로 '견고하지 않다'는 내용과 맞지 않는다. C는 물이 퇴적물을 분급할 수는 있지만, 입자가 쉽게 침식된다는 점이나 퇴적층이 약하다는 점을 설명하지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says the deposit is "far from durable" and then explains that downpours carry the particles into the Yellow River, so the blank needs a word meaning the rain loosens the particles and moves them from where they sit. That makes D correct, since "dislodged" means knocked loose or forced out of position. A describes how the wind built up the silt, but the rain is doing the opposite by carrying the particles away. B might sound reasonable because rain can pack soil down, but packed soil would be sturdier, which contradicts "far from durable." C names something water can really do to sediment, but sorting doesn't explain why the deposit is fragile or how it erodes so easily.

advisory.note: 사실관계(약 260만 년, 100m 이상 퇴적, 세계 최고 수준의 부유사량)가 정확하다. 오답 A·B·C 모두 퇴적 관련 어휘라 그럴듯하며, '견고하지 않다'와 '운반한다'를 연결해야 풀리므로 중간 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
Because potassium-40 in volcanic minerals decays to argon-40 at a known rate, and because argon gas escapes from molten rock but becomes trapped once crystals form, the potassium-argon method can assign absolute ages to ash layers lying above and below archaeological finds. Dates obtained this way at East African sites have long anchored the chronology of early stone tools. Geochronologist Ama Ofori, however, ______ that reliance, pointing out that crystals formed in an earlier eruption and later swept into a younger ash deposit can retain their accumulated argon, making a layer seem older than it actually is.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: Because potassium-40 in volcanic minerals decays to argon-40 at a known rate, and because argon gas escapes from molten rock but becomes trapped once crystals form, the potassium-argon method can assign absolute ages to ash layers lying above and below archaeological finds. Dates obtained this way at East African sites have long anchored the chronology of early stone tools. Geochronologist Ama Ofori, however, ______ that reliance, pointing out that crystals formed in an earlier eruption and later swept into a younger ash deposit can retain their accumulated argon, making a layer seem older than it actually is.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: confirms
describes
skeptical of
questions
problem.explanation:
지문의 첫 단계는 칼륨-아르곤 연대측정법의 원리와 그것이 초기 석기 연대를 뒷받침해 왔다는 기존의 신뢰를 소개한다. 'however'로 시작하는 두 번째 단계에서 Ofori는 오래된 결정이 섞여 들어와 아르곤이 남아 있으면 지층이 실제보다 오래되어 보일 수 있다고 지적하므로, 그런 신뢰에 이의를 제기하는 동사 'questions'(D)가 정답이다.
A 'confirms'는 첫 단계의 신뢰하는 어조에는 맞지만, 'however'와 오류 가능성을 지적하는 내용과는 모순된다.
B 'describes'는 중립적인 동사여서 뒤따르는 비판적 지적과 'however'가 나타내는 반박 기능을 담아내지 못한다.
C 'skeptical of'는 의미는 비슷하지만 형용사구라서 동사가 필요한 자리('Ofori ... ______ that reliance')에 들어갈 수 없다(문법적으로 'is skeptical of'가 되어야 함).
problem.explanationEn:
The first part of the text explains how the potassium-argon method works and notes that scientists have long relied on it to date early stone tools. The second part begins with "however" and reports Ofori's point that older crystals mixed into younger ash can keep their argon, which would make a layer look older than it really is. Because she is raising doubts about that reliance, "questions" (D) is the answer.
A, "confirms," fits the trusting tone of the first part, but it contradicts "however" and the problem Ofori points out.
B, "describes," is too neutral. It doesn't show that Ofori is challenging the reliance, which is what "however" and her criticism signal.
C, "skeptical of," has a similar meaning, but it's an adjective phrase. The sentence needs a main verb after "Ofori," so this choice is ungrammatical without "is."

hardJudge.note: 1단계(원리 설명+기존 신뢰) → 2단계(however+반박)로 명확히 구분되며 빈칸은 2단계 첫 문장에 위치. 'questions'는 뒤의 'pointing out… seem older than it actually is'와 논리적으로 정합. A는 1단계 어조용 오답, C는 유의어이나 형용사구로 품사 불일치, B는 중립 동사로 반박 기능 결여. 과학적 사실(K-40→Ar-40 붕괴, 용융 시 아르곤 탈출·결정화 후 포획, 동아프리카 유적 연대 기준, 재퇴적된 고기 결정의 과대 연대 문제)은 모두 정확. 다만 'however'와 마지막 절이 방향을 비교적 명시적으로 제시해 reversed-relation 추론 부담은 중간 상위 수준이며, 난이도의 상당 부분은 품사 함정(C)에서 발생함.

advisory.note: 정답 D는 맞음. 내재 아르곤(xenocryst) 때문에 연대가 실제보다 오래되게 나온다는 설명도 사실과 맞음. 다만 'however'라는 단서와 오류를 지적하는 내용만으로 답이 바로 정해짐. A는 방향이 반대라 쉽게 제거되고, B는 너무 중립적이며, C는 문법에 맞지 않아 기계적으로 제거됨. 관계 역전이나 다중 증거 통합이 실제로 필요하지 않음. 길이와 전문 용어를 빼면 전형적인 medium 수준임. 또 실제 SAT에서는 품사가 다른 선택지를 거의 쓰지 않으므로, 형식은 허용 범위이지만 실제 시험 문항과 다름.

problem.passage:
On the first day of her forecasting seminar, meteorologist Dana Ruiz told her students that the high-pressure system parked over their region was "the dullest weather there is": sinking air, clear skies, and light winds spiraling clockwise outward from the center, as the Coriolis effect dictates in the Northern Hemisphere. She then asked them to record surface conditions beneath the system every morning for a week. By Friday, their logs showed dense valley fog at dawn and steadily rising levels of particulate pollution, both trapped under the layer of warm, sinking air that the system maintained. Ruiz had not predicted either outcome aloud, but weeks earlier she had already scheduled Friday's session as a lecture titled "Hazards of Calm."

Based on the text, what can most reasonably be inferred about Ruiz's remark on the first day of the seminar?

problem.explanation:
정답 B: Ruiz는 고기압을 '가장 지루한 날씨'라고 했지만, 학생들에게 일주일간 관측을 시켰고, 몇 주 전에 이미 금요일 강의를 '고요함의 위험'으로 잡아 두었다. 그러므로 그녀는 안개와 오염 축적을 예상하고 있었으면서 일부러 그 중요성을 낮춰 말해 학생들이 직접 발견하게 했다고 추론할 수 있다.
A: 지문에 나온 묘사(하강 기류, 맑은 하늘, 시계 방향 바람)를 그대로 옮긴 오답이다. 그녀의 말을 말 그대로의 요약으로 보면 금요일 강의를 미리 준비했다는 사실과 말한 내용이 어긋나는 점을 놓친다.
C: 어긋남을 거꾸로 해석했다. '고요함의 위험' 강의를 몇 주 전에 미리 잡아 둔 것은 그녀가 놀란 것이 아니라 이 결과를 예상했음을 보여 준다.
D: 코리올리 효과에 관한 일반 상식으로는 맞지만, 그녀의 발언이 무엇을 노렸는지에 대한 추론은 아니다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer B: Ruiz called the high-pressure system "the dullest weather there is." But she then had her students log conditions for a week, and weeks earlier she had already scheduled a lecture called "Hazards of Calm" for Friday. This suggests she expected the fog and pollution to build up and played down the system on purpose so that students would discover its risks themselves.
A copies the description straight from the text (sinking air, clear skies, clockwise winds). If you take her remark as a literal summary, you miss the gap between what she said and the lecture she had already planned.
C gets the gap backward. Scheduling "Hazards of Calm" weeks in advance shows she expected these results and wasn't surprised by them.
D is true as general science about the Coriolis effect, but it isn't an inference about what her remark was meant to do.

hardJudge.note: 기상학 내용(북반구 고기압의 시계방향 발산 바람, 하강기류·역전층에 의한 안개·오염 축적) 정확. '가장 지루한 날씨' 발언과 '몇 주 전 예약된 Hazards of Calm 강의'의 시간 순서를 결합해야 의도적 축소라는 함의가 도출되므로 B가 유일한 최선 답. A는 지문 묘사 그대로 옮긴 오답, C는 방향 반전 오답, D는 세부사항 과잉초점 오답으로 기능. 해설도 정답 근거와 오답 결함을 일관되게 설명함.

advisory.note: 표면 발언('가장 지루한 날씨')과 미리 잡아 둔 'Hazards of Calm' 강의, 관측 과제를 함께 보아야 의도를 추론할 수 있다. 과학 사실(북반구 고기압은 시계 방향으로 바람이 불어 나가고, 하강 기류로 생긴 역전층에 안개와 오염이 갇힘)은 정확하다. A는 지문 문장을 그대로 옮긴 오답, C는 어긋남의 방향을 뒤집은 오답이다. B의 'deliberately'는 다소 강한 표현이지만 근거가 충분해 정답으로 가장 적절하다.

problem.passage:
In ultrasonic cleaning, high-frequency sound waves create tiny vapor bubbles in a liquid that swell and then collapse violently. A bubble that collapses far from any solid object stays roughly spherical, releasing a shockwave that weakens rapidly as it spreads outward through the liquid. ______ a bubble that collapses beside a metal surface caves in unevenly, driving a narrow jet of liquid into the metal at high speed—which helps explain why erosion pits cluster precisely where bubbles touched the surface.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: In ultrasonic cleaning, high-frequency sound waves create tiny vapor bubbles in a liquid that swell and then collapse violently. A bubble that collapses far from any solid object stays roughly spherical, releasing a shockwave that weakens rapidly as it spreads outward through the liquid. ______ a bubble that collapses beside a metal surface caves in unevenly, driving a narrow jet of liquid into the metal at high speed—which helps explain why erosion pits cluster precisely where bubbles touched the surface.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: As a result,
Similarly,
Specifically,
By contrast,
problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 표면에서 멀리 떨어져 붕괴하는 기포(구형 유지, 퍼지며 약해지는 충격파)를, 뒷 문장은 금속 표면 옆에서 붕괴하는 기포(비대칭 붕괴, 금속을 직접 때리는 집중된 제트)를 설명하므로 두 상황을 대조하는 D가 정답이다. A는 먼 곳의 충격파가 약해지는 것이 표면 근처의 비대칭 붕괴를 일으키는 원인처럼 만들지만, 두 문장은 서로 다른 기포를 다루므로 인과 관계가 없다. B는 두 문장 모두 기포 붕괴를 다룬다는 점에서 그럴듯해 보이지만, 붕괴 방식과 결과가 정반대이므로 '유사함'으로 볼 수 없다. C는 뒷 문장이 앞 문장의 세부 설명일 때 쓰는 말인데, 뒷 문장은 앞 문장과 다른 조건을 제시하므로 맞지 않다.
problem.explanationEn: The first sentence describes a bubble that collapses far from any surface (it stays spherical and its shockwave weakens as it spreads), while the second describes a bubble that collapses beside metal (it collapses unevenly and fires a focused jet into the surface). Because these two cases are being contrasted, D is correct. A suggests that the weakening shockwave far away causes the uneven collapse near the metal, but the sentences describe two different bubbles, so there's no cause-and-effect link. B may look tempting since both sentences are about bubble collapse, but the way each bubble collapses and what it does are opposites, not similar. C would work only if the second sentence gave more detail about the first, but it describes a different condition instead.

quality.seed: physical science — Cavitation bubble collapse in ultrasonic cleaning and shockwave erosion mechanisms on metal surfaces

hardJudge.note: 앞 문장(멀리서 붕괴: 구형, 약해지는 충격파)과 뒷 문장(표면 옆 붕괴: 비대칭, 집중 제트)이 명확히 대조되므로 D가 옳다. 과학적 내용(캐비테이션 마이크로제트, 침식 피트)도 정확하다. B는 두 문장이 모두 기포 붕괴를 다룬다는 점에서 부분적 근거가 있고, A는 인과로 오독할 여지가 있어 비교가 필요하며 C도 문맥상 말이 된다. 한·영 해설 결론과 선택지 참조가 일치한다. 원문은 독창적 서술로 보인다.

advisory.note: 'far from any solid object' vs 'beside a metal surface'의 대비가 표면적으로 명확해 훑어 읽어도 D가 바로 선택됨. 오답 중 부분적 근거를 가진 것은 B 정도뿐이고 A·C는 쉽게 배제되어 medium 기준(오답 2개 이상 비교 필요)에 미달.

problem.passage:
Many metamaterials are assembled from tiny split-ring resonators and thin wires made of ordinary metals such as copper, and none of these components, taken individually, can bend light backward. ______ when physicists arrange the components in a repeating lattice whose spacing is smaller than the wavelength of the incoming radiation, the resulting structure exhibits a negative refractive index, steering waves to the opposite side of the normal from where conventional materials would send them.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: Many metamaterials are assembled from tiny split-ring resonators and thin wires made of ordinary metals such as copper, and none of these components, taken individually, can bend light backward. ______ when physicists arrange the components in a repeating lattice whose spacing is smaller than the wavelength of the incoming radiation, the resulting structure exhibits a negative refractive index, steering waves to the opposite side of the normal from where conventional materials would send them.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Nevertheless,
Consequently,
For example,
Similarly,
problem.explanation: 첫 문장은 구리 같은 평범한 금속 부품 하나하나로는 빛을 거꾸로 굴절시킬 수 없다고 말하고, 둘째 문장은 그 부품들을 파장보다 작은 간격으로 배열하면 음의 굴절률이 나타난다고 말한다. 앞의 예상과 반대되는 결과가 나오므로 대조를 나타내는 A가 정답이다. B는 둘째 문장의 결과가 부품의 평범함 때문에 생긴다는 뜻이 되지만, 실제 원인은 배열 방식이다. C는 둘째 문장을 첫 문장의 사례로 만들지만, 둘째 문장은 첫 문장과 정반대의 내용이다. D는 두 문장이 비슷한 내용이라는 뜻인데, 실제로는 서로 대립한다.
problem.explanationEn: The first sentence says that each ordinary metal component, on its own, can't bend light backward. The second says that arranging those same components in a subwavelength lattice produces a negative refractive index. That result goes against what the first sentence would lead you to expect, so a contrast transition fits, and that's why A is correct. B wrongly suggests the result happens because the parts are ordinary, when the real cause is how they're arranged. C presents the second sentence as an example of the first, but it actually says the opposite. D says the two ideas are similar, when they're really in contrast.

quality.seed: physical science — Metamaterial negative refractive index bending light backwards through periodic subwavelength structure arrangement

hardJudge.note: 첫 문장(개별 부품은 빛을 거꾸로 굴절 불가) ↔ 둘째 문장(격자 배열 시 음의 굴절률 발생)의 대조 관계가 명확하여 'Nevertheless'가 정답으로 타당. 음의 굴절률 = 빛을 '거꾸로' 굴절시킴이라는 연결을 독자가 파악해야 하므로 두 단계 판단 요구. 메타물질·분할 고리 공진기·파장 이하 격자 간격·음의 굴절률 관련 서술은 과학적으로 정확. B(결과 서술 'resulting'에 끌릴 수 있음), C(구체적 세부 서술)는 부분적 유인력이 있고 D도 문법적으로 성립. 한·영 해설 모두 정답 및 오답 배제 근거가 일치하며 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 다만 대조 신호('none... can bend backward' vs 'negative refractive index')가 비교적 선명해 medium 하한에 가까움.

advisory.note: 대조 관계는 명확하다. Consequently는 '부품을 배열하면 결과가 나온다'는 인과로 훑어 읽을 때 끌리는 오답이라 medium 수준에 맞는다. 다만 C와 D는 비교적 쉽게 배제된다.

problem.passage:
A ferrofluid is a liquid in which tiny magnetic particles are suspended. Without a magnetic field, the particles drift randomly and the fluid pours much like ordinary oil. A related material, magnetorheological fluid, contains larger particles, and engineers value it for a striking property: when a magnetic field is applied, the particles line up into chains that resist flow, and the fluid thickens almost instantly. Because this change can be reversed in milliseconds simply by switching the field off, automotive designers use such fluids in shock absorbers whose stiffness can be ______ continuously to match changing road conditions.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: A ferrofluid is a liquid in which tiny magnetic particles are suspended. Without a magnetic field, the particles drift randomly and the fluid pours much like ordinary oil. A related material, magnetorheological fluid, contains larger particles, and engineers value it for a striking property: when a magnetic field is applied, the particles line up into chains that resist flow, and the fluid thickens almost instantly. Because this change can be reversed in milliseconds simply by switching the field off, automotive designers use such fluids in shock absorbers whose stiffness can be ______ continuously to match changing road conditions.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: reinforced
suspended
preserved
modulated
problem.explanation: 지문에 따르면 이 유체는 자기장을 걸면 굳고 자기장을 끄면 밀리초 안에 원래대로 돌아오며, 이 덕분에 쇼크업소버의 강성을 계속 변하는 도로 상황에 맞출 수 있다. 따라서 강성을 올렸다 내렸다 '조절하다'라는 뜻의 D가 가장 정확하다. A는 유체가 굳는다는 내용과 일부 맞지만, 강성을 높이는 한 방향만 뜻해서 '되돌릴 수 있다'는 핵심을 놓친다. B는 지문에서 입자에 대해 쓰인 단어를 그대로 가져온 것으로, 강성을 '중단하다'라는 뜻이 되어 문맥과 맞지 않는다. C는 상태를 그대로 유지한다는 뜻이라 계속 바뀌는 조건에 맞춘다는 내용과 정반대다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says the fluid thickens when a magnetic field is applied and goes back to normal within milliseconds when the field is switched off. That is why a shock absorber's stiffness can keep matching changing road conditions. Choice D fits best because "modulated" means adjusted up or down. Choice A partly fits, since the fluid does thicken, but "reinforced" means making something stronger in one direction only, so it misses the point that the change is reversible. Choice B reuses a word the text uses for the particles, but saying the stiffness is "suspended" (put on hold) makes no sense here. Choice C means keeping something the same, which is the opposite of adjusting to changing conditions.

quality.seed: physical science — Ferrofluids magnetic particle suspension behavior and magnetorheological viscosity damping applications engineering

hardJudge.note: 정답 D(modulated)는 '가역적 변화 + continuously + changing road conditions'와 정확히 부합. A(reinforced)는 굳는다는 내용과 부분 일치하나 단방향, B(suspended)는 지문 어휘 재사용 함정, C(preserved)는 반대 의미로 타당한 오답 구성. 페로플루이드/MR유체 및 MR 댐퍼 관련 사실 정확. 한·영 해설 모두 선택지 글자 일치, 영어 해설 자연스럽고 한글 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 D(modulated)는 '가역적·연속적 조정' 맥락에 정확히 맞는다. A(thickens와 연결)와 B(지문 단어 재사용)는 부분적인 근거가 있는 그럴듯한 오답이고, C는 상대적으로 쉽게 배제된다. 사실관계도 정확하다(MR 유체를 쓴 적응형 댐퍼, 밀리초 단위 응답).

problem.passage:
Text 1
Thermochromic liquid crystal (TLC) sheets, whose molecular layers reflect different wavelengths of light as temperature shifts, offer engineers an inexpensive way to map heat across a surface. Because a single photograph of a coated circuit board reveals its full temperature pattern at once, some engineers argue that TLC coatings can replace infrared cameras for detecting overheating components in electronics testing.

Text 2
A TLC's color is not a direct reading of temperature: the hue an observer records depends on the angle of viewing and on the spectrum of the light illuminating the surface. For this reason, laboratories that use TLCs for heat-transfer measurements first calibrate each coating under the exact lighting and camera position of the experiment, and they repeat the calibration whenever that arrangement changes. Treated this way, TLCs can yield temperature maps of impressive precision.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the engineers' argument in Text 1?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
Thermochromic liquid crystal (TLC) sheets, whose molecular layers reflect different wavelengths of light as temperature shifts, offer engineers an inexpensive way to map heat across a surface. Because a single photograph of a coated circuit board reveals its full temperature pattern at once, some engineers argue that TLC coatings can replace infrared cameras for detecting overheating components in electronics testing.

Text 2
A TLC's color is not a direct reading of temperature: the hue an observer records depends on the angle of viewing and on the spectrum of the light illuminating the surface. For this reason, laboratories that use TLCs for heat-transfer measurements first calibrate each coating under the exact lighting and camera position of the experiment, and they repeat the calibration whenever that arrangement changes. Treated this way, TLCs can yield temperature maps of impressive precision.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the engineers' argument in Text 1?
options: By cautioning that a single photograph's colors could be misread unless the coating had been calibrated for the specific lighting and viewing angle used to take it
By agreeing that a single photograph of a coated board shows its whole temperature pattern and is therefore a cheaper alternative to infrared cameras
By noting that a properly calibrated coating can yield temperature maps of impressive precision in heat-transfer research
By objecting that a coating applied to a circuit board might itself trap heat and thus cause the components to overheat
problem.explanation:
정답 A: Text 2의 전제는 TLC의 색이 조명 스펙트럼과 관찰 각도에 따라 달라지므로 실험 조건마다 보정해야 한다는 것이다. 따라서 "사진 한 장으로 온도 분포 전체가 드러난다"는 Text 1의 근거는 보정이 전제될 때만 성립하며, Text 2의 저자는 이 점을 경고할 것이다. 이 반응은 Text 2에 직접 쓰여 있지 않고, Text 2의 전제를 Text 1의 주장에 적용해야 도출된다.
B: Text 1의 내용을 그대로 반복할 뿐이며, Text 2가 제기하는 보정 문제를 무시한다.
C: Text 2의 결론(정밀한 측정이 가능하다)만 되풀이하고, Text 1의 주장에 대한 반응이 되지 못한다. 보정이라는 조건을 빼면 오히려 동의처럼 읽힌다.
D: 코팅이 열을 가둔다는 쟁점은 Text 2에서 전혀 다루지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn:
A is correct. Text 2's key premise is that a TLC's color depends on the viewing angle and on the light illuminating it, so each setup has to be calibrated. Text 1's argument relies on the idea that one photograph shows the full temperature pattern. Applying Text 2's premise, its author would warn that such a photo can't be trusted unless the coating was calibrated for that exact lighting and camera position. Text 2 never says this directly; you have to infer it by applying its premise to Text 1's claim.
B is wrong because it only repeats Text 1's claim and ignores Text 2's concern about calibration.
C is wrong because it only restates Text 2's conclusion about precision. It drops the calibration condition, so it doesn't actually respond to Text 1's argument.
D is wrong because Text 2 never discusses coatings trapping heat. This issue comes from outside the texts.

hardJudge.note: Text 2는 Text 1을 언급하지 않으며, 정답 A는 Text 2의 전제(색이 조명·시야각에 의존하므로 보정 필요)를 Text 1의 '사진 한 장' 근거에 적용해야만 도출된다. B는 Text 1 반복, D는 본문 밖 쟁점(열 가둠), C는 Text 2 결론만 되풀이해 Text 1 주장에 대한 반응이 되지 못하는 함정으로 기능하며, A와 C를 구분하려면 '조건부 경고'와 '무조건적 동의'의 입장 강도를 가려야 한다. 사실 오류 없음(TLC 색의 시야각·조명 의존성은 실제 알려진 특성). 해설은 정답을 정확히 뒷받침한다.

advisory.note: Text 2는 Text 1을 직접 언급하지 않는다. 따라서 보정이 필요하다는 Text 2의 전제를 "사진 한 장"이라는 Text 1의 근거에 적용해 반응을 추론해야 하므로 hard 특성에 부합한다. C는 Text 2의 내용이지만 Text 1의 주장에 대한 반응이 아니므로 그럴듯한 함정 선택지다. 다만 A는 Text 2의 '각도·조명' 표현을 거의 그대로 재사용해 정답이 쉽게 눈에 띄는 면이 있다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
In electrospinning, a high voltage draws a charged polymer solution from a needle into a thin jet that stretches and dries into nanofibers. Materials engineer Priya Venkataraman argues that fiber diameter can be reliably minimized by tuning just two dials: raising voltage while lowering flow rate. Her reasoning is that a stronger electric field pulls harder on the jet, and that this added stretching, applied to less fluid per second, must translate directly into thinner fibers. Her lab's tests used a single polyvinyl alcohol solution at room temperature.

Text 2
A team led by Tomás Ferreira measured jet behavior directly with high-speed imaging. Like other groups, they found that a modest reduction in flow rate generally yields finer fibers. But beyond a moderate threshold, increasing voltage did not lengthen the stretching phase; instead, the jet began whipping erratically and ejecting from several points on the droplet at once, producing fibers with widely scattered and often larger diameters. The added field strength, the team concluded, changes how the jet forms rather than simply how much it is drawn out.

Based on the texts, which element of Venkataraman's argument in Text 1 would Ferreira's team (Text 2) most likely challenge?

Text 1
