Materials engineer Priya Venkataraman argues that fiber diameter can be reliably minimized by tuning just two dials: raising voltage while lowering flow rate. Her reasoning is that a stronger electric field pulls harder on the jet, and that this added stretching, applied to less fluid per second, must translate directly into thinner fibers. Her lab's tests used a single polyvinyl alcohol solution at room temperature.

Text 2
A team led by Tomás Ferreira measured jet behavior directly with high-speed imaging. Like other groups, they found that a modest reduction in flow rate generally yields finer fibers. But beyond a moderate threshold, increasing voltage did not lengthen the stretching phase; instead, the jet began whipping erratically and ejecting from several points on the droplet at once, producing fibers with widely scattered and often larger diameters. The added field strength, the team concluded, changes how the jet forms rather than simply how much it is drawn out.
problem.question: Based on the texts, which element of Venkataraman's argument in Text 1 would Ferreira's team (Text 2) most likely challenge?
options: The claim that fiber diameter can be reliably minimized by adjusting voltage and flow rate together
The idea that each increase in field strength produces a corresponding increase in how far the jet is drawn out
The decision to conduct the tests with a single polyvinyl alcohol solution kept at room temperature
The view that delivering less solution per second to the needle tends to yield finer fibers
problem.explanation:
정답 B: Venkataraman의 결론은 '전압과 유속을 함께 조절하면 섬유를 가늘게 할 수 있다'는 것이지만, 이 결론은 전기장이 강해질수록 제트가 그만큼 더 늘어난다는 가정에 기대고 있다. Text 2는 일정 문턱을 넘으면 전압을 높여도 늘어나는 단계가 길어지지 않고 제트가 불안정해진다고 보여 주므로, 바로 이 가정을 겨냥한다.
A: 결론 자체를 가리킨다. Text 2는 결론을 간접적으로 약하게 만들지만, 그 근거는 결론이 기대는 가정을 깨뜨리는 데 있다. 또한 Text 2는 유속을 낮추는 쪽은 인정하므로, 결론 전체를 반박한다고 보기 어렵다.
C: 실험 조건이라는 부수적 세부이다. Text 2는 용액 종류나 온도를 전혀 언급하지 않는다.
D: Text 2는 유속을 적당히 줄이면 대체로 섬유가 가늘어진다고 말하므로, 오히려 이 점에 동의한다.
problem.explanationEn:
B is correct. Venkataraman's conclusion rests on an assumption: that a stronger field always stretches the jet more. Text 2 shows that above a threshold, raising the voltage does not lengthen the stretching phase. Instead, the jet whips and splits into several jets, so this assumption is exactly what Text 2 undermines.
A states the conclusion itself. Text 2 weakens the conclusion only indirectly, by attacking the assumption beneath it. It also accepts the point about flow rate, so it doesn't reject the conclusion outright.
C is an incidental detail of the experiments. Text 2 never mentions the solution type or the temperature.
D is something Text 2 actually agrees with: it says a modest reduction in flow rate generally gives finer fibers.

hardJudge.note: Text 1은 결론(전압↑·유속↓로 섬유 직경 최소화)과 근거(전기장이 강할수록 제트가 더 늘어남 + 유속 감소)가 명확히 구분되고, 실험 조건(단일 PVA 용액·실온)은 부수 정보로 배치됨. Text 2는 유속 감소 효과에는 동의(D=동의 오답)하고 문턱 이상 전압에서는 늘어남 단계가 길어지지 않고 제트 형성 방식이 바뀐다고 하여 B의 가정과만 정면 충돌함. 정답 B는 결론이 아닌 가정이며 해설도 수치·논리 모순 없음. A는 결론 자체를 가리키는 함정으로 '함께 조절'이라는 방향 비명시 표현 덕에 Text 2가 절반(유속)은 인정하므로 '가장' 겨냥하는 요소로는 B가 우세하나, 'reliably minimized'가 Text 2에 의해 실질적으로 약화되는 점에서 A의 흡인력이 다소 강한 편임(결정적 결함은 아님). 전기방사에서 고전압 시 whipping 불안정·다중 제트 발생은 실제 문헌과 부합. 두 텍스트 입장을 종합하고 Text 2의 반응을 추론하며 결론/가정/조건의 강도를 가려야 하므로 hard 적합.

advisory.note: 정답 B는 Text 2가 직접 반박하는 가정(전기장 세기에 비례해 제트가 더 늘어난다는 것)이다. A는 결론이며, Text 2가 '전압+유속을 함께 조절'한다는 결론의 유속 부분에는 동의하므로 결론 전체를 반박한다고 보기 어렵다. 다만 A도 부분적으로 매력적이어서 변별력은 충분하지만 약간의 모호성 위험이 있다. D는 Text 2가 동의하는 부분, C는 Text 2와 무관하다.

problem.passage:
Iron oxide nanoparticles are tiny magnetic particles that doctors hope to use to treat tumors. When the particles are placed in a rapidly alternating magnetic field, their magnetic moments flip back and forth, and this motion releases heat that can damage nearby cancer cells. Materials scientist Lena Okafor hypothesizes that the amount of heat a particle produces depends on how well its internal magnetic moments are aligned: particles whose moments line up more uniformly, she argues, will heat their surroundings more than particles whose moments point in mixed directions.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Okafor's hypothesis?
problem.stimulus: Iron oxide nanoparticles are tiny magnetic particles that doctors hope to use to treat tumors. When the particles are placed in a rapidly alternating magnetic field, their magnetic moments flip back and forth, and this motion releases heat that can damage nearby cancer cells. Materials scientist Lena Okafor hypothesizes that the amount of heat a particle produces depends on how well its internal magnetic moments are aligned: particles whose moments line up more uniformly, she argues, will heat their surroundings more than particles whose moments point in mixed directions.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Okafor's hypothesis?
options: Particles with uniformly aligned moments and particles with mixed moments raised the temperature of a test solution by the same amount.
Particles with mixed moments were easier to manufacture in large quantities than particles with uniformly aligned moments.
Particles with uniformly aligned moments raised the temperature of a test solution more than particles with mixed moments did.
Particles with uniformly aligned moments stayed in tumor tissue longer than particles with mixed moments did.
problem.explanation: Okafor의 가설은 자기 모멘트가 더 균일하게 정렬된 입자일수록 열을 더 많이 낸다는 것이다. C는 정렬된 입자가 용액 온도를 더 많이 올렸다고 하므로 이 관계를 직접 보여 준다. A는 가열량에 차이가 없다고 하므로 오히려 가설을 약화한다. B는 제조 용이성, D는 조직 내 체류 시간에 관한 것이어서 둘 다 열 발생과 관련이 없다.
problem.explanationEn: Okafor's hypothesis says that particles with more uniformly aligned magnetic moments produce more heat. Choice C shows exactly that: the aligned particles warmed the solution more than the mixed ones did. Choice A finds no difference in heating, so it actually weakens the hypothesis. Choice B is about how easy the particles are to make, and Choice D is about how long they stay in tissue, so neither one tells you anything about heat output.

hardJudge.note: 가설(정렬 균일 → 열 발생 증가)이 지문에 명시되어 있고, C가 이를 직접 확인하는 실험 결과다. A는 반대 결과(약화), B·D는 열 발생과 무관한 변수로 전형적 오답 유형. 해설 한·영 모두 정답 및 선택지 참조가 일치하며 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 과학적 배경(자기 하이퍼서미아, 네엘/브라운 완화)에 모순되는 서술 없음. 가공의 과학자 이름 사용으로 저작권 의심 없음. easy 난이도 적합.

advisory.note: 가설-증거 대응이 직접적이고 한 단계 추론으로 풀린다. 오답은 전형적이다(A는 반대 결과, B·D는 열과 무관한 속성). B는 다소 쉽게 배제되지만 easy 수준에서는 허용 범위다.

problem.passage:
When tiny silica spheres are suspended in water and left undisturbed, they slowly sink and pile up at the bottom of the container. Under the right conditions, the spheres stack into neat, repeating rows, forming what scientists call a colloidal crystal. These crystals often shimmer with bright colors because the evenly spaced spheres bend light in a regular pattern. Materials scientist Lena Okafor hypothesizes that slow settling is the key to this order: when the spheres sink slowly, they have time to roll into tidy positions, but when they sink quickly, they become jammed in a disordered heap.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Okafor's hypothesis?
problem.stimulus: When tiny silica spheres are suspended in water and left undisturbed, they slowly sink and pile up at the bottom of the container. Under the right conditions, the spheres stack into neat, repeating rows, forming what scientists call a colloidal crystal. These crystals often shimmer with bright colors because the evenly spaced spheres bend light in a regular pattern. Materials scientist Lena Okafor hypothesizes that slow settling is the key to this order: when the spheres sink slowly, they have time to roll into tidy positions, but when they sink quickly, they become jammed in a disordered heap.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Okafor's hypothesis?
options: Silica spheres of a larger size were found to sink faster through water than silica spheres of a smaller size did.
Silica spheres that settled at different speeds were found to produce layers of about the same thickness at the bottom of the container.
Silica spheres that settled quickly were found to form deposits with the same bright colors as deposits formed by spheres that settled slowly.
Silica spheres that settled slowly were found to form evenly spaced, colorful deposits, while spheres that settled quickly formed jumbled, dull deposits.
problem.explanation: Okafor의 가설은 느리게 가라앉으면 질서 있는 결정이, 빠르게 가라앉으면 무질서한 더미가 생긴다는 것이다. D는 느린 침강은 고르고 색이 나는 퇴적층, 빠른 침강은 뒤엉키고 탁한 퇴적층을 만든다고 보여 주므로 가설을 직접 뒷받침한다. A는 입자 크기와 침강 속도의 관계만 말할 뿐 질서 여부를 언급하지 않는다. B는 층의 두께에 관한 것이라 배열의 질서와 무관하다. C는 속도와 상관없이 같은 색이 나타난다고 하므로 오히려 가설을 약화한다.
problem.explanationEn: Okafor claims that slow settling produces ordered crystals, while fast settling produces a disordered heap. D directly supports this because it links slow settling to evenly spaced, colorful deposits and fast settling to jumbled, dull ones. A only tells you how sphere size affects sinking speed and says nothing about order. B is about layer thickness, which has nothing to do with whether the spheres line up neatly. C actually weakens the hypothesis, since it shows that fast settling gives the same ordered colors as slow settling.

hardJudge.note: 가설(느린 침강→질서, 빠른 침강→무질서)이 지문에 명시되어 있고, D가 두 조건을 모두 대응시켜 직접 뒷받침한다. A(크기–속도만), B(두께), C(속도 무관하게 같은 색→약화)는 규칙을 알면 즉시 배제되지만 표면적으로 그럴듯한 오답이다. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답 및 선택지 참조가 일치하고 모순 없음. 가상의 연구자·독창적 지문으로 저작권 우려 없음. 콜로이드 결정의 구조색 설명도 과학적으로 타당함.

advisory.note: 가설의 두 조건(느림→질서, 빠름→무질서)을 D가 그대로 진술하므로 한 단계로 풀 수 있다. 오답은 각각 무관한 변수(A, B)와 반대 증거(C)로 전형적이다. 다만 D가 가설을 거의 그대로 다시 말하고 있어 쉬운 편이며, easy 난이도에는 적합하다.

problem.passage:
In reverse osmosis desalination, pumps push seawater against a membrane that lets water molecules pass but blocks dissolved salt. Seawater naturally resists this process: its dissolved salt creates an osmotic pressure that pulls water back toward the salty side. Water flows through the membrane toward the fresh side only when the pressure applied by the pumps is greater than this osmotic pressure. Engineers note that saltier water has a higher osmotic pressure than less salty water. Therefore, compared with a plant treating mildly salty groundwater, a plant treating highly salty seawater will likely ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: In reverse osmosis desalination, pumps push seawater against a membrane that lets water molecules pass but blocks dissolved salt. Seawater naturally resists this process: its dissolved salt creates an osmotic pressure that pulls water back toward the salty side. Water flows through the membrane toward the fresh side only when the pressure applied by the pumps is greater than this osmotic pressure. Engineers note that saltier water has a higher osmotic pressure than less salty water. Therefore, compared with a plant treating mildly salty groundwater, a plant treating highly salty seawater will likely ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: need its pumps to apply more pressure before any fresh water moves through the membrane.
need its pumps to apply less pressure, since salt helps water cross the membrane.
need its pumps to apply the same pressure, since membranes block salt equally well in both cases.
need its pumps to apply no pressure, since osmotic pressure alone moves water to the fresh side.
problem.explanation: 지문에 따르면 펌프 압력이 삼투압보다 커야만 물이 담수 쪽으로 흐르고, 염도가 높을수록 삼투압도 높다. 따라서 염도가 높은 바닷물을 처리하는 시설은 더 큰 압력이 필요하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 염분이 물의 이동을 돕는다고 보지만, 지문에서 염분은 물을 짠 쪽으로 다시 끌어당긴다. C는 막의 염분 차단 성능만 보고 염도에 따른 삼투압 차이를 무시한다. D는 삼투압의 방향을 거꾸로 이해한 것으로, 삼투압은 물을 짠 쪽으로 끌어당긴다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage says water reaches the fresh side only when pump pressure is greater than the osmotic pressure, and saltier water has a higher osmotic pressure. So a plant treating very salty seawater has to push harder, which makes A correct. B is wrong because salt doesn't help water cross the membrane; it pulls water back toward the salty side. C focuses on how well the membrane blocks salt and ignores the fact that osmotic pressure changes with saltiness. D gets the direction backward: osmotic pressure works against the flow toward the fresh side, so it can't move water there by itself.

hardJudge.note: 지문이 "펌프 압력 > 삼투압일 때만 물 흐름" + "염도↑→삼투압↑"을 명시하므로 한 단계 추론으로 A 도출. 과학적 사실(역삼투, 삼투압과 염도 관계) 정확. 오답 B(염분이 물 이동 돕는다), C(막 성능만 고려), D(삼투압 방향 오해)는 전형적 오개념으로 적절. 한·영 해설 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스러움. 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: 두 가지 명시적 전제(압력 > 삼투압, 염도↑ → 삼투압↑)를 결합하는 한 단계 추론이다. 오답은 전형적 오개념이지만 D는 다소 약하다. 빈칸 뒤 마침표가 선택지 안에 들어 있는데, 이는 SAT 관례와 맞는다.

problem.passage:
When ceramic powders are heated to make solid parts, two things happen at once: the tiny particles fuse together and the gaps between them close, a process called densification, and the small crystals, or grains, inside the material slowly grow larger. Engineers want high density but small grains, because ceramics with small grains tend to be stronger. Grain growth depends heavily on how long the material stays at high temperature. In spark plasma sintering, an electric current passes directly through the powder, heating it so quickly that a part can become fully dense in minutes rather than the hours required by conventional furnaces. Therefore, compared with ceramics made in conventional furnaces, ceramics made by spark plasma sintering are likely to ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: When ceramic powders are heated to make solid parts, two things happen at once: the tiny particles fuse together and the gaps between them close, a process called densification, and the small crystals, or grains, inside the material slowly grow larger. Engineers want high density but small grains, because ceramics with small grains tend to be stronger. Grain growth depends heavily on how long the material stays at high temperature. In spark plasma sintering, an electric current passes directly through the powder, heating it so quickly that a part can become fully dense in minutes rather than the hours required by conventional furnaces. Therefore, compared with ceramics made in conventional furnaces, ceramics made by spark plasma sintering are likely to ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: have larger grains, since electric current makes the material hotter than a furnace does.
have smaller grains, since the material spends much less time at high temperature.
have lower density, since the powder is heated for too short a time to fuse completely.
have the same grain size, since grain growth is not affected by the heating method.
problem.explanation: 지문은 결정립 성장이 고온에 머무는 시간에 크게 좌우된다고 밝히고, 스파크 플라스마 소결은 몇 시간 대신 몇 분 만에 치밀화를 끝낸다고 말한다. 따라서 고온 노출 시간이 짧아 결정립이 더 작을 것이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 온도가 더 높다는 근거가 지문에 없고, 핵심 요인인 시간을 무시한다. C는 지문에서 몇 분 만에 '완전히 치밀해진다'고 했으므로 틀리다. D는 결정립 성장이 시간에 좌우된다는 지문 내용과 모순된다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says grain growth depends heavily on how long the material stays at high temperature, and that spark plasma sintering makes a part fully dense in minutes instead of hours. Less time at high temperature means less grain growth, so B is correct. A is wrong because the text never says the material gets hotter, and it ignores the key factor, which is time. C contradicts the text, which says the parts become fully dense. D is wrong because the text directly ties grain growth to heating time, and that time is very different between the two methods.

hardJudge.note: 지문에 "grain growth depends heavily on how long the material stays at high temperature"와 "fully dense in minutes rather than hours"가 명시되어 있어 한 단계 추론으로 B가 도출된다. A(온도 오개념), C("fully dense"와 직접 모순), D(시간 의존성과 모순)는 규칙을 알면 즉시 배제되지만 그럴듯한 오개념으로 구성됨. 한·영 해설 모두 B를 일관되게 뒷받침하며 글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 스파크 플라스마 소결 관련 과학 내용도 실제와 부합. 독창적 서술로 저작권 우려 없음.

advisory.note: 추론이 한 단계뿐이다(시간이 짧으면 결정립 성장이 적다). 오답은 전형적인 오개념을 노린다. 결정립 크기 측면에서는 D가 다소 쉽게 배제된다.

problem.passage:
When propylene is polymerized with a Ziegler-Natta catalyst, the resulting polypropylene is usually isotactic: nearly every methyl group along the chain points to the same side, which lets the chains pack into rigid crystals. Chemists have long debated where this stereochemical control comes from. One view holds that the growing chain end steers each new monomer. A competing hypothesis, advanced by researchers studying titanium chloride catalysts, holds that control comes from the chiral geometry of the metal site itself: the asymmetric arrangement of atoms around each titanium center lets an incoming propylene molecule bind in only one orientation, no matter how the chain attached to that site happens to be arranged.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the competing hypothesis about the source of stereochemical control?
problem.stimulus: When propylene is polymerized with a Ziegler-Natta catalyst, the resulting polypropylene is usually isotactic: nearly every methyl group along the chain points to the same side, which lets the chains pack into rigid crystals. Chemists have long debated where this stereochemical control comes from. One view holds that the growing chain end steers each new monomer. A competing hypothesis, advanced by researchers studying titanium chloride catalysts, holds that control comes from the chiral geometry of the metal site itself: the asymmetric arrangement of atoms around each titanium center lets an incoming propylene molecule bind in only one orientation, no matter how the chain attached to that site happens to be arranged.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the competing hypothesis about the source of stereochemical control?
options: When the reaction temperature was raised, the catalyst produced polypropylene chains of higher average molecular weight but similar crystallinity.
When a chain grown on the catalyst contained an occasional misinserted unit, the monomers added after that error took on the misinserted unit's orientation and carried it forward along the chain.
When a chain grown on the catalyst contained an occasional misinserted unit, the monomers added after that error went back to the orientation they had before the error.
Polypropylene produced with the titanium chloride catalyst was found to have methyl groups that mostly pointed to the same side of the chain, so it was stiff and highly crystalline.
problem.explanation:
정답 C: 경쟁 가설은 입체 제어가 성장 사슬의 배열과 관계없이 티타늄 자리의 키랄 구조에서 나온다고 본다. 사슬에 잘못 삽입된 단위가 있어도 다음 단량체들이 오류 이전의 방향으로 돌아간다면, 방향을 정하는 것은 사슬 말단이 아니라 금속 자리라는 뜻이므로 가설을 직접 지지한다.
A (무관한 사실): 온도에 따른 분자량 변화는 입체 제어가 어디서 오는지와 상관이 없다.
B (반박하는 결과): 새 단량체가 오류 단위의 방향을 따른다는 것은 사슬 말단이 다음 삽입을 조종한다는 뜻이므로, 경쟁 가설이 아니라 첫 번째 견해를 지지한다.
D (재진술): 이소택틱하고 결정성이 높다는 내용은 지문에 이미 나와 있다. 두 견해 모두 이 결과를 설명할 수 있으므로 둘 중 어느 쪽인지 가려 주지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer C: The competing hypothesis says stereocontrol comes from the chiral titanium site, no matter how the growing chain is arranged. Suppose a chain picks up a misinserted unit, and the monomers added after it go back to their earlier orientation. Then the chain end isn't setting the orientation. The metal site is, so this finding directly supports the hypothesis.
A (irrelevant fact): How temperature affects molecular weight tells you nothing about where stereocontrol comes from.
B (weakening result): If new monomers copy the error's orientation, the chain end is steering each insertion. That supports the chain-end view, not the competing hypothesis.
D (restatement): The passage already says the polymer is isotactic and crystalline. Both views can explain that, so this finding doesn't help you choose between them.

hardJudge.note: 지문은 사슬말단 제어 vs 금속자리(site) 제어라는 두 가설만 제시하고 증거는 없음. 정답 C(오류 뒤 원래 방향으로 복귀)는 "사슬 배열과 무관하게 자리가 방향을 정한다"는 경쟁 가설의 핵심 조건을 정확히 검증하는 새로운 가상 결과이며, 실제 화학(enantiomorphic site control의 입체오류 패턴)과도 부합함. B는 사슬말단 제어를 지지하는 반박 결과, D는 지문 재진술, A는 무관. B/C가 거울상 구조라 지문의 "no matter how the chain... happens to be arranged" 절을 인과적으로 해석해야만 구별 가능하므로 medium 이상의 사고를 요구함. 해설은 정답 및 오답 근거를 정확히 설명하며 모순 없음.

advisory.note: 사이트 제어(오류가 고립되고 원래 방향으로 복귀)와 사슬 말단 제어(오류가 전파됨)를 구분하는 고전적 판별 실험이다. 화학적으로 정확하다. B와 C가 짝을 이룬 대비 구조여서 인과 방향을 판단해야 풀린다. D는 두 견해 모두와 맞는 재진술이다.

problem.passage:
The lotus leaf stays clean because water beads up on its waxy, micro-bumpy surface and rolls away, carrying dust with it. Engineers who try to copy this effect usually measure a coating's static contact angle, which is the angle a resting droplet makes with the surface. Angles above 150° count as "superhydrophobic." Materials scientist Leena Varga and colleagues argue that this measurement alone is misleading. Some surfaces, such as rose petals, have very high contact angles, yet droplets stick to them even when the surface is tipped upside down. Varga's team therefore claims that a coating will reliably clean itself only if it has a high static contact angle and also a low sliding angle, which is the tilt at which a droplet starts to move.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Varga's team's claim?
problem.stimulus: The lotus leaf stays clean because water beads up on its waxy, micro-bumpy surface and rolls away, carrying dust with it. Engineers who try to copy this effect usually measure a coating's static contact angle, which is the angle a resting droplet makes with the surface. Angles above 150° count as "superhydrophobic." Materials scientist Leena Varga and colleagues argue that this measurement alone is misleading. Some surfaces, such as rose petals, have very high contact angles, yet droplets stick to them even when the surface is tipped upside down. Varga's team therefore claims that a coating will reliably clean itself only if it has a high static contact angle and also a low sliding angle, which is the tilt at which a droplet starts to move.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Varga's team's claim?
options: Across twelve tested coatings, those with higher static contact angles removed, on average, more applied dust during simulated rainfall than those with lower static contact angles did.
Across twelve tested coatings, those on which droplets began moving at tilts below 10° removed, on average, more applied dust during simulated rainfall than those requiring steeper tilts did.
Across twelve tested coatings, thicker coatings removed more applied dust during simulated rainfall than thinner coatings did, whatever their contact angles or sliding angles.

Across twelve tested coatings, those with contact angles above 150° and sliding angles below 10° removed most applied dust during simulated rainfall, while those meeting only one of these thresholds removed little.
problem.explanation:
정답 D: 연구팀은 높은 정적 접촉각과 낮은 미끄럼각이 '둘 다' 있어야 자가세정이 된다고 주장한다. D는 두 조건을 모두 갖춘 코팅만 먼지를 잘 제거했고, 한 조건만 갖춘 코팅은 거의 제거하지 못했다고 보여 주므로 두 조건이 모두 필요하다는 점을 직접 뒷받침한다.
A(접촉각만 봄): 접촉각이 높을수록 평균적으로 더 잘 닦였다는 결과일 뿐이어서 미끄럼각도 필요하다는 점은 보여 주지 못한다. 오히려 접촉각 하나로 충분하다는, 연구팀이 반박하는 관점에 더 가깝다.
B(미끄럼각만 봄): 미끄럼각과 세정 효과의 관계만 보여 주며, 높은 접촉각도 함께 있어야 하는지는 알 수 없다.
C(제3의 변수): 코팅 두께는 지문의 주장과 관련이 없고, 접촉각·미끄럼각과 관계없이 결과가 달라졌다면 오히려 주장을 약화시킨다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer D: The team claims that reliable self-cleaning requires both a high static contact angle and a low sliding angle. D shows that only coatings meeting both thresholds removed most of the dust, while coatings meeting just one threshold removed little. That shows both conditions are needed, so it directly supports the claim.
A (contact angle only): A only shows that higher contact angles were linked to better cleaning on average. It says nothing about whether a low sliding angle is also needed. In fact, it fits the single-measurement view that the team rejects.
B (sliding angle only): B links cleaning to sliding angle alone. It doesn't show whether a high contact angle is also required.
C (third variable): Coating thickness isn't part of the claim. If thickness predicted cleaning regardless of either angle, the claim would actually be weakened.

hardJudge.note: 주장이 '접촉각 AND 미끄럼각' 결합 조건임을 파악해야 하며, A·B는 각각 한 변수만으로 그럴듯해 보이는 함정, C는 지문에 없는 두께 변수 도입. D만이 두 조건 충족군과 한 조건 충족군을 대비시켜 결합 필요성을 직접 지지. 정답·해설 모두 타당.

advisory.note: 정답 D만 두 조건을 결합하고 한 조건만 충족한 경우와 대비시키는 유일한 선택지라서 'and also'만 확인하면 바로 풀린다. A·B는 한 변수만 다루는 함정이지만 구조가 너무 뻔히 드러난다. 표준적인 medium 수준의 문항이다.

problem.passage:
Engineers examining failed circuit boards returned from automotive customers noticed that solder joints with large intermetallic layers—brittle copper-tin compounds that form where solder meets a copper pad—were also the joints most likely to contain fatigue cracks. Materials scientist Leena Varkonyi has proposed that the thick intermetallic layers cause the cracks: because these compounds are stiff and brittle, she argues, they concentrate the stress produced as the board repeatedly heats and cools, letting cracks start there. Some of her colleagues point out, however, that joints on hotter parts of a board both grow thicker intermetallic layers and go through larger temperature swings, so the two features might simply occur together.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Varkonyi's hypothesis?
problem.stimulus: Engineers examining failed circuit boards returned from automotive customers noticed that solder joints with large intermetallic layers—brittle copper-tin compounds that form where solder meets a copper pad—were also the joints most likely to contain fatigue cracks. Materials scientist Leena Varkonyi has proposed that the thick intermetallic layers cause the cracks: because these compounds are stiff and brittle, she argues, they concentrate the stress produced as the board repeatedly heats and cools, letting cracks start there. Some of her colleagues point out, however, that joints on hotter parts of a board both grow thicker intermetallic layers and go through larger temperature swings, so the two features might simply occur together.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Varkonyi's hypothesis?
options: When identical boards were put through the same temperature cycles, joints whose intermetallic layers had been thickened in advance by extra heating before testing developed cracks after fewer cycles than joints with thin layers.

When boards from many customers were surveyed, joints with thicker intermetallic layers were found to contain cracks more often than joints with thinner layers, no matter which vehicle model the boards came from.

When cracked joints were compared with joints that had not cracked, the intermetallic layers were found to have thickened more quickly after the cracks appeared, as heat built up along the crack surfaces.

When boards were mounted near engines rather than in cabin areas, the joints went through larger temperature swings and developed cracks after fewer cycles, whatever the thickness of their intermetallic layers.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 온도 사이클 조건을 똑같이 맞추고 금속간화합물층 두께만 미리 조작했는데도 두꺼운 층의 균열이 더 빨리 생겼다. 동료들이 제시한 대안 설명(뜨거운 위치가 두께와 균열을 둘 다 키운다)을 차단하고, 두께가 균열보다 먼저 정해졌으므로 인과 방향도 확인해 준다.
B(상관을 인과로 오해): 차종이 달라도 같은 상관이 나온다는 것은 상관을 재확인할 뿐이다. 보드 위 온도라는 교란 요인은 그대로 남아 있다.
C(인과 방향 반대): 균열이 생긴 뒤 층이 두꺼워졌다면 균열이 원인이고 두께가 결과라는 뜻이다. 가설과 정반대 방향이다.
D(제3의 원인): 층 두께와 상관없이 온도 변동폭이 균열을 일으킨다는 결과로, 동료들의 대안 설명을 지지하고 가설은 약하게 만든다.
problem.explanationEn:
A is correct. All boards went through the same temperature cycles, and only the intermetallic thickness was changed, set in advance. Joints with thicker layers still cracked sooner. This rules out the colleagues' alternative explanation, that hotter locations cause both thick layers and cracks. It also shows the right causal direction, because the thickness was in place before any cracking.
B mistakes correlation for causation. Finding the same link across vehicle models only repeats the correlation. Board temperature could still be causing both thick layers and cracks.
C reverses the causal direction. If layers thickened after cracks appeared, the cracks are driving the thickening, not the other way around.
D points to a third factor. It shows temperature swings cause cracking regardless of layer thickness, which supports the colleagues' alternative and weakens Varkonyi's hypothesis.

hardJudge.note: 지문은 상관(두꺼운 IMC층–피로균열 동시 발생)과 가설, 그리고 동료들의 교란요인(보드 위 온도 위치) 대안만 제시하고 인과를 단정하지 않음. A는 온도 사이클을 통제하고 층 두께를 사전 조작한 실험 결과로, 교란요인을 차단하고 시간 선후(두께→균열)까지 확보하여 가설을 가장 직접 지지함. B는 차종을 바꿔도 상관이 유지될 뿐 보드 내 온도 교란은 남아 있어 상관→인과 단순 치환 오답, C는 균열 후 층이 두꺼워진다는 역방향, D는 두께와 무관하게 온도 변동이 균열을 유발한다는 제3 원인(동료 입장 지지)으로 각각 레시피에 부합. 해설은 정답과 오답 논리를 정확히 뒷받침하며 모순 없음. 사실 오류(IMC = Cu–Sn 취성 화합물, 열사이클 피로균열)는 없고, 공개 시험지 유사 지문 징후 없음. 단일 자료 읽기를 넘어 교란요인 배제·인과 방향 검증이 필요하므로 hard 적합.

advisory.note: 교란변수(국소 온도)를 통제하고 두께만 조작한 실험이 정답이라 인과 판단이 필요하다. 오답 B(상관 재확인), C(인과 역전), D(제3원인 지지)가 각각 레시피의 오답 유형에 정확히 대응한다. D는 '어떤 원인'이라기보다 대안 설명을 지지하는 보기지만, 5번 항목은 충족하는 것으로 본다.

problem.passage:
When a tire rubber sample is stretched and then held at a fixed length, the force needed to keep it stretched does not stay constant. Instead, the stress inside the rubber slowly ______ over time as its long polymer chains shift and untangle. Engineers measure this drop to predict how well a tire will absorb bumps and vibrations on the road.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: When a tire rubber sample is stretched and then held at a fixed length, the force needed to keep it stretched does not stay constant. Instead, the stress inside the rubber slowly ______ over time as its long polymer chains shift and untangle. Engineers measure this drop to predict how well a tire will absorb bumps and vibrations on the road.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: decreases
accumulates
intensifies
stabilizes
problem.explanation: 지문은 고무를 고정된 길이로 유지할 때 필요한 힘이 일정하지 않으며, 엔지니어가 이 '감소(drop)'를 측정한다고 직접 밝힌다. 따라서 응력이 시간에 따라 줄어든다는 뜻의 A(decreases)가 정답이다. B(accumulates)와 C(intensifies)는 응력이 커진다는 의미로 'drop'과 정반대이다. D(stabilizes)는 응력이 일정해진다는 뜻으로 '일정하게 유지되지 않는다'는 진술과 모순된다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says the force needed to hold the stretched rubber does not stay constant, and that engineers measure "this drop." So the stress must go down over time, which makes A (decreases) correct. B (accumulates) and C (intensifies) both mean the stress grows, the opposite of a drop. D (stabilizes) means the stress levels off and stays steady, which contradicts the statement that it does not stay constant.

quality.seed: physical science — Viscoelastic polymer stress relaxation modulus decay and damping mechanisms in tire rubber applications

hardJudge.note: 지문 내 'this drop'과 'does not stay constant'가 직접 단서로 작동하여 A(decreases)가 유일하게 성립한다. 응력 완화(stress relaxation) 현상 서술은 과학적으로 정확하다. 오답 B·C는 방향 반대, D는 '일정하지 않다'와 모순되어 규칙을 알면 즉시 배제되지만 문맥을 놓치면 그럴듯한 전형적 오개념이다. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답·글자 참조가 일치하고 영어는 자연스러우며 한글 혼입 없음. 저작권 의심 없음. easy 난이도 적합.

advisory.note: 응력 완화(stress relaxation)를 정확하게 묘사함. 'this drop'이라는 직접 단서로 한 단계 만에 풀린다. 오답 B와 C(증가)는 'force ... does not stay constant'만 읽은 학생에게 그럴듯해 보이고, D는 '시간이 지나면 일정해진다'는 오개념을 노린 선택지라 easy 난이도에 맞다.

problem.passage:
When tiny particles are mixed into a liquid, weak attractive forces called van der Waals forces pull them toward one another, causing them to clump into larger masses that sink. To keep the particles evenly spread, chemists often coat them with molecules that push neighboring particles apart. These coatings ______ the attraction between particles, so the mixture stays uniform for months instead of separating within hours.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: When tiny particles are mixed into a liquid, weak attractive forces called van der Waals forces pull them toward one another, causing them to clump into larger masses that sink. To keep the particles evenly spread, chemists often coat them with molecules that push neighboring particles apart. These coatings ______ the attraction between particles, so the mixture stays uniform for months instead of separating within hours.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: strengthen
counteract
reveal
imitate
problem.explanation: 지문은 코팅이 입자들을 서로 밀어내어 혼합물이 오래 균일하게 유지된다고 설명하므로, 코팅은 입자 간 인력에 맞서 그 효과를 상쇄해야 한다. 따라서 '대항하다, 상쇄하다'를 뜻하는 B가 정답이다. A는 인력을 강화한다는 뜻이라 입자가 오히려 더 빨리 뭉치게 되므로 결과와 반대된다. C는 인력을 드러낸다는 뜻으로, 혼합물이 안정되는 이유를 설명하지 못한다. D는 인력을 흉내 낸다는 뜻이라 입자를 밀어낸다는 코팅의 역할과 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says the coatings push neighboring particles apart, which keeps the mixture uniform for a long time, so the coatings must work against the attraction between particles. That makes B, meaning "to oppose or cancel the effect of," the best choice. A would mean the coatings make the attraction stronger, which would make the particles clump faster—the opposite of what the text describes. C would mean the coatings simply make the attraction visible, which doesn't explain why the mixture stays stable. D would mean the coatings copy the attraction, which doesn't fit their job of pushing particles apart.

quality.seed: physical science — Nanoparticle agglomeration van der Waals forces and dispersion stability in colloidal suspension stabilization

hardJudge.note: 정답 B 검산 일치: "push neighboring particles apart" + "stays uniform" 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나 인력을 상쇄한다는 의미가 한 단계 추론으로 확정됨. A는 반대 의미, C·D는 맥락 불합치로 규칙을 알면 즉시 배제되며 초보자에겐 그럴듯한 오답. 과학 내용(van der Waals 인력, 입체 안정화 코팅) 사실 오류 없음. 한·영 해설 결론과 글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 원문 지문 아님(독창적 서술).

advisory.note: 입자를 밀어낸다는 직접 단서가 있어 한 단계 추론으로 counteract가 정해짐. 정답 strengthen은 전형적인 반대 방향 오답이고, reveal과 imitate는 다소 약하지만 허용되는 수준임. 입체 안정화(steric stabilization)에 대한 과학적 설명은 정확함.

problem.passage:
Engineers protecting buildings from earthquakes have long relied on passive dampers, devices filled with oil that resist motion by a fixed amount. Such dampers work well for the shaking they were designed for but cannot adjust when an earthquake proves stronger or weaker than expected. Magnetorheological (MR) dampers offer an alternative. They contain a fluid with suspended iron particles; when an electromagnetic coil inside the damper is switched on, the particles line up into chains, and the fluid thickens from a liquid with the consistency of motor oil to something close to a soft solid within milliseconds. By varying the current, sensors and a controller can tune the damper's resistance as ground motion changes. Because the coil needs only about as much power as a household light bulb, MR dampers can keep running on backup batteries even when an earthquake knocks out the electrical grid. This is an important advantage, since the stronger kinds of adjustable systems need large power supplies that may fail at exactly the moment they are needed.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

Such dampers work well for the shaking they were designed for but cannot adjust when an earthquake proves stronger or weaker than expected. Magnetorheological (MR) dampers offer an alternative. They contain a fluid with suspended iron particles; when an electromagnetic coil inside the damper is switched on, the particles line up into chains, and the fluid thickens from a liquid with the consistency of motor oil to something close to a soft solid within milliseconds. By varying the current, sensors and a controller can tune the damper's resistance as ground motion changes. Because the coil needs only about as much power as a household light bulb, MR dampers can keep running on backup batteries even when an earthquake knocks out the electrical grid. This is an important advantage, since the stronger kinds of adjustable systems need large power supplies that may fail at exactly the moment they are needed.

problem.passage:
Enzymatic biofuel cells could one day power implanted medical devices by drawing on glucose already present in the body. In these cells, an enzyme such as glucose oxidase strips electrons from glucose at one electrode. Early designs relied on small "mediator" molecules to shuttle those electrons from the enzyme to the electrode, but mediators can leak into surrounding tissue and slowly lose effectiveness. Engineers have therefore pursued direct electron transfer, in which the enzyme passes electrons straight to the electrode surface. The difficulty is that the enzyme's active site is buried deep inside its protein structure, too far from the electrode for electrons to cross efficiently. Recent work suggests a solution: by anchoring enzymes to carbon nanotubes oriented so that the active site faces the conductive surface, researchers have shortened that distance enough to produce usable current without any mediator.

problem.passage:
Engineers designing acoustic cloaks often borrow an idea first developed for light: metamaterials, structures built from repeating units smaller than the waves they manipulate, can be arranged to give a material properties no natural substance has, including a negative refractive index that bends waves the "wrong" way. By grading these properties carefully, a shell of metamaterial can steer incoming sound around an object and release it on the far side as if nothing had been in the way. Early laboratory demonstrations were striking, but they worked only within a narrow band of frequencies, because the tiny resonating units that produce the unusual behavior respond strongly to some pitches and hardly at all to others.

Researchers at several universities have therefore shifted their focus. Rather than pursuing a perfect cloak, many now design shells that hide objects from the specific frequencies that matter in a given setting, such as the sonar pulses used to locate submarines or the low hum of machinery in a factory. This narrower aim, they argue, turns a laboratory curiosity into something that could actually be built and used.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

It explains how the rotating tool generates heat through friction, which accounts for the temperature the metal reaches during the process.
It explains why aircraft manufacturers have replaced rivets with friction-stir seams, which is the main purpose of the text as a whole.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 밑줄 문장은 알루미늄이 녹지 않고 연화된 상태에서 핀이 재료를 옮겨 접합한다는 원리를 설명한다. 마지막 문장은 바로 이 점(액체 상태를 거치지 않음)을 근거로 응고 결함이 없다는 결론을 내린다. 즉 메커니즘 설명과 결론의 근거라는 두 단계를 모두 연결해야 한다.
B: 용융 시 균열 문제는 첫 문장이 제시한 내용으로, 인접 문장의 역할과 혼동한 것이다. 밑줄 문장은 문제를 제기하지 않고 해결 원리를 설명한다.
C: 마찰에 의한 열 발생과 온도는 앞 문장의 내용이다. 밑줄 문장은 그 온도를 출발점으로 삼을 뿐 열 발생을 설명하지 않으므로, 한 단계만 본 해석이다.
D: 리벳을 대체한 이유는 마지막 문장의 결론이다. 또한 밑줄 문장 하나의 기능을 글 전체의 목적과 뒤바꿔 놓았다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer A: The underlined sentence explains that the aluminum softens without melting, so the pin can move material around the tool and press the sheets together. The final sentence then relies on exactly this point—that the metal never becomes liquid—to conclude that the seams avoid solidification defects. To get the answer, you have to connect two steps: the sentence explains the mechanism, and that mechanism is the support for the conclusion.
B: The cracking of melted alloys is described in the first sentence. This choice mixes up the underlined sentence with an earlier one. The underlined sentence explains the solution; it doesn't raise the problem.
C: Frictional heating and the resulting temperature come from the sentence just before. The underlined sentence starts from that temperature but doesn't explain how the heat is produced, so this choice sees only one step.
D: Replacing rivets is the conclusion in the final sentence. This choice also swaps the role of one sentence for the purpose of the whole text.

hardJudge.note: 지문은 문제 제기(용융 시 결함) → 해결책 도입 → 가열 단계 → 밑줄(고체 상태 접합 메커니즘) → 결론(응고 결함 회피, 리벳 대체)의 명확한 다단계 사슬을 갖는다. 정답 A는 밑줄 문장의 개별 기능(고체 상태 접합 설명)과 그것이 마지막 문장의 결론을 뒷받침하는 근거 역할을 함께 요구하므로 단계 간 연결 없이는 확정되지 않는다. B는 첫 문장, C는 직전 문장의 역할로 인접 단계 혼동형이고, D는 마지막 문장의 결론을 밑줄 기능으로 바꾸면서 글 전체 목적과 뒤바꾼 형태로 설계가 적절하다. 마찰교반용접이 융점의 약 80% 온도에서 고상 접합한다는 서술은 기술적으로 타당하며, 해설도 정답과 오답 사유를 정확히 뒷받침한다. 문장 길이나 숫자 복잡성이 아닌 논리 단계 수로 난이도를 구성했다.

advisory.note: 정답 A는 메커니즘을 설명하는 문장이 마지막 문장의 결론으로 이어지는 관계를 정확히 짚었다. 오답 B, C, D는 각각 1문장, 2문장, 결론 문장의 역할과 섞이도록 설계되었고, 그중 D는 밑줄 문장 하나의 기능을 글 전체의 목적과 뒤바꿨다. 다만 오답이 모두 '다른 문장의 내용'이라 지문과 대조해 쉽게 지울 수 있다. 따라서 hard 변별력은 중상 수준이다. 사실관계(마찰교반용접 약 80% 융점, 고상 접합, 리벳 대체)는 맞다.

problem.passage:
Engineers who design the tiny motion sensors inside smartphones disagree about where accuracy problems originate. Rina Takahashi, a MEMS designer, argues that the capacitive accelerometer itself is close to its physical limits: a silicon proof mass shifts by less than a nanometer, and the resulting change in capacitance between interleaved comb fingers is so small that thermal noise in the structure, not anything downstream, sets the floor on precision. Electrical engineer Marcus Obi accepts that such noise exists but contends that most errors users actually notice, such as a compass that drifts or a step counter that miscounts, arise when software misreads the signals. In vibrating MEMS gyroscopes, for instance, a resonating mass is deflected sideways by the Coriolis force when the phone rotates, and that deflection is likewise read capacitively. __Obi points out that when such gyroscopes are recalibrated in software to correct for temperature-dependent shifts in their output, drift in phone orientation readings drops sharply even though the sensing structures remain unchanged.__

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: Engineers who design the tiny motion sensors inside smartphones disagree about where accuracy problems originate. Rina Takahashi, a MEMS designer, argues that the capacitive accelerometer itself is close to its physical limits: a silicon proof mass shifts by less than a nanometer, and the resulting change in capacitance between interleaved comb fingers is so small that thermal noise in the structure, not anything downstream, sets the floor on precision. Electrical engineer Marcus Obi accepts that such noise exists but contends that most errors users actually notice, such as a compass that drifts or a step counter that miscounts, arise when software misreads the signals. In vibrating MEMS gyroscopes, for instance, a resonating mass is deflected sideways by the Coriolis force when the phone rotates, and that deflection is likewise read capacitively. __Obi points out that when such gyroscopes are recalibrated in software to correct for temperature-dependent shifts in their output, drift in phone orientation readings drops sharply even though the sensing structures remain unchanged.__
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence that Takahashi would cite to show that software corrections confirm that thermal noise in the sensing structure limits accuracy.
It offers an observation suggesting that the physical limit Takahashi emphasizes may not account for the errors that phone users typically encounter.
It describes a result that Obi uses to argue that Coriolis-based gyroscopes are more reliable than capacitive accelerometers.
It reports a finding that leads both engineers to agree that MEMS sensors should be redesigned to reduce temperature sensitivity.
problem.explanation: 정답 B: 밑줄 문장은 구조(하드웨어)는 그대로인데 소프트웨어 보정만으로 오차가 크게 줄었다는 관찰이다. 이는 오차의 주원인이 구조의 열잡음이라는 Takahashi의 주장과 달리, 사용자가 겪는 오류는 신호 해석 문제라는 Obi의 입장을 뒷받침하므로, Takahashi가 강조하는 물리적 한계가 실제 사용자 오류를 설명하지 못할 수 있음을 시사한다. A: 두 입장을 뒤바꾼 오답. 소프트웨어 보정의 성공은 Takahashi가 아니라 Obi에게 유리한 증거다. C: Obi의 입장 일부만 근거로 삼아 지문에 없는 센서 간 신뢰도 비교를 지어냈다. Obi는 자이로스코프를 예시로 썼을 뿐이다. D: 지문에 없는 새로운 반응을 지어낸 오답. 두 사람이 합의한다는 내용도, 하드웨어를 다시 설계하자는 결론도 없으며, 오히려 구조는 바꾸지 않았다는 점이 핵심이다.
problem.explanationEn: B is correct. The underlined sentence reports that drift dropped sharply after software recalibration alone, while the sensing structures stayed the same. That supports Obi's view that the errors users notice come from how software reads the signals. It also challenges Takahashi's claim that thermal noise in the structure sets the limit on accuracy. So the sentence suggests that the physical limit she stresses may not explain everyday errors. A swaps the two positions. A software fix working is evidence for Obi, not for Takahashi. C relies only on Obi's side and adds a reliability comparison between gyroscopes and accelerometers that the text never makes. Obi uses gyroscopes only as an example. D invents a new reaction. The engineers never agree, and nobody calls for a redesign. In fact, the point is that the hardware was left unchanged.

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 구조 불변·소프트웨어 보정만으로 drift 급감이라는 관찰로, Obi의 입장을 뒷받침하며 Takahashi의 물리적 한계 주장이 사용자 오류를 설명하지 못할 수 있음을 간접 시사함 → B 정확. A는 입장 뒤바꿈(Takahashi에게 불리한 증거를 유리한 것으로 제시), C는 Obi의 예시(자이로스코프)만 근거로 지문에 없는 센서 간 신뢰도 비교 조작, D는 합의·재설계라는 지문에 없는 반응 조작. 질문 자체는 문장 기능이지만 정답 판별에 Takahashi 입장에 대한 함의 추론(명시되지 않음)이 필요. MEMS 축전식 가속도계·Coriolis 자이로·온도 보정 기술 서술 사실 오류 없음. 해설은 정답과 오답 사유를 정확히 뒷받침하며 모순 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 B가 맞다. 하드웨어는 그대로 두고 소프트웨어 보정만으로 드리프트가 줄었다는 관찰은 Obi의 입장을 뒷받침한다. 동시에 Takahashi의 물리적 한계론이 사용자가 실제로 겪는 오류를 설명하지 못할 수 있음을 간접적으로 시사한다. A는 입장을 뒤바꾼 오답, C는 Obi 쪽 일부만 근거로 센서 간 비교를 지어낸 오답, D는 지문에 없는 합의를 지어낸 오답이다. 다만 B는 Takahashi의 반응을 추론하라는 형태가 아니라 '시사한다'는 형태로 제시되어 추론 요구가 다소 약하다. 또 Takahashi는 가속도계를, Obi는 자이로스코프를 예로 들어 두 사람이 다루는 대상이 어긋나 있지만, 이 점이 정답 판단에 영향을 주지는 않는다.

problem.passage:
In electrowetting-on-dielectric (EWOD) devices, tiny droplets sit on a grid of electrodes coated with a thin insulating layer. Applying voltage to the electrode next to a droplet makes that edge of the droplet spread, pulling the whole droplet forward, so chemists can move, merge, and mix reagents without pumps or channels. Engineer Lena Osei suspected that the slow, steady voltage ramps used in most EWOD devices were not needed for reliable movement and that sharp, brief pulses could move droplets just as well while reducing the charge that slowly builds up in the insulating layer and eventually stalls droplets. In her tests with aqueous droplets, pulsed control moved droplets across 2,000 electrode steps with a failure rate no higher than ramped control, and measured charge buildup was about 40 percent lower. __However, when Osei repeated the trials with droplets containing dissolved proteins, which tend to stick to the surface, pulsed control failed to move droplets far more often than ramped control did.__ Osei concludes that pulsed control is a better choice for moving simple aqueous droplets, though not yet for every type of sample used in EWOD chemistry.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

Applying voltage to the electrode next to a droplet makes that edge of the droplet spread, pulling the whole droplet forward, so chemists can move, merge, and mix reagents without pumps or channels. Engineer Lena Osei suspected that the slow, steady voltage ramps used in most EWOD devices were not needed for reliable movement and that sharp, brief pulses could move droplets just as well while reducing the charge that slowly builds up in the insulating layer and eventually stalls droplets. In her tests with aqueous droplets, pulsed control moved droplets across 2,000 electrode steps with a failure rate no higher than ramped control, and measured charge buildup was about 40 percent lower. __However, when Osei repeated the trials with droplets containing dissolved proteins, which tend to stick to the surface, pulsed control failed to move droplets far more often than ramped control did.__ Osei concludes that pulsed control is a better choice for moving simple aqueous droplets, though not yet for every type of sample used in EWOD chemistry.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a finding indicating that pulsed control is unsuitable for EWOD devices in general, overturning the advantage reported in the earlier tests.
It presents a finding showing only that protein droplets stick to EWOD surfaces, a detail separate from the comparison of the two voltage methods.
It presents a finding that marks the limit of the earlier results, explaining why Osei confines her recommendation to one kind of sample.
It presents a finding suggesting that the high failure rate of protein droplets is what caused Osei to develop pulsed control in the first place.
problem.explanation:
정답 C: 밑줄 문장은 단백질 시료에서는 펄스 제어가 실패율이 훨씬 높았다는 결과를 제시한다. 이 결과가 앞의 수용액 실험 결과의 적용 범위를 제한하므로, 오세이는 결론을 '단순 수용액 방울'로 한정한다. 근거의 범위와 결론의 범위가 정확히 일치한다.
A(과장): 밑줄 결과는 단백질 시료에만 해당하므로, 펄스 제어가 EWOD 전반에 부적합하다거나 수용액 결과를 뒤집는다는 결론까지 지지하지 않는다. 결론에서도 수용액에 대한 이점은 그대로 유지된다.
B(일부만 반영해 좁게 해석): 단백질이 표면에 달라붙는다는 점만 보고 두 방식의 비교를 놓쳤다. 밑줄 문장의 핵심은 펄스 제어와 램프 제어의 실패율 비교이며, 이것이 결론의 단서 조항과 직접 연결된다.
D(인과 방향 역전): 펄스 제어는 전하 축적을 줄이려는 동기에서 나왔고, 단백질 실험은 그 뒤에 진행된 후속 시험이다. 단백질 실패가 펄스 제어 개발의 원인이었던 것이 아니다.
problem.explanationEn:
C is correct. The underlined sentence reports that pulsed control failed far more often than ramped control when the droplets contained proteins. That finding sets a boundary on the earlier aqueous-droplet results, which is why Osei's conclusion recommends pulsed control only for simple aqueous droplets. The scope of the evidence matches the scope of the conclusion exactly.
A overstates the evidence. The result applies only to protein-containing droplets, so it doesn't show that pulsed control is unsuitable in general, and it doesn't overturn the aqueous results. Osei still keeps that advantage in her conclusion.
B reads the sentence too narrowly. It picks up on protein stickiness but ignores the main point: the sentence compares the failure rates of the two voltage methods, and that comparison is what leads to the qualification in the conclusion.
D reverses cause and effect. Pulsed control was motivated by the goal of reducing charge buildup. The protein trials were a later follow-up test, so protein failures did not prompt the method's development.

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 가설→수용액 결과→단백질 시료 반례→한정된 결론으로 이어지는 논리 사슬에서 '선행 결과의 적용 한계를 표시해 결론의 단서 조항을 설명'하는 역할이며 C가 이를 정확히 기술한다. A는 단백질 시료 한정 결과를 EWOD 전반으로 과장, B는 '단백질 부착'이라는 부분 정보만 반영해 두 제어 방식 비교를 누락, D는 후속 시험 결과를 펄스 제어 개발의 원인으로 인과를 역전시킨 오답으로 체크리스트 3·4·5에 각각 대응한다. EWOD 작동 원리·유전층 전하 축적·단백질 표면 흡착 서술은 사실과 부합하고, 인물·수치는 가상 설정으로 저작권 우려 없음. 해설은 정답 및 각 오답 유형과 수치·논리적으로 일치한다.

advisory.note: 정답 C가 단서 조항이 붙은 결론과 정확히 맞아떨어진다. 오답 A(과장), B(좁은 해석), D(인과 역전)는 각각 의도대로 구성되었다. 다만 B는 'only'·'separate' 표현 때문에, D는 시간 순서상 명백히 맞지 않아 쉽게 걸러진다. 실제 경쟁 오답은 A 하나뿐이다.
